<h1 id="intercom-api-admins">Admins</h1>

Everything about your Admins

## Identify an admin

<a id="opIdidentifyAdmin"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.intercom.io/me \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /me`

You can view the currently authorised admin along with the embedded app object (a "workspace" in legacy terminology).

> 🚧 Single Sign On
>
> If you are building a custom "Log in with Intercom" flow for your site, and you call the `/me` endpoint to identify the logged-in user, you should not accept any sign-ins from users with unverified email addresses as it poses a potential impersonation security risk.

Requires the `read_single_admin` or `read_admins` OAuth scope.

## Set an admin to away

<a id="opIdsetAwayAdmin"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.intercom.io/admins/0/away \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "away_mode_enabled": true,
    "away_mode_reassign": true,
    "away_status_reason_id": 12345
  }'
```

`PUT /admins/{admin_id}/away`

You can set an Admin as away for the Inbox.

Requires the `update_admins` OAuth scope.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "away_mode_enabled": true,
  "away_mode_reassign": true,
  "away_status_reason_id": 12345
}
```

<h3 id="set-an-admin-to-away-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Intercom-Version|header|[intercom_version](#schemaintercom_version)|false|none|
|admin_id|path|integer|true|The unique identifier of a given admin|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» away_mode_enabled|body|boolean|true|Set to `true` to change the status of the admin to away, or `false` to set them back to active.|
|» away_mode_reassign|body|boolean|true|Set to "true" to assign any new conversation replies to your default inbox.|
|» away_status_reason_id|body|integer|false|The unique identifier of the away status reason. Only allowed when `away_mode_enabled` is `true`, and the reason can't be archived, unless it is already the admin's current reason. Required if your workspace makes away status reasons mandatory.|

## List all activity logs

<a id="opIdlistActivityLogs"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.intercom.io/admins/activity_logs \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /admins/activity_logs`

You can get a log of activities by all admins in an app.

Requires the `read_admins` OAuth scope.


<h3 id="list-all-activity-logs-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Intercom-Version|header|[intercom_version](#schemaintercom_version)|false|none|
|created_at_after|query|string|false|The start date that you request data for. It must be formatted as a UNIX timestamp. If you leave it out, it defaults to 30 days before the request.|
|created_at_before|query|string|false|The end date that you request data for. It must be formatted as a UNIX timestamp. If you leave it out, it defaults to the time of the request.|
|page|query|integer|false|The page number of results to return. Defaults to the first page.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of results per page. Must be between 1 and 250.|

## Search activity logs

<a id="opIdsearchActivityLogs"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.intercom.io/admins/activity_logs/search \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "created_at_after": 1677253093,
    "created_at_before": 1677861493,
    "event_types": [
      "app_name_change",
      "message_state_change"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /admins/activity_logs/search`

Search and filter admin activity logs using a POST request with event type filter in the request body. You can find more details about the available event types in the List all activity log event types endpoint.

Results are paginated by page number. Use `page` and `per_page` in the request body to choose a page. The `next` link in the response is a URL that keeps the query string of the request URL and sets `page` and `per_page` for the next page. It does not include the filters from your request body. To fetch the next page, send a POST request with the same request body to that URL. Query parameters in the `next` URL take precedence over `page` and `per_page` in the body.

Requires the `read_admins` OAuth scope.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "created_at_after": 1677253093,
  "created_at_before": 1677861493,
  "event_types": [
    "app_name_change",
    "message_state_change"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="search-activity-logs-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Intercom-Version|header|[intercom_version](#schemaintercom_version)|false|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» created_at_after|body|integer(date-time)|false|The start date that you request data for. It must be formatted as a UNIX timestamp. If you leave it out, it defaults to 30 days before the request.|
|» created_at_before|body|integer(date-time)|false|The end date that you request data for. It must be formatted as a UNIX timestamp. If you leave it out, it defaults to the time of the request.|
|» event_types|body|[string]|false|An optional list of event types to filter activity logs by. Use the list all activity log event types endpoint to retrieve available values.|
|» page|body|integer|false|The page number of results to return.|
|» per_page|body|integer|false|The number of results per page. Must be between 1 and 250.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|Intercom-Version|1.0|
|Intercom-Version|1.1|
|Intercom-Version|1.2|
|Intercom-Version|1.3|
|Intercom-Version|1.4|
|Intercom-Version|2.0|
|Intercom-Version|2.1|
|Intercom-Version|2.2|
|Intercom-Version|2.3|
|Intercom-Version|2.4|
|Intercom-Version|2.5|
|Intercom-Version|2.6|
|Intercom-Version|2.7|
|Intercom-Version|2.8|
|Intercom-Version|2.9|
|Intercom-Version|2.10|

|Intercom-Version|2.15|
|Intercom-Version|2.16|
|Intercom-Version|2.17|

> Example responses

    "type": "pages",

## List all activity log event types

<a id="opIdlistActivityLogEventTypes"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.intercom.io/admins/activity_log_event_types \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /admins/activity_log_event_types`

You can get a list of all activity log event types. This is useful for discovering valid values to use with the `event_types` filter on the Search activity logs endpoint.

Requires the `read_admins` OAuth scope.

<h1 id="intercom-api-ai-content">AI Content</h1>

With the AI Content APIs, you can create and manage External Pages and Content Import Sources for your Fin Content Library.

&nbsp;

*External Pages* are pages that you want Fin to be able to answer questions about. The API for External Pages is a great way to ingest into your Fin Content Library pages that are not publicly accessible and hence can't be crawled by Intercom.

&nbsp;

*Content Import Sources* are the sources of those pages, and they are used to determine the default audience for the pages (configured via the UI). You should create a Content Import Source for each source of External Pages that you want to ingest into your Fin Content Library.

&nbsp;

You can then iterate through the content from that source via its API and POST it to the External Pages endpoint. That endpoint has an *external_id* parameter which allows you to specify the identifier from the source. The endpoint will then either create a new External Page or update an existing one as appropriate.",


## List content import sources

<a id="opIdlistContentImportSources"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.intercom.io/ai/content_import_sources \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /ai/content_import_sources`

You can retrieve a list of all content import sources for a workspace.

`total_count` and `pages.total_pages` are worked out from every content import source in the workspace, including deleted ones that the list leaves out, so both can be higher than the number of sources you get back across all pages. The last pages can be short or empty.

OAuth tokens must have the `read_write_ai_content` scope.


<h3 id="list-content-import-sources-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Intercom-Version|header|[intercom_version](#schemaintercom_version)|false|none|
|page|query|integer|false|The page of results to fetch. Defaults to the first page.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of results to return per page. Maximum 150.|

## Create a content import source

<a id="opIdcreateContentImportSource"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.intercom.io/ai/content_import_sources \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "sync_behavior": "api",
    "url": "https://www.example.com"
  }'
```

`POST /ai/content_import_sources`

You can create a new content import source by sending a POST request to this endpoint.

OAuth tokens must have the `read_write_ai_content` scope.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "sync_behavior": "api",
  "url": "https://www.example.com"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-content-import-source-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|

|Intercom-Version|header|[intercom_version](#schemaintercom_version)|false|none|
|body|body|[create_content_import_source_request](#schemacreate_content_import_source_request)|false|none|
|» sync_behavior|body|string|true|If you intend to create or update External Pages via the API, this should be set to `api`.|
|» status|body|string|false|The status of the content import source.|
|» url|body|string|true|The URL of the content import source. It must be an http or https URL whose host is a valid public domain name.|
|» audience_ids|body|integer \| [integer] \| null|false|The unique identifiers for the audiences to associate with this content import source. Can be a single integer or an array of integers.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|integer|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[integer]|false|none|

## Create an external page (or update an external page by external ID)

<a id="opIdcreateExternalPage"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.intercom.io/ai/external_pages \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "audience_ids": [
      1,
      2
    ],
    "external_id": "abc1234",
    "html": "<html><body><h1>Test</h1></body></html>",
    "locale": "en",
    "source_id": 44,
    "title": "Test",
    "url": "https://www.example.com"
  }'
```

`POST /ai/external_pages`

You can create a new external page by sending a POST request to this endpoint. If an external page already exists with the specified source_id and external_id, it will be updated instead.

OAuth tokens must have the `read_write_ai_content` scope.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "audience_ids": [
    1,
    2
  ],
  "external_id": "abc1234",
  "html": "<html><body><h1>Test</h1></body></html>",
  "locale": "en",
  "source_id": 44,
  "title": "Test",
  "url": "https://www.example.com"
}
```

<h3 id="create-an-external-page-or-update-an-external-page-by-external-id-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Intercom-Version|header|[intercom_version](#schemaintercom_version)|false|none|
|body|body|[create_external_page_request](#schemacreate_external_page_request)|false|none|
|» title|body|string|true|The title of the external page.|
|» html|body|string|true|The body of the external page in HTML.|
|» url|body|string|false|The URL of the external page. This will be used by Fin to link end users to the page it based its answer on. When a URL is not present, Fin will not reference the source.|
|» ai_agent_availability|body|boolean|false|Whether the external page should be used to answer questions by AI Agent. Will not default when updating an existing external page.|
|» ai_copilot_availability|body|boolean|false|Whether the external page should be used to answer questions by AI Copilot. Will not default when updating an existing external page.|
|» ai_sales_agent_availability|body|boolean|false|Whether the external page should be used to answer questions by AI Sales Agent. Will not default when updating an existing external page.|
|» locale|body|string|true|The language code of the external page, for example `en` or `fr`. It must be a language supported by the workspace.|
|» source_id|body|integer|true|The unique identifier for the source of the external page which was given by Intercom. Every external page must be associated with a Content Import Source which represents the place it comes from and from which it inherits a default audience (configured in the UI). For a new source, make a POST request to the Content Import Source endpoint and an ID for the source will be returned in the response.|
|» external_id|body|string|true|The identifier for the external page which was given by the source. Must be unique for the source.|
|» audience_ids|body|[integer]|false|The list of audience IDs to target this external page to for Fin AI Agent. Omitting the field keeps the default audience inherited from the source. Pass `[]` to clear all audience memberships, including the inherited ones. If an external page already exists with the specified source_id and external_id, omitting the field leaves its audience memberships unchanged. Unknown audience IDs return a `404` error.|

## Update an external page

<a id="opIdupdateExternalPage"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.intercom.io/ai/external_pages/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "audience_ids": [
      1,
      2
    ],
    "external_id": "5678",
    "html": "<html><body><h1>Test</h1></body></html>",
    "locale": "en",
    "source_id": 47,
    "title": "Test",
    "url": "https://www.example.com"
  }'
```

`PUT /ai/external_pages/{page_id}`

You can update an existing external page (if it was created via the API).

OAuth tokens must have the `read_write_ai_content` scope.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "audience_ids": [
    1,
    2
  ],
  "external_id": "5678",
  "html": "<html><body><h1>Test</h1></body></html>",
  "locale": "en",
  "source_id": 47,
  "title": "Test",
  "url": "https://www.example.com"
}
```

<h3 id="update-an-external-page-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Intercom-Version|header|[intercom_version](#schemaintercom_version)|false|none|
|page_id|path|string|true|The unique identifier for the external page which is given by Intercom.|
|body|body|[update_external_page_request](#schemaupdate_external_page_request)|false|none|
|» title|body|string|true|The title of the external page.|
|» html|body|string|true|The body of the external page in HTML.|
|» url|body|string|false|The URL of the external page. This will be used by Fin to link end users to the page it based its answer on. If omitted, the page's existing URL is removed.|
|» ai_agent_availability|body|boolean|false|Whether the external page should be used to answer questions by AI Agent.|
|» ai_copilot_availability|body|boolean|false|Whether the external page should be used to answer questions by AI Copilot.|
|» ai_sales_agent_availability|body|boolean|false|Whether the external page should be used to answer questions by AI Sales Agent.|
|» locale|body|string|true|The language code of the external page, for example `en` or `fr`. It must be a language supported by the workspace.|
|» source_id|body|integer|true|The unique identifier for the source of the external page which was given by Intercom. Every external page must be associated with a Content Import Source which represents the place it comes from and from which it inherits a default audience (configured in the UI). For a new source, make a POST request to the Content Import Source endpoint and an ID for the source will be returned in the response.|
|» external_id|body|string|true|The identifier for the external page which was given by the source. Must be unique for the source.|
|» audience_ids|body|[integer]|false|The list of audience IDs to target this external page to for Fin AI Agent. Replaces all existing audience memberships. Omitting the field leaves existing audience memberships unchanged. Pass `[]` to clear all audience memberships. Unknown audience IDs return a `404` error.|

## List all articles

<a id="opIdlistArticles"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.intercom.io/articles \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /articles`

You can fetch a list of all articles by making a GET request to `https://api.intercom.io/articles`.

> 📘 How are the articles sorted and ordered?
>
> Articles will be returned in descending order on the `updated_at` attribute. This means if you need to iterate through results then we'll show the most recently updated articles first.

Requires the `read_articles_scope` OAuth scope.


<h3 id="list-all-articles-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of results to return per page. Defaults to 25. Maximum is 250.|

## Create an article

<a id="opIdcreateArticle"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.intercom.io/articles \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "title": "Thanks for everything",
    "description": "Description of the Article",
    "body": "Body of the Article",
    "author_id": 991267497,
    "state": "published",
    "parent_id": 145,
    "translated_content": {
      "fr": {
        "title": "Merci pour tout",
        "description": "Description de l'\''article",
        "body": "Corps de l'\''article",
        "author_id": 991267497,
        "state": "published"
      }
    }
  }'
```

`POST /articles`

You can create a new article by making a POST request to `https://api.intercom.io/articles`.

> 📘 Tags are managed separately
>
> Tags are returned in article responses but cannot be set in the request body. To add or remove an article's tags, use the `POST /articles/{article_id}/tags` and `DELETE /articles/{article_id}/tags/{id}` endpoints.

Requires the `read_write_articles_scope` OAuth scope.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "title": "Thanks for everything",
  "description": "Description of the Article",
  "body": "Body of the Article",
  "author_id": 991267497,
  "state": "published",
  "parent_id": 145,
  "translated_content": {
    "fr": {
      "title": "Merci pour tout",
      "description": "Description de l'article",
      "body": "Corps de l'article",
      "author_id": 991267497,
      "state": "published"
    }
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-an-article-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Intercom-Version|header|[intercom_version](#schemaintercom_version)|false|none|
|body|body|[create_article_request](#schemacreate_article_request)|false|none|
|» title|body|string|false|The title of the article. For multilingual articles, this will be the title of the default language's content. Required unless a title is provided in `translated_content` under the workspace's default Help Center locale.|
|» description|body|string|false|The description of the article. For multilingual articles, this will be the description of the default language's content.|
|» body|body|string|false|The content of the article in HTML. For multilingual articles, this will be the body of the default language's content. Mutually exclusive with `body_markdown`.|
|» body_markdown|body|string|false|The content of the article in markdown. For multilingual articles, this will be the body of the default language's content. An alternative to `body` — you can provide content as markdown instead of HTML. Mutually exclusive with `body`.|
|» author_id|body|integer|false|The id of the author of the article. For multilingual articles, this will be the id of the author of the default language's content. Must be a teammate on the help center's workspace. Required unless an `author_id` is provided in `translated_content` under the workspace's default Help Center locale.|
|» state|body|string|false|Whether the article will be `published` or will be a `draft`. Defaults to draft. For multilingual articles, this will be the state of the default language's content.|
|» parent_id|body|integer|false|The id of the article's parent collection or section. An article without this field stands alone.|
|» parent_ids|body|[integer]|false|The ids of the parent collections to place this article in. Send an empty array to leave the article without a collection. When provided, this takes precedence over `parent_id`.|
|» locale|body|string|false|The locale of the article's default content, for example `en`. Defaults to the locale of the help center that the parent collection belongs to when `parent_id` is sent, and otherwise to the default Help Center locale. Must be a locale supported by the workspace's Help Center.|
|» translated_content|body|[article_translated_content](#schemaarticle_translated_content)|false|Content for other locales, keyed by locale code. Content for the article's default locale can also be given here instead of at the top level. If it is given in both places, the values must match.|
|» folder_id|body|integer \| null|false|The ID of the folder to place this article in, or null to leave it without a folder.|
|» audience_ids|body|[integer]|false|The list of audience IDs to assign to this article for Fin AI Agent targeting. Sending a top-level `audience_ids` broadcasts the same set to every locale. For per-locale targeting, use `translated_content.<locale>.audience_ids` instead. Sending both top-level and per-locale in the same request causes top-level to win. Unknown audience IDs return a 404 error. No partial commit occurs.|
|» ai_chatbot_availability|body|boolean|false|Whether the article should be available for AI Chatbot (Fin). For multilingual articles, this sets the default language's availability.|
|» ai_copilot_availability|body|boolean|false|Whether the article should be available for AI Copilot. For multilingual articles, this sets the default language's availability.|
|» ai_sales_agent_availability|body|boolean|false|Whether the article should be available for AI Sales Agent. For multilingual articles, this sets the default language's availability.|
|» scheduled_publish_at|body|string(date-time) \| null|false|ISO 8601 timestamp at which to schedule a future publish of the article. When set together with `state: "published"`, the article is scheduled instead of published immediately. Setting `null` cancels a pending publish schedule. Timestamps in the past or equal to the current time are rejected with 400 `parameter_invalid` — the value must be strictly in the future. Combining with `state: "draft"` returns 400 `parameter_invalid`. Sending in the same request as `scheduled_unpublish_at` returns 400 — only one pending schedule per article. Empty string returns 400 `parameter_invalid`.|
|» scheduled_unpublish_at|body|string(date-time) \| null|false|ISO 8601 timestamp at which to schedule a future unpublish of the article. The same request must also publish the article (`state: "published"`), otherwise it returns 400 `parameter_invalid`. The value must be strictly in the future; timestamps in the past or equal to the current time are rejected with 400 `parameter_invalid`. Setting `null` cancels a pending unpublish schedule. Sending in the same request as `scheduled_publish_at` returns 400 — only one pending schedule per article. Empty string returns 400 `parameter_invalid`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|Intercom-Version|1.0|
|Intercom-Version|1.1|
|Intercom-Version|1.2|
|Intercom-Version|1.3|
|Intercom-Version|1.4|
|Intercom-Version|2.0|
|Intercom-Version|2.1|
|Intercom-Version|2.2|
|Intercom-Version|2.3|
|Intercom-Version|2.4|
|Intercom-Version|2.5|
|Intercom-Version|2.6|
|Intercom-Version|2.7|
|Intercom-Version|2.8|
|Intercom-Version|2.9|
|Intercom-Version|2.10|
|Intercom-Version|2.11|
|Intercom-Version|2.12|
|Intercom-Version|2.13|
|Intercom-Version|2.14|
|Intercom-Version|2.15|
|Intercom-Version|2.16|
|Intercom-Version|2.17|
|» state|published|
|» state|draft|

## Update an article

<a id="opIdupdateArticle"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.intercom.io/articles/123 \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "title": "Christmas is here!",
    "body": "<p>New gifts in store for the jolly season</p>"
  }'
```

`PUT /articles/{article_id}`

You can update the details of a single article by making a PUT request to `https://api.intercom.io/articles/<id>`.

> 📘 Tags are managed separately
>
> Tags are returned in article responses but cannot be set in the request body. To add or remove an article's tags, use the `POST /articles/{article_id}/tags` and `DELETE /articles/{article_id}/tags/{id}` endpoints.

Requires the `read_write_articles_scope` OAuth scope.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "title": "Christmas is here!",
  "body": "<p>New gifts in store for the jolly season</p>"
}
```

<h3 id="update-an-article-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Intercom-Version|header|[intercom_version](#schemaintercom_version)|false|none|
|article_id|path|integer|true|The unique identifier for the article which is given by Intercom.|
|body|body|[update_article_request](#schemaupdate_article_request)|false|none|
|» title|body|string|false|The title of the article. For multilingual articles, this will be the title of the default language's content.|
|» description|body|string|false|The description of the article. For multilingual articles, this will be the description of the default language's content.|
|» body|body|string|false|The content of the article in HTML. For multilingual articles, this will be the body of the default language's content. Mutually exclusive with `body_markdown`.|
|» body_markdown|body|string|false|The content of the article in markdown. For multilingual articles, this will be the body of the default language's content. An alternative to `body` — you can provide content as markdown instead of HTML. Mutually exclusive with `body`.|
|» author_id|body|integer|false|The id of the author of the article. For multilingual articles, this will be the id of the author of the default language's content. Must be a teammate on the help center's workspace.|
|» state|body|string|false|Whether the article will be `published` or will be a `draft`. Omitting this field leaves the publish state unchanged, so a draft stays a draft and an edit to a published article goes live immediately unless that article already has a pending draft or a scheduled publish time is set in the same request. For multilingual articles, this will be the state of the default language's content.|
|» parent_id|body|string \| null|false|The id of the collection or section to move the article into. Omitting this field or sending `null` leaves the article's parent unchanged. Send `home` to remove the article from its collection so that it stands alone.|
|» parent_ids|body|[integer]|false|The ids of the parent collections to place this article in. Send an empty array to remove the article from all collections. When provided, this takes precedence over `parent_id`.|
|» translated_content|body|[article_translated_content](#schemaarticle_translated_content)|false|The Translated Content of an Article. The keys are the locale codes and the values are the translated content of the article.|
|» folder_id|body|integer \| null|false|The ID of the folder to place this article in, or null to remove it from its folder.|
|» audience_ids|body|[integer]|false|The list of audience IDs to assign to this article for Fin AI Agent targeting. Sending a top-level `audience_ids` broadcasts the same set to every locale. Sending `audience_ids: []` clears all audience memberships from every locale. For per-locale targeting, use `translated_content.<locale>.audience_ids` instead. Sending both top-level and per-locale in the same request causes top-level to win. Unknown audience IDs return a 404 error. No partial commit occurs.|
|» ai_chatbot_availability|body|boolean|false|Whether the article should be available for AI Chatbot (Fin). For multilingual articles, this sets the default language's availability.|
|» ai_copilot_availability|body|boolean|false|Whether the article should be available for AI Copilot. For multilingual articles, this sets the default language's availability.|
|» ai_sales_agent_availability|body|boolean|false|Whether the article should be available for AI Sales Agent. For multilingual articles, this sets the default language's availability.|
|» scheduled_publish_at|body|string(date-time) \| null|false|ISO 8601 timestamp at which to schedule a future publish of the article. When set together with `state: "published"`, the article is scheduled instead of published immediately. Setting `null` cancels a pending publish schedule. Timestamps in the past or equal to the current time are rejected with 400 `parameter_invalid` — the value must be strictly in the future. Combining with `state: "draft"` returns 400 `parameter_invalid`. Sending in the same request as `scheduled_unpublish_at` returns 400 — only one pending schedule per article. Empty string returns 400 `parameter_invalid`.|
|» scheduled_unpublish_at|body|string(date-time) \| null|false|ISO 8601 timestamp at which to schedule a future unpublish of the article. The article must already be published; setting `state: "published"` in the same request does not count, and the request returns 400 `parameter_invalid`. Combining with `state: "draft"` also returns 400 `parameter_invalid`. The value must be strictly in the future; timestamps in the past or equal to the current time are rejected with 400 `parameter_invalid`. Setting `null` cancels a pending unpublish schedule. Sending in the same request as `scheduled_publish_at` returns 400 — only one pending schedule per article. Empty string returns 400 `parameter_invalid`.|

`GET /articles/{id}/draft`

## Stage an article draft

<a id="opIdstageArticleDraft"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.intercom.io/articles/123/draft \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "title": "Christmas is here!",
    "body": "<p>New gifts in store for the jolly season</p>"
  }'
```

`PUT /articles/{id}/draft`

Stage changes to a published article as a draft by making a PUT request to
`https://api.intercom.io/articles/<id>/draft`. The live article remains
unchanged until the draft is published.

The article must already be published; staging a draft on an article that
has never been published returns `422`. That `422` has the short body
`{ "errors": [{ "message": "...", "status": 422 }] }`, with no `type`,
`request_id` or `code`. Other `422` errors use the standard error format.

Only text content is staged: `title`, `description`, `body` or
`body_markdown`, and `author_id`, including per-locale values in
`translated_content`. Any other field in the request body, such as `state`,
`parent_id`, `folder_id`, `audience_ids`, the AI availability fields or the
scheduling fields, is still validated but not applied, so the live article is left untouched. The
scheduling, state and placement notes on the request schema's other fields
do not apply to this endpoint, because those fields are not applied.

Requires the `read_write_articles_scope` OAuth scope.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "title": "Christmas is here!",
  "body": "<p>New gifts in store for the jolly season</p>"
}
```

<h3 id="stage-an-article-draft-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Intercom-Version|header|[intercom_version](#schemaintercom_version)|false|none|
|id|path|integer|true|The unique identifier for the article which is given by Intercom.|
|body|body|[update_article_request](#schemaupdate_article_request)|false|none|
|» title|body|string|false|The title of the article. For multilingual articles, this will be the title of the default language's content.|
|» description|body|string|false|The description of the article. For multilingual articles, this will be the description of the default language's content.|
|» body|body|string|false|The content of the article in HTML. For multilingual articles, this will be the body of the default language's content. Mutually exclusive with `body_markdown`.|
|» body_markdown|body|string|false|The content of the article in markdown. For multilingual articles, this will be the body of the default language's content. An alternative to `body` — you can provide content as markdown instead of HTML. Mutually exclusive with `body`.|
|» author_id|body|integer|false|The id of the author of the article. For multilingual articles, this will be the id of the author of the default language's content. Must be a teammate on the help center's workspace.|
|» state|body|string|false|Whether the article will be `published` or will be a `draft`. Omitting this field leaves the publish state unchanged, so a draft stays a draft and an edit to a published article goes live immediately unless that article already has a pending draft or a scheduled publish time is set in the same request. For multilingual articles, this will be the state of the default language's content.|
|» parent_id|body|string \| null|false|The id of the collection or section to move the article into. Omitting this field or sending `null` leaves the article's parent unchanged. Send `home` to remove the article from its collection so that it stands alone.|
|» parent_ids|body|[integer]|false|The ids of the parent collections to place this article in. Send an empty array to remove the article from all collections. When provided, this takes precedence over `parent_id`.|
|» translated_content|body|[article_translated_content](#schemaarticle_translated_content)|false|The Translated Content of an Article. The keys are the locale codes and the values are the translated content of the article.|
|» folder_id|body|integer \| null|false|The ID of the folder to place this article in, or null to remove it from its folder.|
|» audience_ids|body|[integer]|false|The list of audience IDs to assign to this article for Fin AI Agent targeting. Sending a top-level `audience_ids` broadcasts the same set to every locale. Sending `audience_ids: []` clears all audience memberships from every locale. For per-locale targeting, use `translated_content.<locale>.audience_ids` instead. Sending both top-level and per-locale in the same request causes top-level to win. Unknown audience IDs return a 404 error. No partial commit occurs.|
|» ai_chatbot_availability|body|boolean|false|Whether the article should be available for AI Chatbot (Fin). For multilingual articles, this sets the default language's availability.|
|» ai_copilot_availability|body|boolean|false|Whether the article should be available for AI Copilot. For multilingual articles, this sets the default language's availability.|
|» ai_sales_agent_availability|body|boolean|false|Whether the article should be available for AI Sales Agent. For multilingual articles, this sets the default language's availability.|
|» scheduled_publish_at|body|string(date-time) \| null|false|ISO 8601 timestamp at which to schedule a future publish of the article. When set together with `state: "published"`, the article is scheduled instead of published immediately. Setting `null` cancels a pending publish schedule. Timestamps in the past or equal to the current time are rejected with 400 `parameter_invalid` — the value must be strictly in the future. Combining with `state: "draft"` returns 400 `parameter_invalid`. Sending in the same request as `scheduled_unpublish_at` returns 400 — only one pending schedule per article. Empty string returns 400 `parameter_invalid`.|
|» scheduled_unpublish_at|body|string(date-time) \| null|false|ISO 8601 timestamp at which to schedule a future unpublish of the article. The article must already be published; setting `state: "published"` in the same request does not count, and the request returns 400 `parameter_invalid`. Combining with `state: "draft"` also returns 400 `parameter_invalid`. The value must be strictly in the future; timestamps in the past or equal to the current time are rejected with 400 `parameter_invalid`. Setting `null` cancels a pending unpublish schedule. Sending in the same request as `scheduled_publish_at` returns 400 — only one pending schedule per article. Empty string returns 400 `parameter_invalid`.|

## Publish an article draft

<a id="opIdpublishArticleDraft"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.intercom.io/articles/123/draft/publish \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "locales": [
      "en",
      "fr"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /articles/{id}/draft/publish`

Publish a staged draft by making a POST request to
`https://api.intercom.io/articles/<id>/draft/publish`, promoting the draft
content to live.

On a single-language workspace no body is required. On a multilingual
workspace you must list which locales to publish via the `locales` array;
omitting it returns `422`. Returns `422` when there is no staged draft to
publish, or when a requested locale has no pending changes.

The `422` for no staged draft has the short body
`{ "errors": [{ "message": "...", "status": 422 }] }`, with no `type`,
`request_id` or `code`. The other `422` errors use the standard error format.

Requires the `read_write_articles_scope` OAuth scope.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "locales": [
    "en",
    "fr"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="publish-an-article-draft-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Intercom-Version|header|[intercom_version](#schemaintercom_version)|false|none|
|id|path|integer|true|The unique identifier for the article which is given by Intercom.|
|body|body|[publish_article_draft_request](#schemapublish_article_draft_request)|false|none|
|» locales|body|[string]|false|The locales whose staged drafts should be published. Required on<br>multilingual workspaces; each locale must have a pending draft.<br>|
|» author_id|body|integer|false|The id of the teammate to publish as. This is only used when the access token is not associated with a teammate, and is then required; omitting it returns 400 `parameter_not_found`. Otherwise the authenticating teammate is used. Must be a teammate on the workspace.|

`POST /articles/{article_id}/tags`

## List article versions

<a id="opIdlistArticleVersions"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.intercom.io/articles/123/versions \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /articles/{article_id}/versions`

Fetch the version history of an article by making a GET request to
`https://api.intercom.io/articles/<article_id>/versions`. Versions are
returned newest-first as a paginated list of metadata. Use
`GET /articles/{article_id}/versions/{id}` to retrieve a single version
with its full content.

A `404` has an empty response body, whether the article or its content
isn't found.

Requires the `read_articles_scope` OAuth scope.


<h3 id="list-article-versions-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Intercom-Version|header|[intercom_version](#schemaintercom_version)|false|none|
|article_id|path|integer|true|The unique identifier for the article whose versions you are listing.|
|page|query|integer|false|The page of results to fetch. Defaults to the first page.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of results to return per page. Defaults to 10.|
|locale|query|string|false|Filter versions to a specific locale. Use the locale identifier (for example `en`, `fr`). If the article has no content in that locale, a `400` is returned.|

## Retrieve an article version

<a id="opIdretrieveArticleVersion"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.intercom.io/articles/123/versions/301 \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /articles/{article_id}/versions/{id}`

Fetch a single prior version of an article, including its body content,
by making a GET request to
`https://api.intercom.io/articles/<article_id>/versions/<id>`. Returns
the version's full content; the live article remains untouched.

A `404` has an empty response body, whether the article, its content or
the version isn't found.

Requires the `read_articles_scope` OAuth scope.

|id|path|string|true|The unique identifier for the version.|
|locale|query|string|false|Return the version's content for a specific locale. If the article has no content in that locale, a `400` is returned.|

<h1 id="intercom-api-banners">Banners</h1>

Retrieve the banners a contact matches and record dismissals, so you can display
banners on surfaces outside the Messenger (native mobile apps, kiosks, embedded
tools). These endpoints require an OAuth token with the `read_write_users` scope.
Requesting a contact's banners records an impression for each banner returned, and
dismissals are shared with the web Messenger.


## List banners for a contact

<a id="opIdlistContactBanners"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.intercom.io/contacts/string/banners \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /contacts/{id}/banners`

Returns the banners a contact currently matches, so you can display them on
surfaces outside the Messenger (native mobile apps, kiosks, embedded tools).

Each banner in the response includes a `view_id`. Use it to record a dismissal
with the dismiss endpoint. A returned banner is treated as shown: requesting
this endpoint records an impression for each banner returned, so call it at the
point you are about to display the banners, not speculatively.

Requires the `read_users_companies` or `read_write_users` OAuth scope.


<h3 id="list-banners-for-a-contact-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|The unique identifier of a contact.|
|Intercom-Version|header|[intercom_version](#schemaintercom_version)|false|none|

## Dismiss a banner for a contact

<a id="opIddismissContactBanner"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.intercom.io/contacts/string/banners/string/dismiss \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /contacts/{id}/banners/{view_id}/dismiss`

Records that a contact has dismissed a banner. Dismissals are shared across
surfaces, so a banner dismissed through this endpoint will also stop appearing
in the web Messenger for that contact, and vice versa.

The request is idempotent: dismissing an already-dismissed banner succeeds and
returns the same response.

Requires the `read_write_users` OAuth scope.


<h3 id="dismiss-a-banner-for-a-contact-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|The unique identifier of a contact.|
|view_id|path|string|true|The `view_id` of the banner to dismiss, as returned by the list banners endpoint.|
|Intercom-Version|header|[intercom_version](#schemaintercom_version)|false|none|

## List calls with transcripts

<a id="opIdlistCallsWithTranscripts"></a>

`POST /calls/search`

Retrieve calls by a list of conversation ids and include transcripts when available.
A maximum of 20 `conversation_ids` can be provided. If none are provided or more than 20 are provided, a 400 error is returned.

|» fin_transcription_url|string(uri) \| null|false|none|API URL to the AI Agent (Fin) call transcript if available.|

## Register a Fin Voice call

<a id="opIdregisterFinVoiceCall"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.intercom.io/fin_voice/register \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "phone_number": "+1234567890",
    "call_id": "call-123-abc",
    "source": "aws_connect",
    "vendor_internal_id": "vendor-internal-abc-123",
    "data": {
      "key": "value"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /fin_voice/register`

Register a Fin Voice call with Intercom. This endpoint creates an external reference
that links an external call identifier to an Intercom call and conversation.

The call can be from different sources:
- AWS Connect (default)
- Five9
- Zoom Phone
- NICE CXone
- Dialpad
- Generic

Requires the `read_conversations` OAuth scope.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "phone_number": "+1234567890",
  "call_id": "call-123-abc",
  "source": "aws_connect",
  "vendor_internal_id": "vendor-internal-abc-123",
  "data": {
    "key": "value"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="register-a-fin-voice-call-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Intercom-Version|header|[intercom_version](#schemaintercom_version)|false|none|
|body|body|[register_fin_voice_call_request](#schemaregister_fin_voice_call_request)|false|none|
|» phone_number|body|string|true|Phone number in E.164 format for the call|
|» call_id|body|string|true|External call identifier from the call provider|
|» source|body|string|false|Source of the call. Can be "five9", "zoom_phone", "nice_cxone", "dialpad", "generic", or "aws_connect". Defaults to "aws_connect", and any other value is treated as "aws_connect".|
|» vendor_internal_id|body|string \| null|false|Optional vendor-supplied identifier for linking the Fin Voice session to records in the vendor's own systems. Stored as-is and returned on every lookup.|
|» data|body|object \| null|false|Additional metadata about the call|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|Intercom-Version|1.0|
|Intercom-Version|1.1|
|Intercom-Version|1.2|
|Intercom-Version|1.3|
|Intercom-Version|1.4|
|Intercom-Version|2.0|
|Intercom-Version|2.1|
|Intercom-Version|2.2|
|Intercom-Version|2.3|
|Intercom-Version|2.4|
|Intercom-Version|2.5|
|Intercom-Version|2.6|
|Intercom-Version|2.7|
|Intercom-Version|2.8|
|Intercom-Version|2.9|
|Intercom-Version|2.10|
|Intercom-Version|2.11|
|Intercom-Version|2.12|
|Intercom-Version|2.13|
|Intercom-Version|2.14|
|Intercom-Version|2.15|
|Intercom-Version|2.16|
|Intercom-Version|2.17|
|» source|five9|
|» source|zoom_phone|
|» source|nice_cxone|
|» source|dialpad|
|» source|generic|
|» source|aws_connect|

  "app_id": 12345,

## Retrieve companies

<a id="opIdretrieveCompany"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.intercom.io/companies \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /companies`

You can fetch a single company by passing in `company_id` or `name`.

  `https://api.intercom.io/companies?name={name}`

  `https://api.intercom.io/companies?company_id={company_id}`

You can fetch all companies and filter by `segment_id` or `tag_id` as a query parameter.

  `https://api.intercom.io/companies?tag_id={tag_id}`

  `https://api.intercom.io/companies?segment_id={segment_id}`

The list is paged by page number. There is a limit of 10,000 companies; beyond that the request returns a `400` error and you should use the scroll endpoint instead.


<h3 id="retrieve-companies-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Intercom-Version|header|[intercom_version](#schemaintercom_version)|false|none|
|name|query|string|false|The `name` of the company to filter by.|
|company_id|query|string|false|The `company_id` of the company to filter by.|
|tag_id|query|string|false|The `tag_id` of the company to filter by.|
|segment_id|query|string|false|The `segment_id` of the company to filter by.|
|type|query|string|false|Set to `user` or `users`, together with `company_id` or `name`, to return that company's users instead of the company. The response is then a `user.list` object with a `users` array in the legacy user format, paged with `page` and `per_page` (default 50).|
|page|query|integer|false|The page of results to fetch. Defaults to first page|
|per_page|query|integer|false|How many results to display per page. Defaults to 15. A value above 60 returns a `400` error with code `parameter_invalid`.|

|---|---|
|Intercom-Version|1.0|

## Create or Update a company

<a id="opIdcreateOrUpdateCompany"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.intercom.io/companies \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "company_id": "company_remote_id",
    "name": "my company",
    "remote_created_at": 1374138000
  }'
```

`POST /companies`

You can create or update a company.

Companies will be only visible in Intercom when there is at least one associated user.

Companies are looked up via `company_id` in a `POST` request, if not found via `company_id`, the new company will be created, if found, that company will be updated.

You must send either `company_id` or `id`. A request with neither returns a `400` error.

Every custom attribute you send must already exist in your workspace. Sending one that doesn't returns a `400` error.

{% admonition type="warning" name="Using `company_id`" %}
  You can set a unique `company_id` value when creating a company. However, it is not possible to update `company_id`. Be sure to set a unique value once upon creation of the company.
{% /admonition %}

Requires the `write_users_companies` OAuth scope.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "company_id": "company_remote_id",
  "name": "my company",
  "remote_created_at": 1374138000
}
```

<h3 id="create-or-update-a-company-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Intercom-Version|header|[intercom_version](#schemaintercom_version)|false|none|
|body|body|[create_or_update_company_request](#schemacreate_or_update_company_request)|false|none|
|» name|body|string|false|The name of the Company. Leading and trailing whitespace is removed.|
|» company_id|body|string|false|The company id you have defined for the company. Can't be updated|
|» id|body|string|false|An alternative name for `company_id`. Supply this or `company_id`.|
|» plan|body|string|false|The name of the plan you have associated with the company.|
|» size|body|integer|false|The number of employees in this company.|
|» website|body|string|false|The URL for this company's website. Please note that the value specified here is not validated. Accepts any string.|
|» industry|body|string|false|The industry that this company operates in.|
|» custom_attributes|body|object|false|Values for custom attributes that already exist in your workspace. Each value can be a string, integer, number, boolean or null. Arrays and objects aren't accepted.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string \| null \| integer \| number \| boolean|false|none|
|» » » *anyOf*|body|string \| null|false|none|
|» » » *anyOf*|body|integer|false|none|
|» » » *anyOf*|body|number|false|none|
|» » » *anyOf*|body|boolean|false|none|
|» remote_created_at|body|integer|false|The time the company was created by you.|
|» update_last_request_at|body|boolean|false|Set to true to update the company's last seen time to now.|
|» monthly_spend|body|integer|false|How much revenue the company generates for your business. Floats are truncated to whole integers, so 155.98 is stored as 155. A value above 2147483647 (2**31-1) is stored as 0. 2147483647 itself, or a value of -2147483648 or below, returns a `422` error.|

## Retrieve a company by ID

<a id="opIdRetrieveACompanyById"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.intercom.io/companies/5f4d3c1c-7b1b-4d7d-a97e-6095715c6632 \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /companies/{company_id}`

You can fetch a single company.

<h3 id="retrieve-a-company-by-id-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Intercom-Version|header|[intercom_version](#schemaintercom_version)|false|none|
|company_id|path|string|true|The unique identifier for the company which is given by Intercom|
|type|query|string|false|Set to `user` or `users` to return the company's users instead of the company. The response is then a `user.list` object with a `users` array in the legacy user format.|
|page|query|integer|false|The page of users to fetch. Used only when `type` is `user` or `users`. Defaults to first page. There is a limit of 10,000 users; a `page` and `per_page` that go past it return a `400` error with code `bad_request`.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|How many users to return per page. Used only when `type` is `user` or `users`. Defaults to 50. A value above 60 returns a `400` error with code `parameter_invalid`.|

## Update a company

<a id="opIdUpdateCompany"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.intercom.io/companies/5f4d3c1c-7b1b-4d7d-a97e-6095715c6632 \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "my company",
    "website": "http://www.mycompany.com/"
  }'
```

`PUT /companies/{company_id}`

You can update a single company using the Intercom provisioned `id`.

Every custom attribute you send must already exist in your workspace. Sending one that doesn't returns a `400` error.

You can also send this request with `PATCH`; it behaves the same as `PUT`.

{% admonition type="warning" name="Using `company_id`" %}
  When updating a company it is not possible to update `company_id`. This can only be set once upon creation of the company.
{% /admonition %}

Requires the `write_users_companies` OAuth scope.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "my company",
  "website": "http://www.mycompany.com/"
}
```

## Delete a company

<a id="opIddeleteCompany"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.intercom.io/companies/5f4d3c1c-7b1b-4d7d-a97e-6095715c6632 \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /companies/{company_id}`

Delete a single company.

The company record is kept in your workspace, but all contacts are detached. The contacts themselves are not deleted. Detaching contacts is permanent and can't be reversed. These changes may take some time to be reflected in your workspace.

The response returns `"deleted": true` as soon as the request is accepted; the contacts are detached in the background. A `company.deleted` webhook is sent after that work finishes, so it arrives some time after the response. No webhook is sent for a company that has no contacts attached, because there is nothing to detach.

{% admonition type="warning" %}
Third-party integrations that sync companies into Intercom (for example, Salesforce or Chargebee) will recreate any company deleted through this endpoint on their next sync. To prevent recreation, remove or filter the company at the source integration before deleting it via the API.
{% /admonition %}

Requires the `write_users_companies` OAuth scope.

## Search companies

<a id="opIdsearchCompanies"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.intercom.io/companies/search \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "query": {
      "operator": "AND",
      "value": [
        {
          "field": "name",
          "operator": "=",
          "value": "my-company"
        }
      ]
    },
    "sort": {
      "field": "name",
      "order": "ascending"
    },
    "pagination": {
      "per_page": 5
    }
  }'
```

`POST /companies/search`

You can search for companies by the value of their attributes in order to fetch exactly the companies you want.

To search for companies, send a `POST` request to `https://api.intercom.io/companies/search`, with a query object in the body defining your filters.

Note that the API does not include companies who have no associated users in search results.

{% admonition type="warning" name="Optimizing search queries" %}
  Search queries can be complex, so optimizing them can help the performance of your search.
  Use the `AND` and `OR` operators to combine multiple filters to get the exact results you need and utilize
  pagination to limit the number of results returned. The default is `15` results per page.
  See the [pagination section](https://developers.intercom.com/docs/build-an-integration/learn-more/rest-apis/pagination/#example-search-conversations-request) for more details on how to use the `starting_after` param.
{% /admonition %}

### Nesting & Limitations

You can nest these filters in order to get even more granular insights that pinpoint exactly what you need. Example: (1 OR 2) AND (3 OR 4).
There are some limitations to the amount of multiple's there can be:
* There's a limit of max 2 nested filters
* There's a limit of max 15 filters for each AND or OR group

### Accepted Fields

Most keys listed as part of the Companies Model are searchable. The value you search for has to match the accepted type, otherwise the query will fail (ie. as `created_at` accepts a date, the `value` cannot be a string such as `"foobar"`).

| Field                              | Type                           |
| ---------------------------------- | ------------------------------ |
| company_id                         | String                         |
| name                               | String                         |
| created_at                         | Date (UNIX Timestamp)          |
| updated_at                         | Date (UNIX Timestamp)          |
| remote_created_at                  | Date (UNIX Timestamp)          |
| last_request_at                    | Date (UNIX Timestamp)          |
| monthly_spend                      | Integer                        |
| session_count                      | Integer                        |
| user_count                         | Integer                        |
| tag_id                             | String                         |
| custom_attributes.{attribute_name} | String                         |

The `plan.id` and `plan.name` fields are not searchable and return a `400` error with code `invalid_field`.

### Accepted Operators

The table below shows the operators you can use to define how you want to search for the value. The operator should be put in as a string (`"="`). The operator has to be compatible with the field's type (eg. you cannot search with `>` for a given string value as it's only compatible for integer's and dates). Searching by `tag_id` supports only the `=` and `!=` operators. The `IN` and `NIN` operators are not supported for Date fields.

| Operator | Valid Types                      | Description                                                      |
| :------- | :------------------------------- | :--------------------------------------------------------------- |
| =        | All                              | Equals                                                           |
| !=       | All                              | Doesn't Equal                                                    |
| IN       | All except Date and tag_id       | In<br>Shortcut for `OR` queries<br>Values must be in Array       |
| NIN      | All except Date and tag_id       | Not In<br>Shortcut for `OR !` queries<br>Values must be in Array |
| >        | Integer<br>Date (UNIX Timestamp) | Greater than                                                     |
| <       | Integer<br>Date (UNIX Timestamp) | Lower than                                                       |
| ~        | String                           | Contains                                                         |
| !~       | String                           | Doesn't Contain                                                  |
| ^        | String                           | Starts With                                                      |
| $        | String                           | Ends With                                                        |

### Sorting

Pass an optional `sort` object with a `field` and an `order` (`ascending` or `descending`; defaults to `descending`) to order the results. An invalid `order` returns a `400` error with code `invalid_sort_order`. `tag_id` can be used as a filter but not as a sort field.

### Pagination

Pass an optional `pagination` object with `per_page` and `starting_after`. `per_page` defaults to 15 and must be between 1 and 150; anything else returns a `400` error with code `invalid_per_page`. Take `starting_after` from `pages.next` in the previous response, and send it with the same `sort` you used for that response. A cursor from a sort on a text field such as `name`, sent with a sort on a number or date field (or the other way round), returns a `400` error with code `client_error`. Leaving out `sort` sorts by `last_request_at`, a date. A cursor sent with a different sort of the same kind is accepted, but the page it returns doesn't follow on from the previous one.

Requires the `read_users_companies` OAuth scope.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "query": {
    "operator": "AND",
    "value": [
      {
        "field": "name",
        "operator": "=",
        "value": "my-company"
      }
    ]
  },
  "sort": {
    "field": "name",
    "order": "ascending"
  },
  "pagination": {
    "per_page": 5
  }
}
```

## List all companies

<a id="opIdlistAllCompanies"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.intercom.io/companies/list \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /companies/list`

You can list companies. The company list is sorted by the `last_request_at` field and by default is ordered descending, most recently requested first.

Note that the API does not include companies who have no associated users in list responses.

When using the Companies endpoint and the pages object to iterate through the returned companies, there is a limit of 10,000 Companies that can be returned. If you need to list or iterate on more than 10,000 Companies, please use the [Scroll API](https://developers.intercom.com/reference#iterating-over-all-companies). Going past that limit returns a `400` error with code `bad_request`.
{% admonition type="warning" name="Pagination" %}
  This endpoint pages by page number, not by cursor. Use the `page` and `per_page` query parameters, and the `page`, `total_pages` and `next` values in the `pages` object of the response. The default is `15` results per page.
  See the [pagination section](https://developers.intercom.com/docs/build-an-integration/learn-more/rest-apis/pagination/#pagination-for-list-apis) for more details.
{% /admonition %}

Requires the `write_users_companies` OAuth scope. A token with only read scopes cannot call this endpoint.

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Intercom-Version|header|[intercom_version](#schemaintercom_version)|false|none|
|page|query|integer|false|The page of results to fetch. Defaults to first page|
|per_page|query|integer|false|How many results to return per page. Defaults to 15. A value above 60 returns a `400` error with code `parameter_invalid`.|
|order|query|string|false|`asc` or `desc`. Return the companies in ascending or descending order. Defaults to desc. Any other value returns a `400` error with code `parameter_invalid`.|

## Scroll over all companies

<a id="opIdscrollOverAllCompanies"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.intercom.io/companies/scroll \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /companies/scroll`

      The `list all companies` functionality does not work well for huge datasets, and can result in errors and performance problems when paging deeply. The Scroll API provides an efficient mechanism for iterating over all companies in a dataset.

- Each app can only have 1 scroll open at a time. Starting a second one returns a `400` error with code `scroll_exists`.
- If the scroll isn't used for 1 minute, it expires and calls with that scroll param return a `404` error with code `not_found`.
- If the end of the scroll is reached, `data` will be empty and the scroll parameter will expire.

The response always has `pages` and `total_count` set to `null`. Use `scroll_param` to fetch the next page.

{% admonition type="info" name="Scroll Parameter" %}
  You can get the first page of companies by simply sending a GET request to the scroll endpoint.
  For subsequent requests you will need to use the scroll parameter from the response.
{% /admonition %}
{% admonition type="danger" name="Scroll network timeouts" %}
  Since scroll is often used on large datasets network errors such as timeouts can be encountered. When this occurs you will see a HTTP 500 error with the following message:
  "Request failed due to an internal network error. Please restart the scroll operation."
  If this happens, you will need to restart your scroll query: It is not possible to continue from a specific point when using scroll.
{% /admonition %}

Requires the `read_users_companies` OAuth scope.

|---|---|---|---|---|
|Intercom-Version|header|[intercom_version](#schemaintercom_version)|false|none|
|scroll_param|query|string|false|The `scroll_param` from the previous response. Omit it to start a new scroll.|

## List attached companies for contact

<a id="opIdlistCompaniesForAContact"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.intercom.io/contacts/63a07ddf05a32042dffac965/companies \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /contacts/{contact_id}/companies`

You can fetch a list of companies that are associated to a contact.

<h3 id="list-attached-companies-for-contact-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|contact_id|path|string|true|The unique identifier for the contact which is given by Intercom|
|Intercom-Version|header|[intercom_version](#schemaintercom_version)|false|none|
|page|query|integer|false|The page of results to fetch. Values below 1 are treated as 1.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of companies to return per page. The maximum is 60; a value above 60 returns a `400` error with code `parameter_invalid`.|
|order|query|string|false|The order of the companies by when they were last active (`last_request_at`). The value is case-insensitive, and any value other than `asc` is treated as `desc`.|

## List subscriptions for a contact

<a id="opIdlistSubscriptionsForAContact"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.intercom.io/contacts/63a07ddf05a32042dffac965/subscriptions \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /contacts/{contact_id}/subscriptions`

You can fetch a list of subscription types that are attached to a contact. These can be subscriptions that a user has 'opted-in' to or has 'opted-out' from, depending on the subscription type.
This will return a list of Subscription Type objects that the contact is associated with.

The data property will show a combined list of:

  1.Opt-out subscription types that the user has opted-out from.
  2.Opt-in subscription types that the user has opted-in to receiving.

**Note:** This endpoint only returns subscriptions where the contact has explicitly configured their preference. Subscriptions that are in the default state — where the contact has not made an explicit opt-in or opt-out choice — are not included in the response.

## List deleted contacts

<a id="opIdlistDeletedContacts"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.intercom.io/contacts/deleted \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /contacts/deleted`

Fetch a paginated list of the contacts in your workspace that are no longer active,
so you can recover ones whose `id`, `email`, or `external_id` you no longer have and
then permanently delete them. Each entry carries a `status` describing why the contact
is inactive: `archived`, `blocked`, `merged`, `pending_deletion`, or `permanently_deleted`.
`merged_into_id` is present only when `status` is `merged`, and `external_id` and `email`
are `null` for `permanently_deleted` contacts.

Requires the `read_users_companies` or `read_write_users` OAuth scope.


<h3 id="list-deleted-contacts-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Intercom-Version|header|[intercom_version](#schemaintercom_version)|false|none|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of results per page. Defaults to `10`, with a maximum of `150`; larger values are treated as `150`. Only the leading digits are read, so `1.5` is treated as `1`. A value that doesn't start with a positive integer, such as `0` or `abc`, returns a `400` error with code `invalid_per_page`.|
|page|query|integer|false|The page of results to fetch. Defaults to `1`.|
|escape_identity|query|boolean|false|By default, `email` values in the response are HTML-escaped (for example, `&` is returned as `&amp;`). Pass `false` to return them unescaped.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|Intercom-Version|1.0|
|Intercom-Version|1.1|
|Intercom-Version|1.2|
|Intercom-Version|1.3|
|Intercom-Version|1.4|
|Intercom-Version|2.0|
|Intercom-Version|2.1|
|Intercom-Version|2.2|
|Intercom-Version|2.3|
|Intercom-Version|2.4|
|Intercom-Version|2.5|
|Intercom-Version|2.6|
|Intercom-Version|2.7|
|Intercom-Version|2.8|
|Intercom-Version|2.9|
|Intercom-Version|2.10|
|Intercom-Version|2.11|
|Intercom-Version|2.12|
|Intercom-Version|2.13|
|Intercom-Version|2.14|
|Intercom-Version|2.15|
|Intercom-Version|2.16|
|Intercom-Version|2.17|

> Example responses

  "type": "list",
  "data": [
    {
      "type": "contact",

## Get a contact

<a id="opIdShowContact"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.intercom.io/contacts/63a07ddf05a32042dffac965 \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /contacts/{contact_id}`

You can fetch the details of a single contact.

{% admonition type="info" name="Merged contacts return 410 Gone" %}
  If a contact has been merged into another contact via the Merge endpoint (`POST /contacts/merge`), requesting it by its original ID will return **HTTP 410 Gone** with a `Link` header pointing to the canonical (merged-into) contact.

  **Response headers:**
  ```
  Link: </contacts/{canonical_id}>; rel="canonical"
  ```

  **Response body:**
  ```json
  {
    "type": "error.list",
    "errors": [{ "code": "contact_merged", "message": "This contact has been merged. See the 'Link' header for the canonical contact." }]
  }
  ```

  The `Link` header contains the path to the final merge target, resolving multi-hop merge chains (up to 3 hops).
{% /admonition %}

Requires the `read_single_user`, `read_users_companies` or `read_write_users` OAuth scope.


<h3 id="get-a-contact-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Intercom-Version|header|[intercom_version](#schemaintercom_version)|false|none|
|contact_id|path|string|true|contact_id|
|include_merge_history|query|boolean|false|Pass `true` to include the contact's merge history in the response. Returned for contacts of any role, with at most the 10 most recent merges.|
|escape_identity|query|boolean|false|By default, `name` and `email` values in the response, including nested ones such as social profile names, are HTML-escaped (for example, `&` is returned as `&amp;`). Custom attributes and tags are never escaped. Pass `false` to return them unescaped.|

|---|---|
|Intercom-Version|1.0|
|Intercom-Version|1.1|
|Intercom-Version|1.2|
|Intercom-Version|1.3|
|Intercom-Version|1.4|
|Intercom-Version|2.0|
|Intercom-Version|2.1|
|Intercom-Version|2.2|

## Update a contact

<a id="opIdUpdateContact"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.intercom.io/contacts/63a07ddf05a32042dffac965 \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "email": "joebloggs@intercom.io",
    "name": "joe bloggs"
  }'
```

`PUT /contacts/{contact_id}`

You can update an existing contact (ie. user or lead).

{% admonition type="info" %}
  This endpoint handles both **contact updates** and **custom object associations**.

  See _`update a contact with an association to a custom object instance`_ in the request/response examples to see the custom object association format.
{% /admonition %}

Requires the `read_write_users` or `write_users_companies` OAuth scope.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "email": "joebloggs@intercom.io",
  "name": "joe bloggs"
}
```

|contact_id|path|string|true|id|
|include_merge_history|query|boolean|false|Pass `true` to include the contact's merge history in the response. Returned for contacts of any role, with at most the 10 most recent merges.|
|body|body|[update_contact_request](#schemaupdate_contact_request)|false|none|
|» *oneOf*|body|[update_contact_request](#schemaupdate_contact_request)|false|You can update a contact|

## Merge a lead and a user

<a id="opIdMergeContact"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.intercom.io/contacts/merge \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "from": "6762f0d51bb69f9f2193bb7f",
    "into": "6762f0d51bb69f9f2193bb80"
  }'
```

`POST /contacts/merge`

You can merge a contact with a `role` of `lead` into a contact with a `role` of `user`.

{% admonition type="warning" name="Merged contacts are not retrievable via the API" %}
  Once a merge is completed, the source contact (`from`) is permanently removed from the active contact list. This means:
  - **GET /contacts/{id}** — Requesting the source contact by its original ID returns `410 Gone` with a `Link` header pointing to the contact it was merged into. See [Get a contact](/docs/references/rest-api/api.intercom.io/contacts/showcontact).
  - **POST /contacts/search** — The source contact will not appear in search results, including queries filtered by `updated_at`.
  - **GET /contacts** — The source contact will not appear in list results.

  Only the target contact (`into`) remains accessible. If your application stores contact IDs, update them to use the target contact's ID after a merge.
{% /admonition %}

Requires the `read_write_users` or `write_users_companies` OAuth scope.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "from": "6762f0d51bb69f9f2193bb7f",
  "into": "6762f0d51bb69f9f2193bb80"
}
```

|---|---|---|---|---|
|Intercom-Version|header|[intercom_version](#schemaintercom_version)|false|none|
|include_merge_history|query|boolean|false|Pass `true` to include the merge history of the resulting contact in the response, with at most the 10 most recent merges.|
|body|body|[merge_contacts_request](#schemamerge_contacts_request)|false|none|
|» from|body|string|true|The unique identifier for the contact to merge away from. Must be a lead.|
|» into|body|string|true|The unique identifier for the contact to merge into. Must be a user.|
|» skip_duplicate_validation|body|boolean|false|Set to `true` to merge two contacts that are not duplicates (they share no matching email or phone).|
