<h1 id="intercom-api-custom-object-instances">Custom Object Instances</h1>

Everything about your Custom Object instances.
{% admonition type="warning" name="Permission Requirements" %}
  From now on, to access this endpoint, you need additional permissions. Please head over to the [Developer Hub](https://app.intercom.com/a/apps/_/developer-hub) app package authentication settings to configure the required permissions.
{% /admonition %}


## List Custom Object Instances

<a id="opIdlistCustomObjectInstances"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.intercom.io/custom_object_instances/Order \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /custom_object_instances/{custom_object_type_identifier}`

List instances of a custom object type. Three modes are supported:
- **No filter** — returns all instances for the type.
- **`references_contact_id`** — returns instances associated with the given contact.
- **`references_conversation_id`** — returns instances associated with the given conversation.

When **`external_id`** is provided, returns a single matching instance (not a list). If no instance matches, the response is still `200`, with the same body the single-instance endpoint returns for a miss.

Requires the `read_conversations`, `read_users_companies`, `read_write_custom_object_instances` or `read_write_users` OAuth scope.


<h3 id="list-custom-object-instances-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|references_contact_id|query|string|false|Return instances associated with the given contact ID.|
|references_conversation_id|query|string|false|Return instances associated with the given conversation ID.|
|external_id|query|string|false|Return the single instance with this external ID. When provided, the response is a single object rather than a list.|
|page|query|integer|false|Page number of results to fetch.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Number of results per page. Maximum 150.|
|Intercom-Version|header|[intercom_version](#schemaintercom_version)|false|none|
|custom_object_type_identifier|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the custom object type that defines the structure of the custom object instance.|

## Create or Update a Custom Object Instance

<a id="opIdcreateCustomObjectInstances"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.intercom.io/custom_object_instances/Order \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "external_id": "123",
    "external_created_at": 1392036272,
    "external_updated_at": 1392036272,
    "custom_attributes": {
      "order_number": "ORDER-12345",
      "total_amount": 99.99
    }
  }'
```

`POST /custom_object_instances/{custom_object_type_identifier}`

Create or update a custom object instance

Requires the `read_write_custom_object_instances` OAuth scope.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "external_id": "123",
  "external_created_at": 1392036272,
  "external_updated_at": 1392036272,
  "custom_attributes": {
    "order_number": "ORDER-12345",
    "total_amount": 99.99
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-or-update-a-custom-object-instance-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Intercom-Version|header|[intercom_version](#schemaintercom_version)|false|none|
|custom_object_type_identifier|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the custom object type that defines the structure of the custom object instance.|
|body|body|[create_or_update_custom_object_instance_request](#schemacreate_or_update_custom_object_instance_request)|false|none|
|» external_id|body|string|false|A unique identifier for the Custom Object instance in the external system it originated from. The value `reference_not_found` is reserved and is rejected with a `400`. Omitting this field creates a new instance on every request instead of updating an existing one.|
|» external_created_at|body|integer(date-time) \| null|false|The time when the Custom Object instance was created in the external system it originated from. A value that cannot be read as a time is stored as `null` rather than rejected.|
|» external_updated_at|body|integer(date-time) \| null|false|The time when the Custom Object instance was last updated in the external system it originated from. A value that cannot be read as a time is stored as `null` rather than rejected.|
|» custom_attributes|body|object \| null|false|The custom attributes which are set for the Custom Object instance.<br><br>Each value must match the type of the attribute it is set on: a string, integer, number or boolean, a Unix timestamp or date string for a datetime attribute, or `null` to clear the attribute. A list attribute takes the label or id of one of its options; a value that matches no option clears the attribute rather than being rejected. A reference attribute takes the Intercom id of the record it points at, or an array of ids for a reference to several records; an id that matches no record is skipped.|

<h1 id="intercom-api-data-attributes">Data Attributes</h1>

Everything about your Data Attributes

## List all data attributes

<a id="opIdlisDataAttributes"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.intercom.io/data_attributes \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /data_attributes`

You can fetch a list of all data attributes belonging to a workspace for contacts or companies.

{% admonition type="warning" %}
Conversation attributes are no longer returned by this endpoint. Calling without a `model` parameter no longer includes them, and `model=conversation` returns a `422` error. Use `GET /conversations/attributes` instead.
{% /admonition %}

Requires the `read_users_companies` or `read_write_users` OAuth scope.

|---|---|---|---|---|
|Intercom-Version|header|[intercom_version](#schemaintercom_version)|false|none|
|model|query|string|false|Specify the data attribute model to return. For conversation attributes, use GET /conversations/attributes instead.|
|include_archived|query|boolean|false|Include archived attributes in the list. By default we return only non archived data attributes.|

## Create a data attribute

<a id="opIdcreateDataAttribute"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.intercom.io/data_attributes \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "Mithril Shirt",
    "model": "company",
    "data_type": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /data_attributes`

You can create a data attributes for a `contact` or a `company`.

Requires the `write_attributes` OAuth scope.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "Mithril Shirt",
  "model": "company",
  "data_type": "string"
}
```

|» name|body|string|true|The name of the data attribute.|
|» model|body|string|true|The model that the data attribute belongs to.|
|» description|body|string|false|The readable description you see in the UI for the attribute.|

## Update a data attribute

<a id="opIdupdateDataAttribute"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.intercom.io/data_attributes/1 \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "description": "Just a plain old ring",
    "options": [
      {
        "value": "1-10"
      },
      {
        "value": "11-20"
      }
    ],
    "archived": false
  }'
```

`PUT /data_attributes/{data_attribute_id}`


You can update a data attribute.

> 🚧 Updating the data type is not possible
>
> It is currently a dangerous action to execute changing a data attribute's type via the API. You will need to update the type via the UI instead.

You can also send this request with `PATCH`; it behaves the same as `PUT`.

Requires the `write_attributes` OAuth scope.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "description": "Just a plain old ring",
  "options": [
    {
      "value": "1-10"
    },
    {
      "value": "11-20"
    }
  ],
  "archived": false
}
```

<h1 id="intercom-api-data-connectors">Data Connectors</h1>

Everything about your Data Connectors

## List all data connectors

<a id="opIdlistDataConnectors"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.intercom.io/data_connectors \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /data_connectors`

Returns a paginated list of all data connectors for the workspace, ordered by most recently updated first. Data connectors allow workflows and AI agents to make HTTP requests to external APIs.

OAuth tokens must have the `read_workflow_connector_execution_result` or `read_write_data_connectors` scope.


<h3 id="list-all-data-connectors-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Intercom-Version|header|[intercom_version](#schemaintercom_version)|false|none|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of results to return per page. Defaults to 20, minimum 1, maximum 50.|
|starting_after|query|string|false|The cursor value from `pages.next.starting_after` in a previous response. Used to paginate through results.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Intercom-Version|1.0|

## Create a data connector

<a id="opIdcreateDataConnector"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.intercom.io/data_connectors \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "Get Order Status",
    "description": "Looks up order status from an external service",
    "http_method": "get",
    "url": "https://api.example.com/orders/{{order_id}}/status",
    "direct_fin_usage": true,
    "audiences": [
      "leads",
      "visitors"
    ],
    "headers": [
      {
        "name": "Content-Type",
        "value": "application/json"
      }
    ],
    "data_inputs": [
      {
        "name": "order_id",
        "type": "string",
        "description": "The order ID to look up",
        "required": true,
        "default_value": ""
      }
    ],
    "customer_authentication": true,
    "bypass_authentication": false,
    "validate_missing_attributes": true
  }'
```

`POST /data_connectors`

Create a new data connector. The connector is created in `draft` state. Configure its URL, headers, data inputs, and other settings, then set it to `live` when ready.

OAuth tokens must have the `read_write_data_connectors` scope.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "Get Order Status",
  "description": "Looks up order status from an external service",
  "http_method": "get",
  "url": "https://api.example.com/orders/{{order_id}}/status",
  "direct_fin_usage": true,
  "audiences": [
    "leads",
    "visitors"
  ],
  "headers": [
    {
      "name": "Content-Type",
      "value": "application/json"
    }
  ],
  "data_inputs": [
    {
      "name": "order_id",
      "type": "string",
      "description": "The order ID to look up",
      "required": true,
      "default_value": ""
    }
  ],
  "customer_authentication": true,
  "bypass_authentication": false,
  "validate_missing_attributes": true
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-data-connector-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Intercom-Version|header|[intercom_version](#schemaintercom_version)|false|none|
|body|body|[create_data_connector_request](#schemacreate_data_connector_request)|false|none|
|» name|body|string|true|The name of the data connector.|
|» description|body|string|false|A description of what this data connector does.|
|» internal_description|body|string|false|The internal description of the data connector. If omitted, it is an empty string.|
|» http_method|body|string|false|The HTTP method used when calling the external API.|
|» url|body|string|false|The URL of the external API endpoint. Supports template variables like `{{order_id}}`.|
|» body|body|string|false|The request body template. Supports template variables.|
|» direct_fin_usage|body|boolean|false|Whether the connector is used directly by Fin (true) or only in workflows (false). Defaults to false.|
|» audiences|body|[string]|false|The user types this connector is available for.|
|» headers|body|[object]|false|HTTP headers to include in the request. Don't put credentials such as API keys here: header values are recorded unmasked in the connector's execution logs, except `Authorization`, which is always masked. Attach an authentication token with `token_ids` instead; its value is masked in execution logs.<br>|
|» » name|body|string|true|The header name.|
|» » value|body|string|true|The header value. Supports template variables.|

|» customer_authentication|body|boolean|false|Whether the connector requires customer authentication before executing. Defaults to false.|
|» bypass_authentication|body|boolean|false|Whether authentication is bypassed entirely (public endpoint). Defaults to false.|

<a id="opIdupdateDataConnector"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.intercom.io/data_connectors/12345 \
```

`PATCH /data_connectors/{id}`

Update an existing data connector. Only provided fields are changed. Set `state` to `live` or `draft` to change the connector's state.

OAuth tokens must have the `read_write_data_connectors` scope.

```json
  "name": "Updated Connector Name",
  "description": "Updated description"
}
```

|» direct_fin_usage|body|boolean|false|Whether this connector is used directly by Fin.|
|» audiences|body|[string]|false|The audience types this connector targets.|
|» headers|body|[object]|false|HTTP headers to include in the request. Don't put credentials such as API keys here: header values are recorded unmasked in the connector's execution logs, except `Authorization`, which is always masked. ## List execution results for a data connector

<a id="opIdlistDataConnectorExecutionResults"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.intercom.io/data_connectors/12345/execution_results \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /data_connectors/{data_connector_id}/execution_results`

Retrieve paginated execution logs for a specific data connector.
Results from the last hour are returned by default. Use `start_ts` and `end_ts` to customize the time range.

Request/response bodies are excluded by default. Use `include_bodies=true` to include them.

OAuth tokens must have the `read_workflow_connector_execution_result` or `read_write_data_connectors` scope.


<h3 id="list-execution-results-for-a-data-connector-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Intercom-Version|header|[intercom_version](#schemaintercom_version)|false|none|
|data_connector_id|path|string|true|The unique identifier for the data connector.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of results per page (1-30, default 10).|
|starting_after|query|string|false|Cursor for pagination. Use the value from `pages.next.starting_after` in a previous response.|
|success|query|string|false|Filter by success status. Use `true`, `false`, or omit for all.|
|error_type|query|string|false|Filter by error type.|
|start_ts|query|integer|false|Unix timestamp for start of time range (default 1 hour ago).|
|end_ts|query|integer|false|Unix timestamp for end of time range (default now).|
|include_bodies|query|string|false|Include request/response bodies in the response (default false).|

## List versions of a data connector

<a id="opIdlistDataConnectorVersions"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.intercom.io/data_connectors/12345/versions \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /data_connectors/{id}/versions`

Retrieve the version history of a data connector, newest first. Each entry is a point-in-time snapshot of the connector's configuration, with the status it has today and an optional note.

Results are paginated. `pages.next` is omitted on the last page. A data connector that has never been published returns an empty `data` list.

Requires the `read_data_connector_versions` or `read_write_data_connector_versions` OAuth scope.


<h3 id="list-versions-of-a-data-connector-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Intercom-Version|header|[intercom_version](#schemaintercom_version)|false|none|
|id|path|string|true|The unique identifier for the data connector.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of results per page (1-50, default 20). Values outside this range are clamped, so values below 1 are treated as 1. A non-integer value falls back to the default of 20.|
|starting_after|query|string|false|Cursor for pagination. Use the value from `pages.next.starting_after` in a previous response.|

## Update the note on a data connector version

<a id="opIdupdateDataConnectorVersion"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.intercom.io/data_connectors/12345/versions/9821 \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "note": "Switched to the v2 orders endpoint"
  }'
```

`PATCH /data_connectors/{id}/versions/{version_id}`

Update the note on a data connector version. The note is the only field that can be changed. This does not publish the version or roll the connector back to it.

Send an empty string to clear the note.

Requires the `read_write_data_connector_versions` OAuth scope.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "note": "Switched to the v2 orders endpoint"
}
```

|id|path|string|true|The unique identifier for the data connector.|

|body|body|[update_data_connector_version_request](#schemaupdate_data_connector_version_request)|true|none|

<h1 id="intercom-api-data-events">Data Events</h1>

Everything about your Data Events

## List all data events

<a id="opIdlisDataEvents"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.intercom.io/events?user_id=string&type=user' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /events`


> 🚧
>
> Please note that you can only 'list' events that are less than 90 days old. Event counts and summaries will still include your events older than 90 days but you cannot 'list' these events individually if they are older than 90 days

The events belonging to a customer can be listed by sending a GET request to `https://api.intercom.io/events` with a user or lead identifier along with a `type` parameter. The identifier parameter can be one of `user_id`, `email`, `intercom_user_id` or `anonymous_id`. The `type` parameter value must be `user` or `lead`.

- `https://api.intercom.io/events?type=user&user_id={user_id}`
- `https://api.intercom.io/events?type=user&email={email}`
- `https://api.intercom.io/events?type=user&intercom_user_id={id}` (this call can be used to list leads)

When `type` is `lead`, a `user_id` you send is matched against the lead's anonymous id instead.

The `email` parameter value should be [url encoded](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Percent-encoding) when sending.

You can optionally define the result page size as well with the `per_page` parameter.

Requires the `read_events` or `write_events` OAuth scope.

|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of events to return per page.|
|since|query|integer(int64)|false|Only return events created after this time, as a Unix timestamp in milliseconds. Take the value from the `since` link in the `pages` object of a previous response.|
|before|query|integer(int64)|false|Only return events created before this time, as a Unix timestamp in milliseconds. Take the value from the `next` link in the `pages` object of a previous response.|
|summary|query|boolean|false|Set to `true` (or `1`) to return an event summary (`event.summary`) instead of the list of events. Omit for the paginated event list (`event.list`).|

## Submit a data event

<a id="opIdcreateDataEvent"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.intercom.io/events \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "event_name": "invited-friend",
    "created_at": 1671028894,
    "user_id": "314159",
    "id": "8a88a590-e1c3-41e2-a502-e0649dbf721c",
    "email": "frodo.baggins@example.com",
    "metadata": {
      "invite_code": "ADDAFRIEND"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /events`


You will need an Access Token that has write permissions to send Events. Once you have a key you can submit events via POST to the Events resource, which is located at https://api.intercom.io/events, or you can send events using one of the client libraries. When working with the HTTP API directly a client should send the event with a `Content-Type` of `application/json`.

When using the JavaScript API, [adding the code to your app](http://docs.intercom.io/configuring-Intercom/tracking-user-events-in-your-app) makes the Events API available. Once added, you can submit an event using the `trackEvent` method. This will associate the event with the Lead or currently logged-in user or logged-out visitor/lead and send it to Intercom. The final parameter is a map that can be used to send optional metadata about the event.

With the Ruby client you pass a hash describing the event to `Intercom::Event.create`, or call the `track_user` method directly on the current user object (e.g. `user.track_event`).

**NB: For the JSON object types, please note that we do not currently support nested JSON structure.**

| Type            | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                     | Example                                                                           |
| :-------------- | :-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | :-------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| String          | The value is a JSON String                                                                                                                                                                                      | `"source":"desktop"`                                                              |
| Number          | The value is a JSON Number                                                                                                                                                                                      | `"load": 3.67`                                                                    |
| Date            | The key ends with the String `_date` and the value is a [Unix timestamp](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unix_time), assumed to be in the [UTC](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coordinated_Universal_Time) timezone. | `"contact_date": 1392036272`                                                      |
| Link            | The value is a HTTP or HTTPS URI.                                                                                                                                                                               | `"article": "https://example.org/ab1de.html"`                                     |
| Rich Link       | The value is a JSON object that contains `url` and `value` keys.                                                                                                                                                | `"article": {"url": "https://example.org/ab1de.html", "value":"the dude abides"}` |
| Monetary Amount | The value is a JSON object that contains `amount` and `currency` keys. The `amount` key is a positive integer representing the amount in cents. The price in the example to the right denotes €349.99.          | `"price": {"amount": 34999, "currency": "eur"}`                                   |

**Lead Events**

When submitting events for Leads, you will need to specify the Lead's `id`.

**Metadata behaviour**

- We currently limit the number of tracked metadata keys to 20 per event name. The limit counts every key ever recorded for that event name, not the keys in a single request, so it is reached cumulatively as you send more events with the same name. Once the quota is reached, we ignore any further keys we receive. The keys that count towards the quota are determined by the order in which they are sent in with the event.
- It is not possible to change the metadata keys once the event has been sent. A new event will need to be created with the new keys and you can archive the old one.
- There might be up to 24 hrs delay when you send a new metadata for an existing event.

**Event de-duplication**

The API may detect and ignore duplicate events. Each event is uniquely identified as a combination of the following data - the Workspace identifier, the Contact external identifier, the Data Event name and the Data Event created time. As a result, it is **strongly recommended** to send a second granularity Unix timestamp in the `created_at` field.

Duplicated events are responded to using the normal `202 Accepted` code - an error is not thrown, however repeat requests will be counted against any rate limit that is in place.

### HTTP API Responses

- Successful responses to submitted events return `202 Accepted` with an empty body.
- Unauthorised access will be rejected with a `401 Unauthorized` or `403 Forbidden` response code.
- Events sent about users that cannot be found will return a `404 Not Found`.
- Event lists containing duplicate events will have those duplicates ignored.
- Server errors will return a `500` response code and may contain an error message in the body.

Requires the `write_events` OAuth scope.



> Body parameter

```json
{
  "event_name": "invited-friend",
  "created_at": 1671028894,
  "user_id": "314159",
  "id": "8a88a590-e1c3-41e2-a502-e0649dbf721c",
  "email": "frodo.baggins@example.com",
  "metadata": {
    "invite_code": "ADDAFRIEND"
  }
}
```

## Create event summaries

<a id="opIddataEventSummaries"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.intercom.io/events/summaries \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "user_id": "314159",

      {
        "event_name": "invited-friend",
        "count": 1,
        "first": 1671028894,
        "last": 1671028894
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /events/summaries`

Create event summaries for a user. Event summaries are used to track the number of times an event has occurred, the first time it occurred and the last time it occurred.

Identify the user with one of `id`, `user_id` or `email`. If more than one is sent, `id` is used first, then `user_id`, then `email`.

Requires the `write_events` OAuth scope.


> Body parameter

```json

  "user_id": "314159",
  "id": "63a0979a5eeebeaf28dd56ba",
  "email": "frodo.baggins@example.com",
  "event_summaries": [
    {
      "event_name": "invited-friend",
      "count": 1,
      "first": 1671028894,
      "last": 1671028894
    }
  ]
}
```

<h1 id="intercom-api-data-export">Data Export</h1>

Export message delivery and engagement statistics (opens, clicks, replies, completions, dismissals, unsubscribes, bounces) for outbound content such as Emails, Posts, Custom Bots, Surveys, Tours, and Series.

## Create content data export

<a id="opIdcreateDataExport"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.intercom.io/export/content/data \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "created_at_after": 1734519776,
    "created_at_before": 1734537776
  }'
```

`POST /export/content/data`

To create your export job, you need to send a `POST` request to the export endpoint `https://api.intercom.io/export/content/data`.

This endpoint exports **message delivery and engagement data** for outbound content (Emails, Posts, Custom Bots, Surveys, Tours, Series, and more). The exported data includes who received each message, when they received it, and how they engaged with it (opens, clicks, replies, completions, dismissals, unsubscribes, and bounces). It does not export raw message or conversation content.

The only parameters you need to provide are the range of dates that you want exported. The range cannot be longer than 90 days.

>🚧 Limit of two active jobs
>
> You can only have two active jobs per workspace. You will receive a HTTP status code of 429 with the message Exceeded rate limit of 2 pending content data export jobs if you attempt to create a third concurrent job.

>❗️ Updated_at not included
>
> It should be noted that the timeframe only includes messages sent during the time period and not messages that were only updated during this period. For example, if a message was updated yesterday but sent two days ago, you would need to set the created_at_after date before the message was sent to include that in your retrieval job.

>📘 Date ranges are inclusive
>
> Requesting data for 2018-06-01 until 2018-06-30 will get all data for those days including those specified - e.g. 2018-06-01 00:00:00 until 2018-06-30 23:59:99.

Requires the `export_content_data` OAuth scope.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "created_at_after": 1734519776,
  "created_at_before": 1734537776
}
```

<h3 id="create-content-data-export-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Intercom-Version|header|[intercom_version](#schemaintercom_version)|false|none|
|body|body|[create_data_exports_request](#schemacreate_data_exports_request)|false|none|
|» created_at_after|body|integer|true|The start date that you request data for. It must be formatted as a unix timestamp.|
|» created_at_before|body|integer|true|The end date that you request data for. It must be formatted as a unix timestamp.|

## Show content data export

<a id="opIdgetDataExport"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.intercom.io/export/content/data/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /export/content/data/{job_identifier}`

You can view the status of your job by sending a `GET` request to the URL
`https://api.intercom.io/export/content/data/{job_identifier}` - the `{job_identifier}` is the value returned in the response when you first created the export job. More on it can be seen in the Export Job Model.

> 🚧 Jobs expire after one week
> All jobs that have completed processing (and are thus available to download from the provided URL) will have an expiry limit of one week from when the export job was created. After this, the data will no longer be available.

A job that failed is returned with a `504` status code and a `status` of `failed`. A job left in progress for more than a day is marked failed when you poll it.

Requires the `export_content_data` OAuth scope.

## Download content data export

<a id="opIddownloadDataExport"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.intercom.io/download/content/data/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /download/content/data/{job_identifier}`

When a job has a status of complete, and thus a filled download_url, you can download your data by hitting that provided URL, formatted like so: https://api.intercom.io/download/content/data/xyz1234.

Your exported message data is returned as a ZIP archive containing one CSV file per data group. The response is sent with the header `Content-Encoding: zip`.

> 📘 Octet header required
>
> You will have to specify the header Accept: `application/octet-stream` when hitting this endpoint.

Requires the `export_content_data` OAuth scope.

## Create dynamic content

<a id="opIdcreateDynamicContent"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.intercom.io/dynamic_contents \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "Support phone number",
    "content_type": "inline",
    "default_locale": "en",
    "variations": [
      {
        "locale": "en",
        "text_content": "+1-555-0100"
      },
      {
        "locale": "fr",
        "text_content": "+33 1 23 45 67 89"
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /dynamic_contents`

You can create dynamic content.

Requires the `read_write_dynamic_content` OAuth scope.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "Support phone number",
  "content_type": "inline",
  "default_locale": "en",
  "variations": [
    {
      "locale": "en",
      "text_content": "+1-555-0100"
    },
    {
      "locale": "fr",
      "text_content": "+33 1 23 45 67 89"
    }
  ]
}
```

|» name|body|string|true|The name of the dynamic content. Must be unique in the workspace.|
|» content_type|body|string|true|Whether the dynamic content is a short inline value (`inline`) or one or more blocks of content (`block`). Can't be changed later.|
|» default_locale|body|string|true|The locale whose variation is used when there's no variation for the requested locale. `variations` must include a variation for this locale that applies to all brands.|
|» variations|body|[[dynamic_content_variation_request](#schemadynamic_content_variation_request)]|true|The variations of the dynamic content, one per locale and optionally per brand. Set `brand_id` on a variation to override the all-brands value for that brand. At least one is required.|

## Update dynamic content

<a id="opIdupdateDynamicContent"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.intercom.io/dynamic_contents/123 \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "variations": [
      {
        "locale": "en",
        "text_content": "+1-555-0199"
      },
      {
        "locale": "fr",
        "text_content": "+33 1 23 45 67 89"
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`PUT /dynamic_contents/{id}`

You can update existing dynamic content. Only the fields you provide are changed.

You can also send this request with `PATCH`; it behaves the same as `PUT`.

Requires the `read_write_dynamic_content` OAuth scope.


> Body parameter

```json
{
```

<h1 id="intercom-api-fin-agent">Fin Agent</h1>

Access Fin programmatically via the Fin Agent API endpoints.

&nbsp;

{% admonition type="warning" %}
To request access to the Fin Agent API, go to **Settings > Integrations > Fin Agent API** in your workspace and tell us about your use case. Once access is granted, **Fin Agent API** appears under **Fin AI Agent > Deploy**.
{% /admonition %}

&nbsp;

Integration centres on the Fin Agent API endpoints — start a conversation with `/fin/start` and continue it with `/fin/reply`, or drive Fin from your own agent with `/fin/capabilities`, `/fin/ask`, `/fin/procedures/{procedure_id}/run`, and `/fin/escalate` — plus a set of events that notify your application of Fin's status and responses. Events are delivered via webhooks. You can also record a customer satisfaction rating with `/fin/csat`.

&nbsp;

**Events**

Configure a webhook endpoint in the Fin Agent API settings to receive events. See the [setup guide](/docs/guides/fin-agent-api/setup) for configuration details.

- `fin_status_updated` - Fired when Fin's status changes (awaiting_user_reply, escalated, resolved, complete)
- `fin_replied` - Fired when Fin sends a reply to the user
- `csat_requested` - Fired when Fin asks the user to rate the conversation (submit the choice with `POST /fin/csat`)

All webhook requests include an `X-Fin-Agent-API-Webhook-Signature` header for request validation.


## Start a conversation with Fin

<a id="opIdstartFinConversation"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.intercom.io/fin/start \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "conversation_id": "ext-123",
    "message": {
      "author": "user",
      "body": "How can I see my account details?",
      "timestamp": "2025-01-24T10:01:20.000Z"
    },
    "user": {
      "id": "123456",
      "name": "John Doe",
      "email": "john.doe@example.com"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /fin/start`

Initialize Fin by passing it the user's message along with conversation history and user details.

These additional pieces of context will be used by Fin to provide a better and more contextual answer to the user.

{% admonition type="warning" %}
To request access to the Fin Agent API, go to **Settings > Integrations > Fin Agent API** in your workspace and tell us about your use case. Once access is granted, **Fin Agent API** appears under **Fin AI Agent > Deploy**.
{% /admonition %}

Once Fin is initialized, it progresses through a series of statuses such as *thinking*, *replying*, *awaiting_user_reply*, or *resolved* before ending with a status of *complete*.

During this workflow, the client should allow Fin to continue uninterrupted until a final *complete* status is returned via webhook, at which point control of the conversation passes back to the client.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "conversation_id": "ext-123",
  "message": {
    "author": "user",
    "body": "How can I see my account details?",
    "timestamp": "2025-01-24T10:01:20.000Z"
  },
  "user": {
    "id": "123456",
    "name": "John Doe",
    "email": "john.doe@example.com"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="start-a-conversation-with-fin-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Intercom-Version|header|[intercom_version](#schemaintercom_version)|false|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» conversation_id|body|string|true|The ID of the conversation that is calling Fin via this API.|
|» message|body|[fin_agent_message](#schemafin_agent_message)|true|A message exchanged within a Fin Agent conversation.|
|» user|body|[fin_agent_user](#schemafin_agent_user)|true|A user object representing the user in a Fin Agent conversation.|
|» attachments|body|[[fin_agent_attachment](#schemafin_agent_attachment)]|false|An array of attachments to include with the message. Maximum of 10 attachments.|
|» conversation_metadata|body|[fin_agent_conversation_metadata](#schemafin_agent_conversation_metadata)|false|Metadata about the conversation, including history and attributes.|
|» environment|body|string|false|The identifier of the environment to start the conversation in. Only Fin for Platforms workspaces use it; other workspaces ignore it. Use the same value as `messenger_environment` in your Messenger installation. Defaults to the workspace's default environment. On a Fin for Platforms workspace, an identifier that matches no environment returns a 422 error.|
|» response_format|body|string|false|The format of the `body` in Fin's replies. Defaults to `html`. Requesting `markdown` on a workspace where it is not enabled returns a 403 error.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|Intercom-Version|1.0|
|Intercom-Version|1.1|
|Intercom-Version|1.2|
|Intercom-Version|1.3|
|Intercom-Version|1.4|
|Intercom-Version|2.0|
|Intercom-Version|2.1|
|Intercom-Version|2.2|
|Intercom-Version|2.3|
|Intercom-Version|2.4|
|Intercom-Version|2.5|
|Intercom-Version|2.6|
|Intercom-Version|2.7|
|Intercom-Version|2.8|
|Intercom-Version|2.9|
|Intercom-Version|2.10|
|Intercom-Version|2.11|
|Intercom-Version|2.12|
|Intercom-Version|2.13|
|Intercom-Version|2.14|
|Intercom-Version|2.15|
|Intercom-Version|2.16|
|Intercom-Version|2.17|
|» response_format|html|
|» response_format|markdown|

<h3 id="start-a-conversation-with-fin-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Fin conversation started successfully|Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Bad Request|[error](#schemaerror)|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized|[error](#schemaerror)|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden|[error](#schemaerror)|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|The request could not be processed. The response body maps each field name to its error message, or uses `base` for request-level failures. Values are usually strings. When a required field inside an object, such as `user.id`, is missing or invalid, the error is a nested object keyed by the inner field.|Inline|

## Reply to Fin

<a id="opIdreplyToFin"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.intercom.io/fin/reply \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "conversation_id": "123456",
    "message": {
      "author": "user",
      "body": "Here'\''s the information you requested.",
      "timestamp": "2025-01-24T09:01:00.000Z"
    },
    "user": {
      "id": "123456",
      "name": "John Doe",
      "email": "john.doe@example.com"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /fin/reply`

Once Fin has returned a response to a user's message, its status will be `awaiting_user_reply`.

If a user replies, use this endpoint to send this response to Fin.

{% admonition type="warning" %}
To request access to the Fin Agent API, go to **Settings > Integrations > Fin Agent API** in your workspace and tell us about your use case. Once access is granted, **Fin Agent API** appears under **Fin AI Agent > Deploy**.
{% /admonition %}

## Submit a CSAT rating

<a id="opIdsubmitFinCsat"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.intercom.io/fin/csat \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "conversation_id": "ext-123",
    "rating": "amazing"
  }'
```

`POST /fin/csat`

Record a customer's satisfaction rating for a conversation, with an optional free-text
remark.

Fin decides *when* to ask for a rating — this reuses the CSAT settings on your Fin
workflow, not this API. When Fin asks, it fires a `csat_requested` event over webhooks
carrying the rating options to show the user. Present those options, then submit the
user's choice here.

Submitting the same rating again, with no new remark, is a no-op and stays successful,
so an at-least-once client can safely retry. Submitting a *different* rating updates the
stored rating while the update window is still open, and a first remark can be added to
an already-rated survey. Once a remark has been recorded the rating is locked and can no
longer be changed.

{% admonition type="warning" %}
To request access to the Fin Agent API, go to **Settings > Integrations > Fin Agent API** in your workspace and tell us about your use case. Once access is granted, **Fin Agent API** appears under **Fin AI Agent > Deploy**.
{% /admonition %}


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "conversation_id": "ext-123",
  "rating": "amazing"
}
```

<h3 id="submit-a-csat-rating-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Intercom-Version|header|[intercom_version](#schemaintercom_version)|false|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» conversation_id|body|string|true|Your external conversation ID — the same ID you started the conversation with, and the one echoed on the `csat_requested` event.|
|» rating|body|string|true|The rating the user selected — one of the `key` values from the `csat_requested` event's options.|
|» remark|body|string|false|Optional free-text comment the user left alongside the rating. Can be added to an already-rated survey, but only once — the rating locks after a remark is recorded.|

## Discover Fin's capabilities

<a id="opIdlistFinCapabilities"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.intercom.io/fin/capabilities \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "user": {
      "id": "123456"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /fin/capabilities`

Return a machine-readable, per-user list of what Fin can do for a given end user, so an
orchestrating agent can decide which endpoint to call.

The response is audience-matched to the supplied user: each live, API-triggerable
procedure is checked against that user before being included, alongside the static
`reply`, `ask`, and `escalate` actions.

{% admonition type="warning" %}
To request access to the Fin Agent API, go to **Settings > Integrations > Fin Agent API** in your workspace and tell us about your use case. Once access is granted, **Fin Agent API** appears under **Fin AI Agent > Deploy**.
{% /admonition %}


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "user": {
    "id": "123456"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="discover-fins-capabilities-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Intercom-Version|header|[intercom_version](#schemaintercom_version)|false|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» user|body|object|true|none|
|» » id|body|string|true|The ID of the user. This value will be used to uniquely identify the user<br>during a conversation with Fin. Maps to the user_id field on the Intercom User object.<br>|
|» » name|body|string|false|The name of the user.|
|» » email|body|string(email)|false|The email of the user.|
|» » attributes|body|object|false|A hash of attributes associated with the user.<br>Attributes can be used by Fin to target content and responses.<br>Limit to 10 attributes.<br>|

## Ask Fin

<a id="opIdaskFin"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.intercom.io/fin/ask \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "conversation_id": "ext-123",
    "message": {
      "author": "user",
      "body": "How do I reset my password?",
      "timestamp": "2025-01-24T10:01:20.000Z"
    },
    "user": {
      "id": "123456",
      "name": "John Doe",
      "email": "john.doe@example.com"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /fin/ask`

Ask Fin a single, self-contained question and receive one informational answer.

Unlike a conversation, `/fin/ask` is non-conversational: Fin will not ask follow-up
questions, will not run procedures, and will not decide to hand over to a human itself.
Escalation rules can still match, and the conversation can still be routed to a team or
finish without resolution. You can also escalate one yourself with `POST /fin/escalate`;
the ask conversation is already closed after its one-shot answer, and escalation leaves
it closed while routing the handoff separately.

Fin's answer is delivered asynchronously via the `fin_replied` event. The conversation
ends with a `complete` status — there is no `awaiting_user_reply` cycle.

{% admonition type="warning" %}
To request access to the Fin Agent API, go to **Settings > Integrations > Fin Agent API** in your workspace and tell us about your use case. Once access is granted, **Fin Agent API** appears under **Fin AI Agent > Deploy**.
{% /admonition %}


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "conversation_id": "ext-123",
  "message": {
    "author": "user",
    "body": "How do I reset my password?",
    "timestamp": "2025-01-24T10:01:20.000Z"
  },
  "user": {
    "id": "123456",
    "name": "John Doe",
    "email": "john.doe@example.com"
  }
}
```

## Run a Fin procedure

<a id="opIdrunFinProcedure"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.intercom.io/fin/procedures/12345/run \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "conversation_id": "ext-123",
    "user": {
      "id": "123456",
      "name": "John Doe",
      "email": "john.doe@example.com"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /fin/procedures/{procedure_id}/run`

Deterministically run a specific procedure on a new conversation. Calling this endpoint
guarantees that the named procedure runs — there is no non-deterministic routing.

Fin's progress is delivered asynchronously via events. If the
procedure pauses for user input, the conversation status becomes `awaiting_user_reply` —
send the user's response with [`/fin/reply`](/docs/references/rest-api/api.intercom.io/fin-agent/replytofin).

{% admonition type="warning" %}
To request access to the Fin Agent API, go to **Settings > Integrations > Fin Agent API** in your workspace and tell us about your use case. Once access is granted, **Fin Agent API** appears under **Fin AI Agent > Deploy**.
{% /admonition %}


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "conversation_id": "ext-123",
  "user": {
    "id": "123456",
    "name": "John Doe",
    "email": "john.doe@example.com"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="run-a-fin-procedure-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Intercom-Version|header|[intercom_version](#schemaintercom_version)|false|none|

|» message|body|object|false|Optional message posted to the conversation before the procedure runs. Only `body` is required.|

## Escalate to a human

<a id="opIdescalateFinConversation"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.intercom.io/fin/escalate \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "conversation_id": "ext-123",
    "context": "Customer is requesting a refund and is frustrated."
  }'
```

`POST /fin/escalate`

Hand a conversation off to a human teammate. If you use the Intercom Helpdesk, the
handoff lands in your team inbox.

Provide either `conversation_id` or `user`:

- `conversation_id` — escalate an existing agent conversation, including one started
  with `/fin/ask`. On the Intercom Helpdesk, Fin by default summarises the conversation
  and opens a new Helpdesk conversation that carries the summary as an internal note.
  Configure an escalation Operator Workflow to change this default. Escalation closes the
  original agent conversation if it is open.
- `user` — escalate on behalf of a user with no prior agent conversation. Fin creates an
  agent conversation for the escalation and closes it once the handoff completes. On the
  Intercom Helpdesk, the teammate works in a separate new Helpdesk conversation. Not
  supported on Fin for Platforms — see below.

In both cases, pass the optional `context` to give the receiving teammate background your
orchestrating agent has and Fin does not. On the Intercom Helpdesk, it appears above the
summary in the internal note of the new conversation the teammate picks up. It is never
shown to the end user.

Escalating an existing conversation also sets its AI Agent resolution state to
`escalated`, readable as `ai_agent.resolution_state` on the Conversations API. This is a
resolution state, not a billable resolution.

On Fin for Platforms, `conversation_id` is required — `user` is not supported and is
rejected, because there is no Intercom Helpdesk in which to create a conversation. There
is no Intercom inbox either, so an escalation that no workflow handles does not open a
Helpdesk conversation for a teammate. `context` is not surfaced. The conversation is closed,
as on the Intercom Helpdesk, and your platform hands the user off to a human.

You are notified via webhooks with an `escalated` status
followed by `complete`. The `complete` status signals that Fin is done. By then the
original agent conversation has been closed. An escalation Operator Workflow may act
on it afterwards, but it is closed again once the workflow's first steps have run, so
only steps that run later (for example after a wait) can reopen it. On the Intercom
Helpdesk, the new human conversation remains open.

{% admonition type="warning" %}
To request access to the Fin Agent API, go to **Settings > Integrations > Fin Agent API** in your workspace and tell us about your use case. Once access is granted, **Fin Agent API** appears under **Fin AI Agent > Deploy**.
{% /admonition %}


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "conversation_id": "ext-123",
  "context": "Customer is requesting a refund and is frustrated."
}
```

<h3 id="escalate-to-a-human-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Intercom-Version|header|[intercom_version](#schemaintercom_version)|false|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» conversation_id|body|string|false|The external ID of the conversation to escalate. Provide this or `user`. Required on Fin for Platforms, where `user` is not supported.|
|» user|body|object|false|none|
|» » id|body|string|true|The ID of the user. This value will be used to uniquely identify the user<br>during a conversation with Fin. Maps to the user_id field on the Intercom User object.<br>|
|» » name|body|string|false|The name of the user.|
|» » email|body|string(email)|false|The email of the user.|
|» » attributes|body|object|false|A hash of attributes associated with the user.<br>Attributes can be used by Fin to target content and responses.<br>Limit to 10 attributes.<br>|
|» context|body|string|false|Optional background for the receiving teammate, valid with either `conversation_id` or `user`. On the Intercom Helpdesk, it appears above the summary in the internal note of the new conversation the teammate picks up, and is never shown to the end user. Not surfaced on Fin for Platforms. Avoid including credentials or unnecessary personal data — it is visible to any teammate with access to the conversation.|
|» *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|

<h1 id="intercom-api-folders">Folders</h1>

## List all folders

<a id="opIdlistFolders"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.intercom.io/folders \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /folders`

You can fetch a list of all folders for organizing content by making a GET request to `https://api.intercom.io/folders`.

Requires the `read_articles_scope` or `read_write_articles_scope` OAuth scope.


<h3 id="list-all-folders-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Intercom-Version|header|[intercom_version](#schemaintercom_version)|false|none|
|page|query|integer|false|The page number|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Number of results per page|

## Update a folder

<a id="opIdupdateFolder"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.intercom.io/folders/6 \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "folder": {
      "name": "Updated Product Documentation",
      "emoji": "📖"
    }
  }'
```

`PUT /folders/{id}`

You can update a folder by making a PUT request to `https://api.intercom.io/folders/<id>`.

Fields you leave out keep their current values. Send `parent_folder_id` as `null` to move the folder to the top level. Folder names longer than 191 characters are truncated.

Requires the `read_write_articles_scope` OAuth scope.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "folder": {
    "name": "Updated Product Documentation",
    "emoji": "📖"
  }
}
```

`POST /help_center/collections`

## Update a collection

<a id="opIdupdateCollection"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.intercom.io/help_center/collections/123 \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "Update collection name"
  }'
```

`PUT /help_center/collections/{collection_id}`

You can update the details of a single collection by making a PUT request to `https://api.intercom.io/help_center/collections/<id>`.

`help_center_id` is checked but never applied. It must match the help center of the collection's articles and sub-collections, or the request returns a `400`. A collection with no content rejects any `help_center_id`, so leave it out. Moving a collection to another help center isn't supported.

Requires the `read_write_articles_scope` OAuth scope.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "Update collection name"
}
```

<h3 id="update-a-collection-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Intercom-Version|header|[intercom_version](#schemaintercom_version)|false|none|
|collection_id|path|integer|true|The unique identifier for the collection which is given by Intercom.|
|body|body|[update_collection_request](#schemaupdate_collection_request)|false|none|
|» name|body|string|false|The name of the collection. For multilingual collections, this will be the name of the default language's content.|
|» description|body|string|false|The description of the collection. For multilingual collections, this will be the description of the default language's content.|
|» icon|body|string|false|The icon of the collection, for example `book-bookmark`. If you leave out `icon`, or send it empty, the collection's icon is reset to `folder`.|
|» translated_content|body|[group_translated_content](#schemagroup_translated_content)|false|The Translated Content of an Group. The keys are the locale codes and the values are the translated content of the Group.|
|» parent_id|body|string \| null|false|The id of the parent collection to move the collection into. Omitting this field or sending `null` leaves the collection where it is. Send `home` to move it to the first level.|
|» help_center_id|body|integer \| null|false|Checked against the collection's Help Center but not applied, so it can't move the collection to another Help Center.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|Intercom-Version|1.0|
|Intercom-Version|1.1|
|Intercom-Version|1.2|
|Intercom-Version|1.3|
|Intercom-Version|1.4|
|Intercom-Version|2.0|
|Intercom-Version|2.1|
|Intercom-Version|2.2|
|Intercom-Version|2.3|
|Intercom-Version|2.4|
|Intercom-Version|2.5|
|Intercom-Version|2.6|
|Intercom-Version|2.7|
|Intercom-Version|2.8|
|Intercom-Version|2.9|
|Intercom-Version|2.10|
|Intercom-Version|2.11|
|Intercom-Version|2.12|
|Intercom-Version|2.13|
|Intercom-Version|2.14|
|Intercom-Version|2.15|
|Intercom-Version|2.16|
|Intercom-Version|2.17|

```json
{
  "id": "176",
  "type": "collection",
```

## Create an internal article

<a id="opIdcreateInternalArticle"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.intercom.io/internal_articles \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "title": "Thanks for everything",
    "body": "Body of the Article",
    "owner_id": 991266252,
    "author_id": 991266252,
    "locale": "en"
  }'
```

`POST /internal_articles`

You can create a new internal article by making a POST request to `https://api.intercom.io/internal_articles`.

Requires the `read_write_articles_scope` OAuth scope.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "title": "Thanks for everything",
  "body": "Body of the Article",
  "owner_id": 991266252,
  "author_id": 991266252,
  "locale": "en"
}
```

<h3 id="create-an-internal-article-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Intercom-Version|header|[intercom_version](#schemaintercom_version)|false|none|
|body|body|[create_internal_article_request](#schemacreate_internal_article_request)|false|none|
|» title|body|string|true|The title of the article.|
|» body|body|string|false|The content of the article in HTML. Mutually exclusive with `body_markdown`.|
|» body_markdown|body|string|false|The content of the article in markdown. An alternative to `body` — you can provide content as markdown instead of HTML. Mutually exclusive with `body` and `json_blocks`.|
|» json_blocks|body|[object]|false|The content of the article as a list of content blocks. Used only when `body` is not provided. Cannot be combined with `body_markdown`.|
|» locale|body|string|false|The locale of the article. Defaults to `en`.|
|» author_id|body|integer|true|The id of the author of the article.|
|» owner_id|body|integer|true|The id of the owner of the article.|
|» folder_id|body|integer \| null|false|The ID of the folder to place this article in. Pass `null` to leave it without a folder.|
|» audience_ids|body|[integer]|false|The list of audience IDs to target this internal article to for Fin AI Agent. Pass an empty array or omit the field for no audience targeting. Unknown audience IDs return a `404` error with no partial commit.|
|» ai_chatbot_availability|body|boolean|false|Whether the internal article should be available for AI Chatbot (Fin). Defaults to false.|
|» ai_copilot_availability|body|boolean|false|Whether the internal article should be available for AI Copilot. Defaults to false.|
|» ai_sales_agent_availability|body|boolean|false|Whether the internal article should be available for AI Sales Agent. Defaults to false.|

## Update an internal article

<a id="opIdupdateInternalArticle"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.intercom.io/internal_articles/123 \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "title": "Christmas is here!",
    "body": "<p>New gifts in store for the jolly season</p>"
  }'
```

`PUT /internal_articles/{internal_article_id}`

You can update the details of a single internal article by making a PUT request to `https://api.intercom.io/internal_articles/<id>`.

Fields you leave out keep their current values.

Requires the `read_write_articles_scope` OAuth scope.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "title": "Christmas is here!",
  "body": "<p>New gifts in store for the jolly season</p>"
}
```

<h3 id="update-an-internal-article-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Intercom-Version|header|[intercom_version](#schemaintercom_version)|false|none|
|internal_article_id|path|integer|true|The unique identifier for the internal article which is given by Intercom.|
|body|body|[update_internal_article_request](#schemaupdate_internal_article_request)|false|none|
|» title|body|string|false|The title of the article.|
|» body|body|string|false|The content of the article in HTML. Mutually exclusive with `body_markdown`.|
|» body_markdown|body|string|false|The content of the article in markdown. An alternative to `body` — you can provide content as markdown instead of HTML. Mutually exclusive with `body` and `json_blocks`.|
|» json_blocks|body|[object]|false|The content of the article as a list of content blocks. Used only when `body` is not provided. Cannot be combined with `body_markdown`. If none of `body`, `body_markdown` and `json_blocks` is provided, the existing content is kept.|
|» locale|body|string|false|The locale of the article. If omitted, the existing locale is kept.|
|» author_id|body|integer|false|The id of the author of the article.|
|» owner_id|body|integer|false|The id of the author of the article.|
|» folder_id|body|integer \| null|false|The ID of the folder to place this article in. Pass `null` to remove it from its folder. If omitted, the folder is unchanged.|
|» audience_ids|body|[integer]|false|The list of audience IDs to target this internal article to for Fin AI Agent. Omitting the field leaves existing audience memberships unchanged (PATCH semantics). Pass `[]` to clear all audience memberships. Unknown audience IDs return a `404` error with no partial commit.|
|» ai_chatbot_availability|body|boolean|false|Whether the internal article should be available for AI Chatbot (Fin).|
|» ai_copilot_availability|body|boolean|false|Whether the internal article should be available for AI Copilot.|
|» ai_sales_agent_availability|body|boolean|false|Whether the internal article should be available for AI Sales Agent.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|

<h1 id="intercom-api-ip-allowlist">IP Allowlist</h1>

Manage IP allowlist settings for your workspace.

The IP Allowlist API allows you to configure which IP addresses teammates can use your workspace from, in the web app and mobile apps. This is useful for restricting teammate access to specific corporate networks or VPNs. It doesn't apply to REST API requests, which use a separate REST API allowlist that this API doesn't manage.

{% admonition type="info" name="Authentication" %}
  This endpoint requires the `manage_ip_allowlist` OAuth scope.
{% /admonition %}

```bash
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

## Update IP allowlist settings

<a id="opIdupdateIpAllowlist"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.intercom.io/ip_allowlist \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "enabled": true,
    "ip_allowlist": [
      "192.168.1.0/24",
      "10.0.0.1"
    ]
  }'
```

`PUT /ip_allowlist`

Update the IP allowlist configuration for the workspace.

Both `enabled` and `ip_allowlist` are optional. A field you omit is left unchanged, and a request with neither returns the current settings without changing anything. Sending `null` for a field is the same as omitting it.

Every non-blank `ip_allowlist` entry must be an IPv4 address or an IPv4 range in CIDR notation. Blank entries are ignored and surrounding whitespace is trimmed. Any other entry, including an IPv6 address, returns a 422 `parameter_invalid` error.

When the update leaves the allowlist enabled with at least one entry, the request must come from an IPv4 address that is on the list. A request from an IPv6 address can never match an IPv4 allowlist, so it returns the lockout 422 below.

Requires the `manage_ip_allowlist` OAuth scope.

{% admonition type="warning" name="Lockout Protection" %}
  The API will reject updates that would lock out the caller's IP address. Ensure your current IP is included in the allowlist when enabling the feature.
{% /admonition %}


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "enabled": true,
  "ip_allowlist": [
    "192.168.1.0/24",
    "10.0.0.1"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="update-ip-allowlist-settings-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Intercom-Version|header|[intercom_version](#schemaintercom_version)|false|none|
|body|body|[ip_allowlist](#schemaip_allowlist)|false|none|
|» type|body|string|false|String representing the object's type. Always has the value `ip_allowlist`.|
|» enabled|body|boolean|false|Whether the IP allowlist is enabled for the workspace.|
|» ip_allowlist|body|[string]|false|List of allowed IP addresses and/or IP ranges in CIDR notation.<br>Examples:<br>- Single IP: `192.168.0.1`<br>- IP range: `192.168.0.1/24` (allows 192.168.0.0 - 192.168.0.255)<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|Intercom-Version|1.0|
|Intercom-Version|1.1|
|Intercom-Version|1.2|
|Intercom-Version|1.3|
|Intercom-Version|1.4|
|Intercom-Version|2.0|
|Intercom-Version|2.1|
|Intercom-Version|2.2|
|Intercom-Version|2.3|
|Intercom-Version|2.4|
|Intercom-Version|2.5|

|Intercom-Version|2.14|
|Intercom-Version|2.15|

|Intercom-Version|2.17|

```json
  "type": "ip_allowlist",
  "enabled": true,
  "ip_allowlist": [
    "192.168.1.0/24",
    "10.0.0.1"
  ]
}
```

> 401 Response


<h1 id="intercom-api-macros">Macros</h1>

Operations related to saved replies (macros) in conversations

## Retrieve a macro

<a id="opIdgetMacro"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.intercom.io/macros/123 \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /macros/{id}`

You can fetch a single macro (saved reply) by its ID. The macro will only be returned if it is visible to the authenticated user based on its visibility settings.

**Visibility Rules**

A macro is returned based on its `visible_to` setting:
- `everyone`: Always visible to all team members
- `specific_teams`: Only visible if the authenticated user belongs to one of the teams specified in `visible_to_team_ids`

If a macro exists but is not visible to the authenticated user, a 404 error is returned.

**Placeholder Transformation**

The API transforms Intercom placeholders to a more standard XML-like format in the `body` field:
- From: `{{user.name | fallback: 'there'}}`
- To: `<attribute key="user.name" default="there"/>`

Default values in placeholders are HTML-escaped for security.

## List all macros

<a id="opIdlistMacros"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.intercom.io/macros \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /macros`

You can fetch a list of all macros (saved replies) in your workspace for use in automating responses.

The macros are returned in descending order by updated_at.

**Pagination**

This endpoint uses cursor-based pagination via the `starting_after` parameter. The cursor is a Base64-encoded JSON array containing `[updated_at, id]` of the last item from the previous page.

**Placeholder Transformation**

The API transforms Intercom placeholders to a more standard XML-like format:
- From: `{{user.name | fallback: 'there'}}`
- To: `<attribute key="user.name" default="there"/>`

|Intercom-Version|header|[intercom_version](#schemaintercom_version)|false|none|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of results per page|
|starting_after|query|string|false|Base64-encoded cursor containing [updated_at, id] for pagination|
|updated_since|query|integer(int64)|false|Unix timestamp to filter macros updated after this time|

<h1 id="intercom-api-messages">Messages</h1>

Everything about your messages

## Create a message

<a id="opIdcreateMessage"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.intercom.io/messages \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "from": {
      "type": "user",
      "id": "6762f2341bb69f9f2193bc17"
    },
    "body": "heyy",
    "referer": "https://twitter.com/bob"
  }'
```

`POST /messages`

You can create a message that has been initiated by an admin. The conversation can be either an in-app message, an email or whatsapp.

> 🚧 Sending for visitors
>
> There can be a short delay between when a contact is created and when a contact becomes available to be messaged through the API. A 404 Not Found error will be returned in this case.

This will return the Message model that has been created.

> 🚧 Retrieving Associated Conversations
>
> As this is a message, there will be no conversation present until the contact responds. Once they do, you will have to search for a contact's conversations with the id of the message.

{% admonition type="warning" name="Messages from contacts" %}
`from` should be an admin. A request with a user or lead as `from` is not rejected: it creates a conversation initiated by that contact, as the Create a conversation endpoint (`POST /conversations`) does, and the `to`, `cc` and `bcc` fields are ignored. To create a conversation initiated by a contact, use `POST /conversations`.
{% /admonition %}


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "from": {
    "type": "user",
    "id": "6762f2341bb69f9f2193bc17"
  },
  "body": "heyy",
  "referer": "https://twitter.com/bob"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-message-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Intercom-Version|header|[intercom_version](#schemaintercom_version)|false|none|
|body|body|[create_message_request](#schemacreate_message_request)|false|none|
|» message_type|body|string|false|The kind of message being created. Values: `in_app`, `email` or `whatsapp`.|
|» subject|body|string|false|The title of the email.|
|» body|body|string|false|The content of the message. HTML and plaintext are supported.|
|» template|body|string|false|The style of the outgoing message. Possible values `plain` or `personal`.|
|» from|body|object|false|The sender of the message. If not provided, the default sender will be used.|
|» » type|body|string|true|Always `admin`.|
|» » id|body|integer|true|The identifier for the admin which is given by Intercom.|
|» to|body|[recipient](#schemarecipient) \| [[recipient](#schemarecipient)]|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[recipient](#schemarecipient)|false|A recipient of a message|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[[recipient](#schemarecipient)]|false|The recipients of the message.|
|» cc|body|[recipient](#schemarecipient) \| [[recipient](#schemarecipient)]|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[recipient](#schemarecipient)|false|A recipient of a message|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[[recipient](#schemarecipient)]|false|The CC recipients of the message.|
|» bcc|body|[recipient](#schemarecipient) \| [[recipient](#schemarecipient)]|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[recipient](#schemarecipient)|false|A recipient of a message|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[[recipient](#schemarecipient)]|false|The BCC recipients of the message.|
|» created_at|body|integer|false|The time the message was created. If not provided, the current time will be used.|
|» create_conversation_without_contact_reply|body|boolean|false|Whether a conversation should be opened in the inbox for the message without the contact replying. Defaults to false if not provided.|
|» *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|

## Get statuses of all messages sent based on the specified ruleset_id

`GET /messages/status`

Retrieves statuses of messages sent from the Outbound module. Currently, this API only supports WhatsApp messages.


This endpoint returns paginated status events for WhatsApp messages sent via the Outbound module, providing
information about delivery state and related message details.

## Create a news item

<a id="opIdcreateNewsItem"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.intercom.io/news/news_items \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "title": "Halloween is here!",
    "body": "<p>New costumes in store for this spooky season</p>",
    "labels": [
      "Product",
      "Update",
      "New"
    ],
    "sender_id": 991267834,
    "deliver_silently": true,
    "reactions": [
      "😆",
      "😅"
    ],
    "state": "live",
    "newsfeed_assignments": [
      {
        "newsfeed_id": 53,
        "published_at": 1664638214
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /news/news_items`

You can create a news item

Requires the `read_write_news_scope` OAuth scope.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "title": "Halloween is here!",
  "body": "<p>New costumes in store for this spooky season</p>",
  "labels": [
    "Product",
    "Update",
    "New"
  ],
  "sender_id": 991267834,
  "deliver_silently": true,
  "reactions": [
    "😆",
    "😅"
  ],
  "state": "live",
  "newsfeed_assignments": [
    {
      "newsfeed_id": 53,
      "published_at": 1664638214
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-news-item-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Intercom-Version|header|[intercom_version](#schemaintercom_version)|false|none|
|body|body|[news_item_request](#schemanews_item_request)|false|none|
|» title|body|string|true|The title of the news item.|
|» body|body|string|false|The news item body, which may contain HTML.|
|» sender_id|body|integer|true|The id of the sender of the news item. Must be a teammate on the workspace.|
|» state|body|string|false|News items will not be visible to your users in the assigned newsfeeds until they are set live.|
|» deliver_silently|body|boolean|false|When set to `true`, the news item will appear in the messenger newsfeed without showing a notification badge.|
|» labels|body|[string]|false|Label names displayed to users to categorize the news item.|
|» cover_image_url|body|string(uri)|false|URL of the image to use as the cover. Must contain `.png` or `.jpg` in lower case, so `.jpeg` and `.PNG` are rejected. Intercom copies the image and serves it from its own signed URL.|
|» reactions|body|[string]|false|Ordered list of emoji reactions to the news item. Send an empty list to disable reactions. Send at most five, each a single Unicode code point, so an emoji with a skin tone, a joiner sequence or a variation selector (such as ❤️) is rejected. More than five returns a 400, but the news item is still saved as a draft, with no reactions or cover image.|
|» newsfeed_assignments|body|[[newsfeed_assignment](#schemanewsfeed_assignment)]|false|A list of newsfeed_assignments to assign to the specified newsfeed.|

## Update a news item

<a id="opIdupdateNewsItem"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.intercom.io/news/news_items/123 \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "title": "Christmas is here!",
    "body": "<p>New gifts in store for the jolly season</p>",
    "sender_id": 991267845,
    "reactions": [
      "😝",
      "😂"
    ]
  }'
```

`PUT /news/news_items/{news_item_id}`

You can update a news item.

You can also send this request with `PATCH`; it behaves the same as `PUT`.

`title`, `body`, `state`, `deliver_silently` and `cover_image_url` keep their current values when you leave them out. `labels` and `newsfeed_assignments` do not: leaving either out clears it, so send the full list on every update. Leaving `reactions` out disables reactions, although the list in the response does not change.

Requires the `read_write_news_scope` OAuth scope.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "title": "Christmas is here!",
  "body": "<p>New gifts in store for the jolly season</p>",
  "sender_id": 991267845,
  "reactions": [
    "😝",
    "😂"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="update-a-news-item-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Intercom-Version|header|[intercom_version](#schemaintercom_version)|false|none|
|news_item_id|path|integer|true|The unique identifier for the news item which is given by Intercom.|
|body|body|[update_news_item_request](#schemaupdate_news_item_request)|false|none|
|» title|body|string|false|The title of the news item.|
|» body|body|string|false|The news item body, which may contain HTML.|
|» sender_id|body|integer|true|The id of the sender of the news item. Must be a teammate on the workspace.|
|» state|body|string|false|News items will not be visible to your users in the assigned newsfeeds until they are set live.|
|» deliver_silently|body|boolean|false|When set to `true`, the news item will appear in the messenger newsfeed without showing a notification badge.|
|» labels|body|[string]|false|Label names displayed to users to categorize the news item. Send the full list; the labels you leave out are removed.|
|» cover_image_url|body|string(uri)|false|URL of the image to use as the cover. Must contain `.png` or `.jpg` in lower case, so `.jpeg` and `.PNG` are rejected. Intercom copies the image and serves it from its own signed URL.|
|» reactions|body|[string]|false|Ordered list of emoji reactions to the news item. Send an empty list to disable reactions. Send at most five, each a single Unicode code point, so an emoji with a skin tone, a joiner sequence or a variation selector (such as ❤️) is rejected.|
|» newsfeed_assignments|body|[[newsfeed_assignment](#schemanewsfeed_assignment)]|false|A list of newsfeed_assignments to assign to the specified newsfeed. Send the full list; the assignments you leave out are removed.|
