## Update an office hours exception

<a id="opIdupdateOfficeHoursException"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.intercom.io/office_hours_schedules/123/office_hours_exceptions/456 \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "exception_type": "custom_hours",
    "name": "Christmas Day (reduced hours)",
    "time_intervals": [
      {
        "start_minute": 540,
        "end_minute": 780
      }
    ],
    "recurring_annually": true
  }'
```

`PUT /office_hours_schedules/{office_hours_schedule_id}/office_hours_exceptions/{id}`

You can update an existing office hours exception.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "exception_type": "custom_hours",
  "name": "Christmas Day (reduced hours)",
  "time_intervals": [
    {
      "start_minute": 540,
      "end_minute": 780
    }
  ],
  "recurring_annually": true
}
```

<h3 id="update-an-office-hours-exception-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Intercom-Version|header|[intercom_version](#schemaintercom_version)|false|none|

|id|path|string|true|The unique identifier for the office hours exception.|
|body|body|[update_office_hours_exception_request](#schemaupdate_office_hours_exception_request)|false|none|
|» exception_date|body|string(date)|false|The date the exception applies to, in `YYYY-MM-DD` format. A schedule can have only one exception for each date.|
|» exception_type|body|string|false|The type of exception.|
|» name|body|string|false|An optional name for the exception.|
|» time_intervals|body|[[office_hours_time_interval](#schemaoffice_hours_time_interval)]|false|The open intervals for the exception date. Required for `custom_hours`; omit for `closed`, which returns a 422 error if intervals are sent. `start_minute` and `end_minute` must be on a 15-minute boundary. Don't send `day_of_week`; it is read-only and a request that includes it is rejected with a 400 error.|
|» recurring_annually|body|boolean|false|Whether the exception repeats every year on the same date.|

## Create an office hours exception

<a id="opIdcreateOfficeHoursException"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.intercom.io/office_hours_schedules/123/office_hours_exceptions \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "exception_date": "2026-12-25",
    "exception_type": "closed",
    "name": "Christmas Day",
    "recurring_annually": true
  }'
```

`POST /office_hours_schedules/{office_hours_schedule_id}/office_hours_exceptions`

You can create an exception for an office hours schedule. Use `closed` to mark the day closed (omit `time_intervals`) or `custom_hours` to supply replacement intervals.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "exception_date": "2026-12-25",
  "exception_type": "closed",
  "name": "Christmas Day",
  "recurring_annually": true
}
```

<h3 id="create-an-office-hours-exception-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Intercom-Version|header|[intercom_version](#schemaintercom_version)|false|none|
|office_hours_schedule_id|path|string|true|The unique identifier for the office hours schedule.|
|body|body|[create_office_hours_exception_request](#schemacreate_office_hours_exception_request)|true|none|
|» exception_date|body|string(date)|true|The date the exception applies to, in `YYYY-MM-DD` format. A schedule can have only one exception for each date; a second one returns a 422 error.|
|» exception_type|body|string|true|The type of exception.|
|» name|body|string|false|An optional name for the exception.|
|» time_intervals|body|[[office_hours_time_interval](#schemaoffice_hours_time_interval)]|false|The open intervals for the exception date. Required for `custom_hours`; omit for `closed`, which returns a 422 error if intervals are sent. `start_minute` and `end_minute` must be on a 15-minute boundary. Don't send `day_of_week`; it is read-only and a request that includes it is rejected with a 400 error.|
|» recurring_annually|body|boolean|false|Whether the exception repeats every year on the same date.|

<h1 id="intercom-api-reporting-data-export">Reporting Data Export</h1>

Everything about Reporting Data Export. See this [article](https://www.intercom.com/help/en/articles/12089688-api-metrics-documentation) for details on using the data to generate various metrics.

## Enqueue a new reporting data export job

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.intercom.io/export/reporting_data/enqueue \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "dataset_id": "conversation",
    "attribute_ids": [
      "standard.conversation_id",
      "timestamp.conversation_started_at"
    ],
    "start_time": 1788220800,
    "end_time": 1788307200
  }'
```

`POST /export/reporting_data/enqueue`

For the conversation dataset, from API version 2.16 this export returns all conversations, including those that never received a user reply. Earlier versions return only conversations that received at least one user reply. Other datasets are unaffected.

Requires the `export_reporting_data` OAuth scope.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "dataset_id": "conversation",
  "attribute_ids": [
    "standard.conversation_id",
    "timestamp.conversation_started_at"
  ],
  "start_time": 1788220800,
  "end_time": 1788307200
}
```

<h3 id="enqueue-a-new-reporting-data-export-job-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Intercom-Version|header|[intercom_version](#schemaintercom_version)|false|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» dataset_id|body|string|true|none|
|» attribute_ids|body|[string]|true|List of attribute identifiers to include in the export. Requires qualified_id format (e.g., "people.Brand", "standard.conversation_id"). Use the qualified_id returned from the get_datasets response.|
|» start_time|body|integer(int64)|true|Start of the export period, as a Unix timestamp in seconds. Must be within your workspace's reporting data retention period, which is 2 years by default (3 years for workspaces with extended retention).|
|» end_time|body|integer(int64)|true|End of the export period, as a Unix timestamp in seconds. Must not be earlier than start_time and must also be within the retention period.|

`GET /segments`

Segment names are returned HTML-escaped, for example `&` as `&amp;`.

The counts are added whenever this parameter has a value in the query string, even `false` or an empty one, so omit it entirely to leave them out. A bare `include_count` with no `=` adds no counts. With `type=company`, a company segment gets no count unless a contact segment has the same name, and then it shows that contact segment's count.|

<h1 id="intercom-api-subscription-types">Subscription Types</h1>

## Add subscription to a contact

<a id="opIdattachSubscriptionTypeToContact"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.intercom.io/contacts/63a07ddf05a32042dffac965/subscriptions \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "id": 106,
    "consent_type": "opt_in"
  }'
```

`POST /contacts/{contact_id}/subscriptions`

You can add a specific subscription to a contact. In Intercom, we have two different subscription types based on user consent - opt-out and opt-in:

  1.Attaching a contact to an opt-out subscription type will opt that user out from receiving messages related to that subscription type.

  2.Attaching a contact to an opt-in subscription type will opt that user in to receiving messages related to that subscription type.

This will return a subscription type model for the subscription type that was added to the contact.

Requires the `read_write_users` or `write_users_companies` OAuth scope.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "id": 106,
  "consent_type": "opt_in"
}
```

<h3 id="add-subscription-to-a-contact-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Intercom-Version|header|[intercom_version](#schemaintercom_version)|false|none|
|contact_id|path|string|true|The unique identifier for the contact which is given by Intercom|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» id|body|string|true|The unique identifier for the subscription which is given by Intercom|
|» consent_type|body|string|false|Ignored. Whether the contact is opted in or out is decided by the subscription type's own `consent_type`, not by this value.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Intercom-Version|1.0|
|Intercom-Version|1.1|

|Intercom-Version|2.0|

## Create a phone Switch

<a id="opIdcreatePhoneSwitch"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.intercom.io/phone_call_redirects \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "phone": "+353832345678",
    "custom_attributes": {
      "issue_type": "Billing",
      "priority": "High"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /phone_call_redirects`

You can use the API to deflect phone calls to the Intercom Messenger.
Calling this endpoint will send an SMS with a link to the Messenger to the phone number specified.

If custom attributes are specified, they will be added to the user or lead's custom data attributes.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "phone": "+353832345678",
  "custom_attributes": {
    "issue_type": "Billing",
    "priority": "High"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-phone-switch-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Intercom-Version|header|[intercom_version](#schemaintercom_version)|false|none|
|body|body|[create_phone_switch_request](#schemacreate_phone_switch_request)|false|none|
|» phone|body|string|true|Phone number in E.164 format, that will receive the SMS to continue the conversation in the Messenger.|
|» custom_attributes|body|[custom_attributes_request](#schemacustom_attributes_request)|false|The custom attributes which are set on this object, as key-value pairs. For relationship attributes the value should be a list of custom object instance models. Only attributes a caller may set should be sent here — attributes Intercom generates are returned in responses only.|

#### Enumerated Values

## Create or update a tag, Tag or untag companies, Tag contacts

<a id="opIdcreateTag"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.intercom.io/tags \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "test"
  }'
```

`POST /tags`

You can use this endpoint to perform the following operations:

  **1. Create a new tag:** You can create a new tag by passing in the tag name as specified in "Create or Update Tag Request Payload" described below.

  **2. Update an existing tag:** You can update an existing tag by passing the id of the tag as specified in "Create or Update Tag Request Payload" described below.

  **3. Tag Companies:** You can tag single company or a list of companies. You can tag a company by passing in the tag name and the company details as specified in "Tag Company Request Payload" described below. Also, if the tag doesn't exist then a new one will be created automatically.

  **4. Untag Companies:** You can untag a single company or a list of companies. You can untag a company by passing in the tag id and the company details as specified in "Untag Company Request Payload" described below.

  **5. Tag Multiple Users:** You can tag a list of users. You can tag the users by passing in the tag name and the user details as specified in "Tag Users Request Payload" described below.

Each operation will return a tag object.

Contacts and companies listed in `users` or `companies` that do not exist are skipped: they are left out of the `users` and `companies` arrays in the response and the request still succeeds. With `ids_to_add` it depends on `taggable_type`: a contact id that does not exist returns a 404, while a company id that does not exist is skipped. With `ids_to_add`, the `users` and `companies` arrays in the response are always empty, and a 404 still leaves the tag created or renamed.

Requires the `write_tags` or `write_users_companies` OAuth scope.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "test"
}
```

<h3 id="create-or-update-a-tag-tag-or-untag-companies-tag-contacts-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Intercom-Version|header|[intercom_version](#schemaintercom_version)|false|none|
|body|body|[create_or_update_tag_request](#schemacreate_or_update_tag_request) \| [tag_company_request](#schematag_company_request) \| [untag_company_request](#schemauntag_company_request) \| [tag_multiple_users_request](#schematag_multiple_users_request)|false|none|
|» *anyOf*|body|[create_or_update_tag_request](#schemacreate_or_update_tag_request)|false|You can create or update an existing tag, and optionally apply it to a list of contact or company ids.|
|» *anyOf*|body|[tag_company_request](#schematag_company_request)|false|You can tag a single company or a list of companies.|
|» *anyOf*|body|[untag_company_request](#schemauntag_company_request)|false|You can tag a single company or a list of companies.|
|» *anyOf*|body|[tag_multiple_users_request](#schematag_multiple_users_request)|false|You can tag or untag a list of users.|

## Retrieve team metrics

<a id="opIdgetTeamMetrics"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.intercom.io/teams/42/metrics \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /teams/{team_id}/metrics`

Returns real-time activity metrics for admins in the specified team. For each admin, the response includes counts of open, idle, and snoozed conversations.

This endpoint requires the `realtime_monitoring` feature to be enabled for your workspace.


<h3 id="retrieve-team-metrics-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Intercom-Version|header|[intercom_version](#schemaintercom_version)|false|none|
|team_id|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the team to retrieve metrics for. Use `GET /teams` to list available team IDs.|
|idle_threshold|query|integer|false|The number of seconds after which an open conversation is considered idle. Clamped to the range 1–86400. Defaults to 1800 (30 minutes).|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|Intercom-Version|1.0|
|Intercom-Version|1.1|
|Intercom-Version|1.2|
|Intercom-Version|1.3|

<h1 id="intercom-api-ticket-type-attributes">Ticket Type Attributes</h1>

## Create a new attribute for a ticket type

<a id="opIdcreateTicketTypeAttribute"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.intercom.io/ticket_types/string/attributes \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "Attribute Title",
    "description": "Attribute Description",
    "data_type": "string",
    "required_to_create": false
  }'
```

`POST /ticket_types/{ticket_type_id}/attributes`

You can create a new attribute for a ticket type.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "Attribute Title",
  "description": "Attribute Description",
  "data_type": "string",
  "required_to_create": false
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-new-attribute-for-a-ticket-type-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Intercom-Version|header|[intercom_version](#schemaintercom_version)|false|none|
|ticket_type_id|path|string|true|The unique identifier for the ticket type which is given by Intercom.|
|body|body|[create_ticket_type_attribute_request](#schemacreate_ticket_type_attribute_request)|false|none|
|» name|body|string|true|The name of the ticket type attribute|
|» description|body|string|false|The description of the attribute presented to the teammate or contact|
|» data_type|body|string|true|The data type of the attribute|
|» required_to_create|body|boolean|false|Whether the attribute is required to be filled in when teammates are creating the ticket in Inbox.|
|» required_to_create_for_contacts|body|boolean|false|Whether the attribute is required to be filled in when contacts are creating the ticket in Messenger.|
|» visible_on_create|body|boolean|false|Whether the attribute is visible to teammates when creating a ticket in Inbox.|
|» visible_to_contacts|body|boolean|false|Whether the attribute is visible to contacts when creating a ticket in Messenger.|
|» multiline|body|boolean|false|Whether the attribute allows multiple lines of text (only applicable to string attributes)|
|» list_items|body|string|false|A comma delimited list of items for the attribute value (only applicable to list attributes)|
|» allow_multiple_values|body|boolean|false|Whether the attribute allows multiple files to be attached to it (only applicable to file attributes)|

|» data_type|string|

## Update an existing attribute for a ticket type

<a id="opIdupdateTicketTypeAttribute"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.intercom.io/ticket_types/string/attributes/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "description": "New Attribute Description"
  }'
```

`PUT /ticket_types/{ticket_type_id}/attributes/{attribute_id}`

You can update an existing attribute for a ticket type.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "description": "New Attribute Description"
}
```

<h3 id="update-an-existing-attribute-for-a-ticket-type-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Intercom-Version|header|[intercom_version](#schemaintercom_version)|false|none|
|ticket_type_id|path|string|true|The unique identifier for the ticket type which is given by Intercom.|
|attribute_id|path|string|true|The unique identifier for the ticket type attribute which is given by Intercom.|
|body|body|[update_ticket_type_attribute_request](#schemaupdate_ticket_type_attribute_request)|false|none|
|» name|body|string|false|The name of the ticket type attribute|
|» description|body|string|false|The description of the attribute presented to the teammate or contact|
|» required_to_create|body|boolean|false|Whether the attribute is required to be filled in when teammates are creating the ticket in Inbox.|
|» required_to_create_for_contacts|body|boolean|false|Whether the attribute is required to be filled in when contacts are creating the ticket in Messenger.|
|» visible_on_create|body|boolean|false|Whether the attribute is visible to teammates when creating a ticket in Inbox.|
|» visible_to_contacts|body|boolean|false|Whether the attribute is visible to contacts when creating a ticket in Messenger.|
|» multiline|body|boolean|false|Whether the attribute allows multiple lines of text (only applicable to string attributes)|
|» list_items|body|string|false|A comma delimited list of items for the attribute value (only applicable to list attributes)|
|» allow_multiple_values|body|boolean|false|Whether the attribute allows multiple files to be attached to it (only applicable to file attributes)|
|» archived|body|boolean|false|Whether the attribute should be archived and not shown during creation of the ticket (it will still be present on previously created tickets)|

## Create a ticket type

<a id="opIdcreateTicketType"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.intercom.io/ticket_types \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "Customer Issue",
    "description": "Customer Report Template",
    "icon": "🎟️",
    "category": "Customer"
  }'
```

`POST /ticket_types`

You can create a new ticket type.
> 📘 Creating ticket types.
>
> Every ticket type will be created with two default attributes: _default_title_ and _default_description_.
> For the `icon` propery, use an emoji from [Twemoji Cheatsheet](https://twemoji-cheatsheet.vercel.app/)


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "Customer Issue",
  "description": "Customer Report Template",
  "icon": "🎟️",
  "category": "Customer"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-ticket-type-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Intercom-Version|header|[intercom_version](#schemaintercom_version)|false|none|
|body|body|[create_ticket_type_request](#schemacreate_ticket_type_request)|false|none|
|» name|body|string|true|The name of the ticket type.|
|» description|body|string|false|The description of the ticket type.|
|» category|body|string|true|Category of the Ticket Type.|
|» icon|body|string|false|The icon of the ticket type.|
|» is_internal|body|boolean|false|Whether the tickets associated with this ticket type are intended for internal use only or will be shared with customers. This is currently a limited attribute.|

## Reply to a ticket

<a id="opIdreplyTicket"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.intercom.io/tickets/123/reply \
```

`POST /tickets/{ticket_id}/reply`

## Link a conversation to a ticket

<a id="opIdlinkConversationToTicket"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.intercom.io/tickets/64619700005694/linked_conversations \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "conversation_id": "204"
  }'
```

`POST /tickets/{ticket_id}/linked_conversations`

Link a conversation to an existing tracker ticket. The conversation can be
a regular conversation or one that has been converted into a customer ticket.

Use this when related conversations surface after a tracker ticket has
already been created. The ticket in the path must be a tracker ticket, and
`conversation_id` in the body is the conversation (or customer ticket) to
link to it. This returns the linked conversation.

A tracker ticket can have up to 2,500 linked conversations; once that
limit is reached, further requests return `linked_conversation_limit_exceeded`.

Requires the `write_tickets` OAuth scope.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "conversation_id": "204"
}
```

<h3 id="link-a-conversation-to-a-ticket-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Intercom-Version|header|[intercom_version](#schemaintercom_version)|false|none|
|ticket_id|path|string|true|The unique identifier for the tracker ticket which is given by Intercom.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» conversation_id|body|string|true|The unique identifier (given by Intercom) for the conversation or customer ticket to link to the tracker ticket.|

#### Enumerated Values

|---|---|
|Intercom-Version|1.0|

## Unlink a conversation from a ticket

<a id="opIdunlinkConversationFromTicket"></a>

> Code samples

```bash

  -X DELETE \
```

`DELETE /tickets/{ticket_id}/linked_conversations/{id}`

## Create a ticket

<a id="opIdcreateTicket"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.intercom.io/tickets \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "ticket_type_id": "88",
    "contacts": [
      {
        "id": "6762f2d81bb69f9f2193bc54"
      }
    ],
```

`POST /tickets`

You can create a new ticket.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "ticket_type_id": "88",
  "contacts": [
    {
      "id": "6762f2d81bb69f9f2193bc54"
    }
  ],
  "ticket_attributes": {
    "_default_title_": "example",
    "_default_description_": "there is a problem"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-ticket-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|

|Intercom-Version|header|[intercom_version](#schemaintercom_version)|false|none|

|» » *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» » email|body|string|true|The email you have defined for the contact who is being added as a participant. If a contact with this email does not exist, one will be created.|

## Enqueue create ticket

<a id="opIdenqueueCreateTicket"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.intercom.io/tickets/enqueue \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "ticket_type_id": "88",
    "contacts": [
      {
        "id": "6762f2d81bb69f9f2193bc54"
      }
    ],
    "ticket_attributes": {
      "_default_title_": "example",
      "_default_description_": "there is a problem"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /tickets/enqueue`

Enqueues ticket creation for asynchronous processing, returning if the job was enqueued successfully to be processed. We attempt to perform a best-effort validation on inputs before tasks are enqueued. If the given parameters are incorrect, we won't enqueue the job.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "ticket_type_id": "88",
  "contacts": [
    {
      "id": "6762f2d81bb69f9f2193bc54"
    }
  ],
  "ticket_attributes": {
    "_default_title_": "example",
    "_default_description_": "there is a problem"
  }
}
```

## Update a ticket

<a id="opIdupdateTicket"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.intercom.io/tickets/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "ticket_attributes": {
      "_default_title_": "example",
      "_default_description_": "there is a problem"
    },
    "admin_id": 991268011,
    "assignee_id": "991268013",
    "open": true,
    "snoozed_until": 1673609604,
    "ticket_state_id": "8498"
  }'
```

`PUT /tickets/{ticket_id}`

You can update a ticket.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "ticket_attributes": {
    "_default_title_": "example",
    "_default_description_": "there is a problem"
  },
  "admin_id": 991268011,
  "assignee_id": "991268013",
  "open": true,
  "snoozed_until": 1673609604,
  "ticket_state_id": "8498"
}
```

<h3 id="update-a-ticket-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Intercom-Version|header|[intercom_version](#schemaintercom_version)|false|none|
|ticket_id|path|string|true|The unique identifier for the ticket which is given by Intercom.<br>{% admonition type="info" name="Not the Inbox ticket ID" %}<br>This is the internal `id` field from the API response, not the `ticket_id` displayed in the Intercom Inbox (e.g., #12345). Use the `id` value from the ticket object returned by the API.<br>{% /admonition %}<br>|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» ticket_attributes|body|object|false|The attributes set on the ticket.|
|» ticket_state_id|body|string|false|The ID of the ticket state associated with the ticket type.|
|» company_id|body|string|false|The ID of the company that the ticket is associated with. The unique identifier for the company which is given by Intercom. Set to nil to remove company.|
|» open|body|boolean|false|Specify if a ticket is open. Set to false to close a ticket. Closing a ticket will also unsnooze it.|
|» is_shared|body|boolean|false|Set to `true` to share a ticket with the customer. Only a ticket that isn't shared yet can be shared: a Back-office ticket, of a ticket type that isn't internal, that is linked to a conversation with no other shared linked ticket. Sending `false`, or `true` for a ticket that is already shared (Customer tickets are shared by default) or can't be shared (Tracker tickets), returns a `400`.|
|» snoozed_until|body|integer(timestamp)|false|The time you want the ticket to reopen.|
|» admin_id|body|integer|false|The ID of the admin performing ticket update. Needed for workflows execution and attributing actions to specific admins.|
|» assignee_id|body|string|false|The ID of the admin or team to which the ticket is assigned. Set this 0 to unassign it.|
|» skip_notifications|body|boolean|false|Option to disable notifications when a Ticket is updated.|

## Delete a ticket

<a id="opIddeleteTicket"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.intercom.io/tickets/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /tickets/{ticket_id}`

{% admonition type="warning" name="Irreversible operation" %}
Deleting a ticket is permanent and cannot be reversed.
{% /admonition %}

Deleting a ticket permanently removes it from the inbox. All sensitive data is deleted, including admin and user replies, ticket attributes, uploads, and related content. The ticket will still appear in reporting, though some data may be incomplete due to the deletion.

|ticket_id|path|string|true|The unique identifier for the ticket which is given by Intercom.<br>{% admonition type="info" name="Not the Inbox ticket ID" %}<br>This is the internal `id` field from the API response, not the `ticket_id` displayed in the Intercom Inbox (e.g., #12345). Use the `id` value from the ticket object returned by the API.<br>{% /admonition %}<br>|

## Change ticket type

<a id="opIdchangeTicketType"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.intercom.io/tickets/string/change_type \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "ticket_type_id": "1234",
    "ticket_state_id": "5678"
  }'
```

`POST /tickets/{ticket_id}/change_type`

You can change the type of a ticket. The new ticket type must be in the same category as the current type. Attributes matching by name and type are automatically transferred from the old type; values provided in ticket_attributes override transferred values.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "ticket_type_id": "1234",
  "ticket_state_id": "5678"
}
```

<h3 id="change-ticket-type-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|

|ticket_id|path|string|true|The unique identifier for the ticket which is given by Intercom.|
|body|body|[change_ticket_type_request](#schemachange_ticket_type_request)|false|none|
|» ticket_type_id|body|string|true|The ID of the new ticket type. Must be in the same category as the current type.|
|» ticket_state_id|body|string|true|The ID of the ticket state for the new ticket type.|
|» ticket_attributes|body|object|false|The attributes to set on the ticket for the new type. Attributes matching by name and type are transferred automatically from the old type; values provided here override the transferred values.|

## Search tickets

<a id="opIdsearchTickets"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.intercom.io/tickets/search \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "query": {
      "operator": "AND",
      "value": [
        {
          "field": "created_at",
          "operator": ">",
          "value": "1306054154"
        }
      ]
    },
    "pagination": {
      "per_page": 5
    }
  }'
```

`POST /tickets/search`

You can search for multiple tickets by the value of their attributes in order to fetch exactly which ones you want.

To search for tickets, you send a `POST` request to `https://api.intercom.io/tickets/search`.

This will accept a query object in the body which will define your filters.
{% admonition type="warning" name="Optimizing search queries" %}
  Search queries can be complex, so optimizing them can help the performance of your search.
  Use the `AND` and `OR` operators to combine multiple filters to get the exact results you need and utilize
  pagination to limit the number of results returned. The default is `20` results per page and maximum is `150`.
  See the [pagination section](https://developers.intercom.com/docs/build-an-integration/learn-more/rest-apis/pagination/#example-search-conversations-request) for more details on how to use the `starting_after` param.
{% /admonition %}

### Nesting & Limitations

You can nest these filters in order to get even more granular insights that pinpoint exactly what you need. Example: (1 OR 2) AND (3 OR 4).
There are some limitations to the amount of multiples there can be:
- There's a limit of max 2 nested filters
- There's a limit of max 15 filters for each AND or OR group

### Accepted Fields

Most keys listed as part of the Ticket model are searchable, whether writeable or not. The value you search for has to match the accepted type, otherwise the query will fail (ie. as `created_at` accepts a date, the `value` cannot be a string such as `"foobar"`).
Fields not in the table below, such as `source.body`, are rejected with a `400` error.

| Field                                     | Type                                                                                     |
| :---------------------------------------- | :--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| id                                        | Integer                                                                                  |
| created_at                                | Date (UNIX timestamp)                                                                    |
| updated_at                                | Date (UNIX timestamp)                                                                    |
| title                           | String                                                                                   |
| description                     | String                                                                                   |
| category                                  | String                                                                                   |
| ticket_type_id                            | Integer                                                                                  |
| contact_ids                               | String                                                                                   |
| admin_assignee_id                         | Integer                                                                                  |
| team_assignee_id                          | Integer                                                                                  |
| open                                      | Boolean                                                                                  |
| state                                     | String                                                                                   |
| snoozed_until                             | Date (UNIX timestamp)                                                                    |
| ticket_attribute.{id}                     | String or Boolean or Date (UNIX timestamp) or Float or Integer                           |

{% admonition type="info" name="Searching by Category" %}
When searching for tickets by the **`category`** field, specific terms must be used instead of the category names:
* For **Customer** category tickets, use the term `request`.
* For **Back-office** category tickets, use the term `task`.
* For **Tracker** category tickets, use the term `tracker`.
{% /admonition %}

### Sorting

You can sort the results with a `sort` object, for example `{"field": "created_at", "order": "ascending"}`. `field` must be one of the fields in the table above, other than `ticket_attribute.{id}`, `title` and `description`. `order` is `ascending` or `descending`, and any other value is treated as `descending`. Without `sort`, results are sorted by `updated_at`, newest first.

### Accepted Operators

{% admonition type="info" name="Searching based on `created_at`" %}
  You may use the `<=` or `>=` operators to search by `created_at`.
{% /admonition %}

The table below shows the operators you can use to define how you want to search for the value.  The operator should be put in as a string (`"="`). The operator has to be compatible with the field's type  (eg. you cannot search with `>` for a given string value as it's only compatible for integer's and dates).

| Operator | Valid Types                    | Description                                                  |
| :------- | :----------------------------- | :----------------------------------------------------------- |
| =        | All                            | Equals                                                       |
| !=       | All                            | Doesn't Equal                                                |
| IN       | All                            | In  Shortcut for `OR` queries  Values most be in Array       |
| NIN      | All                            | Not In  Shortcut for `OR !` queries  Values must be in Array |
| >        | Integer  Date (UNIX Timestamp) | Greater (or equal) than                                      |
| <       | Integer  Date (UNIX Timestamp) | Lower (or equal) than                                        |
| ~        | String                         | Contains                                                     |
| !~       | String                         | Doesn't Contain                                              |
| ^        | String                         | Starts With                                                  |
| $        | String                         | Ends With                                                    |


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "query": {
    "operator": "AND",
    "value": [
      {
        "field": "created_at",
        "operator": ">",
        "value": "1306054154"
      }
    ]
  },
  "pagination": {
    "per_page": 5
  }
}
```

## Update a visitor

<a id="opIdupdateVisitor"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.intercom.io/visitors \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "id": "6762f30c1bb69f9f2193bc5e",
    "name": "Gareth Bale"
  }'
```

`PUT /visitors`

Sending a PUT request to `/visitors` will result in an update of an existing Visitor.

**Option 1.** You can update a visitor by passing in the `user_id` of the visitor in the Request body.

**Option 2.** You can update a visitor by passing in the `id` of the visitor in the Request body.

Sending an `email` promotes the visitor to a lead. When that happens the response is a contact object with a `role` of `lead`, not a visitor object.

Requires the `read_write_users` or `write_users_companies` OAuth scope.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "id": "6762f30c1bb69f9f2193bc5e",
  "name": "Gareth Bale"
}
```

|» id|body|string|false|A unique identified for the visitor which is given by Intercom. Used to look the visitor up; it is not changed by this request.|
|» user_id|body|string|false|A unique identified for the visitor which is given by you. Used to look the visitor up; it is not changed by this request.|
|» name|body|string|false|The visitor's name.|
|» email|body|string|false|The visitor's email address. Sending this promotes the visitor to a lead and the response becomes a contact object.|
|» phone|body|string|false|The visitor's phone number.|
|» owner_id|body|integer|false|The id of the teammate who owns the visitor.|
|» last_request_at|body|integer|false|The time the visitor was last seen, as a Unix timestamp.|
|» last_seen_ip|body|string|false|The IP address the visitor was last seen from.|
|» last_seen_user_agent|body|string|false|The user agent the visitor was last seen with.|

## Convert a visitor

<a id="opIdconvertVisitor"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.intercom.io/visitors/convert \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "visitor": {
      "user_id": "3ecf64d0-9ed1-4e9f-88e1-da7d6e6782f3"
    },
    "user": {
      "email": "foo@bar.com"
    },
    "type": "user"
  }'
```

`POST /visitors/convert`

You can merge a Visitor to a Contact of role type `lead` or `user`.

> 📘 What happens upon a visitor being converted?
>
> If the User exists, then the Visitor will be merged into it, the Visitor deleted and the User returned. If the User does not exist, the Visitor will be converted to a User, with the User identifiers replacing it's Visitor identifiers.

Identify the visitor with `visitor.id` or `visitor.user_id`. The `user` object is required when `type` is `user`, and is not read when `type` is `lead`.

Requires the `read_write_users` or `write_users_companies` OAuth scope.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "visitor": {
    "user_id": "3ecf64d0-9ed1-4e9f-88e1-da7d6e6782f3"
  },
  "user": {
    "email": "foo@bar.com"
  },
  "type": "user"
}
```

<h3 id="convert-a-visitor-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Intercom-Version|header|[intercom_version](#schemaintercom_version)|false|none|
|body|body|[convert_visitor_request](#schemaconvert_visitor_request)|false|none|
|» type|body|string|true|Represents the role of the Contact model. Accepts `lead` or `user`.|
|» user|body|object|false|The unique identifiers retained after converting or merging. Required when `type` is `user`; not read when `type` is `lead`.|
|» » id|body|string|false|The unique identifier for the contact which is given by Intercom.|
|» » user_id|body|string|false|A unique identifier for the contact which is given to Intercom, which will be represented as external_id.|
|» » email|body|string|false|The contact's email, retained by default if one is present.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» visitor|body|object|true|The unique identifiers to convert a single Visitor. One of `id` or `user_id` is required; an `email` on its own does not identify a visitor.|
|» » id|body|string|false|The unique identifier for the contact which is given by Intercom.|
|» » user_id|body|string|false|A unique identifier for the contact which is given to Intercom.|
|» » email|body|string|false|The visitor's email.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|

<h1 id="intercom-api-workflows">Workflows</h1>

Everything about your Workflows

## Export a workflow

<a id="opIdexportWorkflow"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.intercom.io/export/workflows/12345 \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /export/workflows/{id}`

Export a workflow configuration by its ID. This endpoint returns the complete workflow definition including its steps, targeting rules, and attributes.

The `id` in the path is the workflow's ruleset ID, the number at the end of the workflow's URL in Intercom (`https://app.intercom.com/a/apps/<app_id>/automation/workflows/<id>`). The `workflow.id` in the response is a different ID, so don't pass it back as `id`.

This endpoint is designed for EU Data Act compliance, allowing customers to export their workflow configurations.


<h3 id="export-a-workflow-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Intercom-Version|header|[intercom_version](#schemaintercom_version)|false|none|
|id|path|string|true|The ruleset ID of the workflow. This is the number at the end of the workflow's URL in Intercom, `https://app.intercom.com/a/apps/<app_id>/automation/workflows/<id>`. It is not the `workflow.id` returned in the response, so don't pass that value back here.|

# Schemas

<h2 id="tocS_office_hours_time_interval">office_hours_time_interval</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaoffice_hours_time_interval"></a>
<a id="schema_office_hours_time_interval"></a>
<a id="tocSoffice_hours_time_interval"></a>
<a id="tocsoffice_hours_time_interval"></a>

```json
{
  "start_minute": 540,
  "end_minute": 1020,
  "day_of_week": 0
}
```

A single open interval. For schedules, `start_minute` and `end_minute` are minute offsets from the start of the week (Monday 00:00 = 0), in the range 0 to 10080. For exceptions, they are minute offsets from midnight on `exception_date`, in the range 0 to 1440.

In requests, `start_minute` and `end_minute` must be multiples of 15. The one exception is a schedule's whole-week interval, `0` to `10079`, which makes the schedule open 24/7. A request interval can contain only `start_minute` and `end_minute`; any other field, including the read-only `day_of_week`, is rejected with a 400 error.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|start_minute|integer|false|none|Minute the interval starts. For schedules, offset from the start of the week (Monday 00:00 = 0); for exceptions, offset from midnight on `exception_date`.|
|end_minute|integer|false|none|Minute the interval ends. For schedules, offset from the start of the week (Monday 00:00 = 0); for exceptions, offset from midnight on `exception_date`.|
|day_of_week|integer|false|read-only|Derived day of the week the interval falls on (0 = Monday … 6 = Sunday). For exceptions, this is derived from `exception_date`. It is returned in responses only; a request that includes it is rejected with a 400 error.|

An exception overrides a schedule's regular hours on a specific date, such as a public holiday.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|type|string|false|none|The type of the object - always `office_hours_exception`.|

|exception_date|string(date)|false|none|The date the exception applies to, in `YYYY-MM-DD` format.|
|exception_type|string|false|none|`closed` means the workspace is closed all day; `custom_hours` replaces the regular hours with `time_intervals`.|
|name|string \| null|false|none|An optional name for the exception.|
|time_intervals|[[office_hours_time_interval](#schemaoffice_hours_time_interval)]|false|none|The open intervals for the exception date. `null` when `exception_type` is `closed`.|
|recurring_annually|boolean|false|none|Whether the exception repeats every year on the same date.|
|created_at|integer|false|none|The time the exception was created as a Unix timestamp.|
|updated_at|integer|false|none|The time the exception was last updated as a Unix timestamp.|

|created_at|integer(date-time)|false|none|The time the activity was created.|
|activity_type|string|false|none|none|
|activity_description|string \| null|false|none|A sentence or two describing the activity. `null` when the admin who performed the activity isn't available.|

Additional data provided about Admin activity.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|sign_in_method|string \| null|false|none|The way the admin signed in.|
|external_id|string \| null|false|none|The unique identifier for the contact which is provided by the Client.|
|away_mode|boolean \| null|false|none|The away mode status which is set to true when away and false when returned.|
|away_status_reason|string \| null|false|none|The reason the Admin is away.|
|reassign_conversations|boolean \| null|false|none|Indicates if conversations should be reassigned while an Admin is away.|
|source|string \| null|false|none|The action that initiated the status change.|
|auto_changed|string \| null|false|none|Indicates if the status was changed automatically or manually.|
|update_by|integer \| null|false|none|The ID of the Admin who initiated the activity.|
|update_by_name|string \| null|false|none|The name of the Admin who initiated the activity.|

|threshold_minutes|integer \| null|false|none|The inactivity window, in minutes, used to classify the Admin.|
|last_activity_at|integer(date-time) \| null|false|none|The time of the Admin's last recorded activity.|
|auto|boolean \| null|false|none|Indicates the state was derived automatically rather than set by an Admin.|
|setting_type|string \| null|false|none|The group of workspace settings the change belongs to, for example `teammate_occupancy` or `automatic_away_mode`.|
|changes|object \| null|false|none|The settings altered by the change, keyed by setting name. Only settings whose value actually moved are included, so an unchanged setting is absent rather than present with equal values.|
|conversation_assignment_limit|integer \| null|false|none|The conversation assignment limit value for an admin.|
|ticket_assignment_limit|integer \| null|false|none|The ticket assignment limit value for an admin.|
|team|object \| null|false|none|Details about the team whose assignment limit was changed.|
|team_assignment_limit|integer \| null|false|none|The team assignment limit value (null if limit was removed).|
|enabled|boolean \| null|false|none|Indicates if the setting is enabled or disabled.|
|mode|string \| null|false|none|The mode of the setting (e.g., when_away_only, when_away_and_reassign).|
|consent_id|integer \| null|false|none|The ID of the impersonation consent.|
|expired_at|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|The timestamp when the impersonation consent expires.|
|before|object \| null|false|none|The state of settings or values before the change. Structure varies by activity type.|
|after|object \| null|false|none|The state of settings or values after the change. Structure varies by activity type.|

```json
  "comparison": "contains",
  "value": "Acme",
  "predicates": [
    {
      "attribute": "company.name",
      "type": "string",
      "comparison": "contains",
      "value": "Acme",
      "predicates": [
        {}
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

A condition used to filter contacts in an audience. An attribute predicate compares one attribute. A logical predicate has a `type` of `and`, `or` or `not` and groups other predicates instead.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|attribute|string|false|none|The attribute to filter on. Required on an attribute predicate.|
|type|string|false|none|The type of the attribute, or `and`, `or` or `not` on a logical predicate.|
|comparison|string|false|none|The comparison operator. Required on an attribute predicate.|
|value|object|false|none|The value to compare against. The accepted value depends on the attribute and the comparison, and can be a string, a number, a boolean, an array or `null`.|
|predicates|[[predicate](#schemapredicate)]|false|none|The predicates grouped by a logical predicate. Only used when `type` is `and`, `or` or `not`.|

The Articles API is a central place to gather all information and take actions on your articles. Articles can live within collections and sections, or alternatively they can stand alone.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|type|string|false|none|The type of object - `article`.|
|id|string|false|none|The unique identifier for the article which is given by Intercom.|
|workspace_id|string|false|none|The id of the workspace which the article belongs to.|
|content_id|string|false|none|The unique identifier for the article's content. For multilingual articles, this will be the identifier of the default language's content.|
|title|string|false|none|The title of the article. For multilingual articles, this will be the title of the default language's content.|
|description|string \| null|false|none|The description of the article. For multilingual articles, this will be the description of the default language's content.|
|body|string \| null|false|none|The body of the article in HTML. For multilingual articles, this will be the body of the default language's content.|
|body_markdown|string \| null|false|none|The body of the article in markdown. For multilingual articles, this will be the body of the default language's content.|
|author_id|integer|false|none|The id of the author of the article. For multilingual articles, this will be the id of the author of the default language's content. Must be a teammate on the help center's workspace.|
|state|string|false|none|Whether the article is `published` or is a `draft`. For multilingual articles, this will be the state of the default language's content.|
|created_at|integer(date-time)|false|none|The time when the article was created. For multilingual articles, this will be the timestamp of creation of the default language's content in seconds.|
|updated_at|integer(date-time)|false|none|The time when the article was last updated. For multilingual articles, this will be the timestamp of last update of the default language's content in seconds.|
|has_unpublished_changes|boolean|false|none|Whether the published article has unpublished changes staged as a draft on top of its live content. For multilingual articles this reflects the default language's content; a pure draft (never published) reports `false`.|
|draft_updated_at|integer(date-time) \| null|false|none|The time, in seconds, when the staged draft was last edited, or `null` when there is no staged draft.|
|url|string \| null|false|none|The URL of the article. For multilingual articles, this will be the URL of the default language's content.|
|parent_ids|[integer]|false|none|The ids of the article's parent collections or sections. An article without this field stands alone.|
|audience_ids|[integer]|false|none|The list of audience IDs this article is targeted to for Fin AI Agent. This field is only returned for single-language help centers. For multilingual help centers it appears per locale inside `translated_content`. Empty array means no audience targeting is set.|
|ai_chatbot_availability|boolean|false|none|Whether the article is available for AI Chatbot. For multilingual articles, this will be the value of the default language's content.|
|ai_copilot_availability|boolean|false|none|Whether the article is available for AI Copilot. For multilingual articles, this will be the value of the default language's content.|
|ai_sales_agent_availability|boolean|false|none|Whether the article is available for AI Sales Agent. For multilingual articles, this will be the value of the default language's content.|
|created_by_id|integer \| null|false|read-only|The ID of the teammate who created the article. For multilingual articles, this will be the creator of the default language's content.|
|updated_by_id|integer \| null|false|read-only|The ID of the teammate who last updated the article. For multilingual articles, this will be the last editor of the default language's content.|
|exclude_from_article_suggestions|boolean|false|read-only|Whether the article is excluded from Fin AI Agent article suggestions.|
|help_center_audience|string \| null|false|read-only|The audience that can view this article in the Help Center. `everyone` means all users and visitors can view it; `restricted` indicates a custom audience ruleset. For multilingual articles, this is the article-level audience.|
|scheduled_publish_at|integer(date-time) \| null|false|read-only|The Unix timestamp (in seconds) at which the article is scheduled to be published. `null` when no publish is scheduled. Mutually exclusive with `scheduled_unpublish_at` — at most one pending schedule exists per article.|
|scheduled_unpublish_at|integer(date-time) \| null|false|read-only|The Unix timestamp (in seconds) at which the article is scheduled to be unpublished. `null` when no unpublish is scheduled. Mutually exclusive with `scheduled_publish_at` — at most one pending schedule exists per article.|
|default_locale|string|false|none|The default locale of the help center. This field is only returned for multilingual help centers.|
|translated_content|[article_translated_content](#schemaarticle_translated_content)|false|none|The Translated Content of an Article. The keys are the locale codes and the values are the translated content of the article.|
|tags|[tags](#schematags)|false|none|A list of tags objects associated with a conversation, article or internal article|
|folder_id|integer \| null|false|none|The ID of the folder this article belongs to, or null if not in a folder.|
|statistics|[article_statistics](#schemaarticle_statistics)|false|none|The statistics of an article.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|article|
|state|published|
|state|draft|
|help_center_audience|everyone|
|help_center_audience|all_users|
|help_center_audience|all_visitors|
|help_center_audience|all_leads|
|help_center_audience|all_visitors_and_leads|
|help_center_audience|restricted|

The Internal Articles API is a central place to gather all information and take actions on your internal articles.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|integer|false|none|The unique identifier for the article which is given by Intercom.|
|title|string|false|none|The title of the article.|
|body|string \| null|false|none|The body of the article in HTML.|
|body_markdown|string \| null|false|none|The body of the article in markdown.|
|owner_id|integer|false|none|The id of the owner of the article.|
|author_id|integer|false|none|The id of the author of the article.|
|created_at|integer(date-time)|false|none|The time when the article was created.|
|updated_at|integer(date-time)|false|none|The time when the article was last updated.|
|locale|string|false|none|The default locale of the article.|
|folder_id|integer \| null|false|none|The ID of the folder this article belongs to, or null if not in a folder.|
|audience_ids|[integer]|false|none|The list of audience IDs this internal article is targeted to for Fin AI Agent. Empty array means no audience targeting is set.|
|ai_chatbot_availability|boolean|false|none|Whether the internal article is available for AI Chatbot (Fin).|
|ai_copilot_availability|boolean|false|none|Whether the internal article is available for AI Copilot.|
|ai_sales_agent_availability|boolean|false|none|Whether the internal article is available for AI Sales Agent.|
|tags|[tags](#schematags)|false|none|A list of tags objects associated with a conversation, article or internal article|

<a id="schemadeleted_folder_object"></a>
<a id="schema_deleted_folder_object"></a>
<a id="tocSdeleted_folder_object"></a>
<a id="tocsdeleted_folder_object"></a>

```json
{
  "id": "6",
  "object": "folder",
  "deleted": true
}
```

Response returned when a folder is deleted

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|false|none|The unique identifier for the deleted folder|
|object|string|false|none|The type of object - `folder`.|
|deleted|boolean|false|none|Whether the folder was successfully deleted.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|object|folder|

This will return a list of articles for the App.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|type|string|false|none|The type of the object - `list`.|
|pages|[pages_link](#schemapages_link)|false|none|The majority of list resources in the API are paginated to allow clients to traverse data over multiple requests.<br><br>Their responses are likely to contain a pages object that hosts pagination links which a client can use to paginate through the data without having to construct a query. The link relations for the pages field are as follows.<br>|
|total_count|integer|false|none|A count of the total number of articles.|
|data|[[article_list_item](#schemaarticle_list_item)]|false|none|An array of Article objects|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|list|


The data returned about your articles when you list them.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|type|string|false|none|The type of object - `article`.|
|id|string|false|none|The unique identifier for the article which is given by Intercom.|
|workspace_id|string|false|none|The id of the workspace which the article belongs to.|
|content_id|string|false|none|The unique identifier for the article's content. For multilingual articles, this will be the identifier of the default language's content.|
|title|string|false|none|The title of the article. For multilingual articles, this will be the title of the default language's content.|
|description|string \| null|false|none|The description of the article. For multilingual articles, this will be the description of the default language's content.|
|body|string \| null|false|none|The body of the article in HTML. For multilingual articles, this will be the body of the default language's content.|
|body_markdown|string \| null|false|none|The body of the article in markdown. For multilingual articles, this will be the body of the default language's content.|
|author_id|integer|false|none|The id of the author of the article. For multilingual articles, this will be the id of the author of the default language's content. Must be a teammate on the help center's workspace.|
|state|string|false|none|Whether the article is `published` or is a `draft`. For multilingual articles, this will be the state of the default language's content.|
|created_at|integer(date-time)|false|none|The time when the article was created. For multilingual articles, this will be the timestamp of creation of the default language's content in seconds.|
|updated_at|integer(date-time)|false|none|The time when the article was last updated. For multilingual articles, this will be the timestamp of last update of the default language's content in seconds.|
|has_unpublished_changes|boolean|false|none|Whether the published article has unpublished changes staged as a draft on top of its live content. For multilingual articles this reflects the default language's content; a pure draft (never published) reports `false`.|
|draft_updated_at|integer(date-time) \| null|false|none|The time, in seconds, when the staged draft was last edited, or `null` when there is no staged draft.|
|url|string \| null|false|none|The URL of the article. For multilingual articles, this will be the URL of the default language's content.|
|parent_ids|[integer]|false|none|The ids of the article's parent collections or sections. An article without this field stands alone.|
|audience_ids|[integer]|false|none|The list of audience IDs this article is targeted to for Fin AI Agent. This field is only returned for single-language help centers. For multilingual help centers it appears per locale inside `translated_content`. Empty array means no audience targeting is set.|
|ai_chatbot_availability|boolean|false|none|Whether the article is available for AI Chatbot. For multilingual articles, this will be the value of the default language's content.|
|ai_copilot_availability|boolean|false|none|Whether the article is available for AI Copilot. For multilingual articles, this will be the value of the default language's content.|
|ai_sales_agent_availability|boolean|false|none|Whether the article is available for AI Sales Agent. For multilingual articles, this will be the value of the default language's content.|
|created_by_id|integer \| null|false|read-only|The ID of the teammate who created the article. For multilingual articles, this will be the creator of the default language's content.|
|updated_by_id|integer \| null|false|read-only|The ID of the teammate who last updated the article. For multilingual articles, this will be the last editor of the default language's content.|
|exclude_from_article_suggestions|boolean|false|read-only|Whether the article is excluded from Fin AI Agent article suggestions.|
|help_center_audience|string \| null|false|read-only|The audience that can view this article in the Help Center. `everyone` means all users and visitors can view it; `restricted` indicates a custom audience ruleset. For multilingual articles, this is the article-level audience.|
|scheduled_publish_at|integer(date-time) \| null|false|read-only|The Unix timestamp (in seconds) at which the article is scheduled to be published. `null` when no publish is scheduled. Mutually exclusive with `scheduled_unpublish_at` — at most one pending schedule exists per article.|
|scheduled_unpublish_at|integer(date-time) \| null|false|read-only|The Unix timestamp (in seconds) at which the article is scheduled to be unpublished. `null` when no unpublish is scheduled. Mutually exclusive with `scheduled_publish_at` — at most one pending schedule exists per article.|
|default_locale|string|false|none|The default locale of the help center. This field is only returned for multilingual help centers.|
|translated_content|[article_translated_content](#schemaarticle_translated_content)|false|none|The Translated Content of an Article. The keys are the locale codes and the values are the translated content of the article.|
|tags|[tags](#schematags)|false|none|A list of tags objects associated with a conversation, article or internal article|
|folder_id|integer \| null|false|none|The ID of the folder this article belongs to, or null if not in a folder.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|

The data returned about your internal articles when you list them.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|integer|false|none|The unique identifier for the article which is given by Intercom.|
|title|string|false|none|The title of the article.|
|body|string \| null|false|none|The body of the article in HTML.|
|body_markdown|string \| null|false|none|The body of the article in markdown.|
|owner_id|integer|false|none|The id of the owner of the article.|
|author_id|integer|false|none|The id of the author of the article.|
|created_at|integer(date-time)|false|none|The time when the article was created.|
|updated_at|integer(date-time)|false|none|The time when the article was last updated.|
|locale|string|false|none|The default locale of the article.|
|folder_id|integer \| null|false|none|The ID of the folder this article belongs to, or null if not in a folder.|
|audience_ids|[integer]|false|none|The list of audience IDs this internal article is targeted to for Fin AI Agent. Empty array means no audience targeting is set.|
|ai_chatbot_availability|boolean|false|none|Whether the internal article is available for AI Chatbot (Fin).|
|ai_copilot_availability|boolean|false|none|Whether the internal article is available for AI Copilot.|
|ai_sales_agent_availability|boolean|false|none|Whether the internal article is available for AI Sales Agent.|
|tags|[tags](#schematags)|false|none|A list of tags objects associated with a conversation, article or internal article|

|highlighted_summary|[[object]]|false|none|An Article description and body text highlighted.|

The results of an Article search

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|type|string|false|none|The type of the object - `list`.|
|total_count|integer|false|none|The total number of Articles matching the search query|
|data|object|false|none|An object containing the results of the search. When no articles match, this is an empty array instead.|
|pages|[pages_link](#schemapages_link)|false|none|The majority of list resources in the API are paginated to allow clients to traverse data over multiple requests.<br><br>Their responses are likely to contain a pages object that hosts pagination links which a client can use to paginate through the data without having to construct a query. The link relations for the pages field are as follows.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|list|

The link relations for the pages field are as follows.<br>|

<h2 id="tocS_article_statistics">article_statistics</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaarticle_statistics"></a>
<a id="schema_article_statistics"></a>
<a id="tocSarticle_statistics"></a>
<a id="tocsarticle_statistics"></a>

```json
{
  "type": "article_statistics",
  "views": 10,
  "conversations": 0,
  "reactions": 10,
  "happy_reaction_percentage": 40,
  "neutral_reaction_percentage": 40,
  "sad_reaction_percentage": 0,
  "fin_involvements": 10,
  "fin_resolutions": 8,
  "fin_resolution_rate": 80
}
```

The statistics of an article.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|type|string|false|none|The type of object - `article_statistics`.|
|views|integer|false|none|The number of total views the article has received.|
|conversations|integer|false|none|The number of conversations started from the article.|
|reactions|integer|false|none|The number of total reactions the article has received.|
|happy_reaction_percentage|number(float)|false|none|The percentage of happy reactions the article has received against other types of reaction.|
|neutral_reaction_percentage|number(float)|false|none|The percentage of neutral reactions the article has received against other types of reaction.|
|sad_reaction_percentage|number(float)|false|none|The percentage of sad reactions the article has received against|
|fin_involvements|integer|false|read-only|The number of conversations in which Fin AI Agent used this article, summed across all of the article's locales.|
|fin_resolutions|integer|false|read-only|The number of conversations Fin AI Agent resolved using this article, summed across all of the article's locales.|
|fin_resolution_rate|number(float)|false|read-only|The percentage of Fin AI Agent involvements that resulted in a resolution (fin_resolutions / fin_involvements * 100).|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|article_statistics|

A historical version of an article, including its content.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|type|string|false|none|String representing the object's type. Always has the value `article_version`.|

|title|string|false|none|The title of the article at this version.|
|description|string \| null|false|none|The description of the article at this version.|
|body|string \| null|false|none|The HTML body of the article at this version.|
|body_markdown|string \| null|false|none|The Markdown body of the article at this version.|
|author_id|string|false|none|The id of the teammate listed as the article's author at this version.|
|created_by_id|string \| null|false|none|The id of the teammate who created this version.|
|created_via|string|false|none|How this version was created (for example `web`, `api`).|
|from_version_id|string \| null|false|none|The id of the version this version was created from, or `null` if this is the first version.|
|state|string|false|none|`published` if this is the version that is currently live; `draft` for every other version, including earlier versions that are no longer live and staged changes that have not been published.|
|created_at|integer(date-time)|false|none|The time the version was created, as a UTC Unix timestamp.|
|updated_at|integer(date-time)|false|none|The time the version was last updated, as a UTC Unix timestamp.|

|state|published|

A banner the contact currently matches, with the content and view identifier needed to display and dismiss it.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|type|string|false|none|String representing the object's type. Always has the value `banner`.|

|show_dismiss_button|boolean|false|none|Whether the banner should display a dismiss control.|
|action|object \| null|false|none|The action a contact can take on the banner, or `null` when the banner has<br>no action. The fields present depend on `type`:<br>`url` (`label`, `target`), `reaction` (`reaction_set`),<br>`email_collector`, or `product_tour` (`tour_id`, `tour_url`).<br>|
|client_targeting|[object]|false|none|Reserved for future use. Always `null` in the current version — banners<br>that depend on client-side targeting rules (such as page URL or time on<br>page) are not returned by this endpoint.<br>|
|created_at|integer(timestamp)|false|none|The time the contact's view of this banner was created.|

|type|string|false|none|The type of object - `collection`.|

|workspace_id|string|false|none|The id of the workspace which the collection belongs to.|
|name|string|false|none|The name of the collection. For multilingual collections, this will be the name of the default language's content.|
|description|string \| null|false|none|The description of the collection. For multilingual help centers, this will be the description of the collection for the default language.|
|created_at|integer(date-time)|false|none|The time when the article was created (seconds). For multilingual articles, this will be the timestamp of creation of the default language's content.|
|updated_at|integer(date-time)|false|none|The time when the article was last updated (seconds). For multilingual articles, this will be the timestamp of last update of the default language's content.|
|url|string \| null|false|none|The URL of the collection. For multilingual help centers, this will be the URL of the collection for the default language.|
|icon|string \| null|false|none|The icon of the collection.|
|order|integer|false|none|The order of the section in relation to others sections within a collection. Values go from `0` upwards. `0` is the default if there's no order.|
|default_locale|string|false|none|The default locale of the help center. This field is only returned for multilingual help centers.|
|translated_content|[group_translated_content](#schemagroup_translated_content)|false|none|The Translated Content of an Group. The keys are the locale codes and the values are the translated content of the Group.|
|parent_id|string \| null|false|none|The id of the parent collection. If `null` then it is the first level collection.|
|help_center_id|integer \| null|false|none|The id of the help center the collection is in.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|collection|

<h2 id="tocS_help_center_redirect">help_center_redirect</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemahelp_center_redirect"></a>
<a id="schema_help_center_redirect"></a>
<a id="tocShelp_center_redirect"></a>
<a id="tocshelp_center_redirect"></a>

```json
{
  "id": "26",
  "type": "help_center_redirect",
  "from_url": "http://help-center.test/lovelyhelpcenter/old-page",
  "locale": "en",
  "help_center_id": "7",
  "target_type": "article",
  "target_id": "11",
  "created_at": 1781619405,
  "updated_at": 1781619405
}
```

A redirect maps a source URL (`from_url`) to an article or collection within a
help center, so that links to old or external URLs resolve to live content.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|false|none|The unique identifier for the redirect.|
|type|string|false|none|The type of the object - `help_center_redirect`.|
|from_url|string|false|none|The source URL that is redirected. This is an absolute URL within the help center's URL space, or a relative path such as `/old-page` for some existing redirects.|
|locale|string|false|none|The locale of the redirect's target. For article targets this is the bound translation's locale, which may differ from the requested locale if no translation exists in that locale.|
|help_center_id|string|false|none|The unique identifier for the help center the redirect belongs to.|
|target_type|string|false|none|The type of the redirect target.|
|target_id|string|false|none|The unique identifier of the target article or collection. For article targets this is the Article ID.|
|created_at|integer|false|none|The time the redirect was created as a UTC Unix timestamp.|
|updated_at|integer|false|none|The time the redirect was last updated as a UTC Unix timestamp.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|help_center_redirect|
|target_type|article|
|target_type|collection|

Companies allow you to represent organizations using your product. Each company will have its own description and be associated with contacts. You can fetch, create, update and list companies.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|type|string|false|none|Value is `company`|
|id|string|false|none|The Intercom defined id representing the company.|
|name|string|false|none|The name of the company. Returned HTML-escaped, for example `&` as `&amp;`.|
|app_id|string|false|none|The Intercom defined code of the workspace the company is associated to.|
|plan|object|false|none|none|
|company_id|string|false|none|The company id you have defined for the company. Returned HTML-escaped, for example `&` as `&amp;`.|
|remote_created_at|integer|false|none|The time the company was created by you.|
|created_at|integer|false|none|The time the company was added in Intercom.|
|updated_at|integer|false|none|The last time the company was updated.|
|last_request_at|integer|false|none|The time the company last recorded making a request.|
|size|integer|false|none|The number of employees in the company.|
|website|string|false|none|The URL for the company website.|
|industry|string|false|none|The industry that the company operates in.|
|monthly_spend|integer|false|none|How much revenue the company generates for your business.|
|session_count|integer|false|none|How many sessions the company has recorded.|
|user_count|integer|false|none|The number of users in the company.|
|custom_attributes|object|false|none|The custom attributes you have set on the company.|
|tags|object|false|none|The list of tags associated with the company|
|segments|object|false|none|Always returned empty. Fetch a company's segments with the list attached segments endpoint.|
|notes|object|false|none|The list of notes associated with the company|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|company|
