Contacts represent your leads and users in Intercom.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|type|string|false|none|The type of object.|
|id|string|false|none|The unique identifier for the contact which is given by Intercom.|
|external_id|string \| null|false|none|The unique identifier for the contact which is provided by the Client.|
|workspace_id|string|false|none|The id of the workspace which the contact belongs to.|
|role|string|false|none|The role of the contact.|
|email|string|false|none|The contact's email.|
|email_domain|string|false|none|The contact's email domain.|
|email_verified|boolean|false|none|Whether the contact has proved they own their current email address. `true` only when this address was marked verified through the Contacts API (`email_verified: true` on create or update) and has not changed since; it becomes `false` again if the contact's email changes, until the new address is verified. Intercom reuses a lead with a verified email when it later matches an inbound email, or an outbound conversation or ticket, to that address, instead of creating a new lead. In List contacts and Search contacts responses it is left out only if the contact can't be loaded, for example when it is deleted while the request runs.|
|phone|string \| null|false|none|The contacts phone.|
|name|string \| null|false|none|The contacts name.|
|owner_id|string \| null|false|none|The id of an admin that has been assigned account ownership of the contact.|
|has_hard_bounced|boolean|false|none|Whether the contact has had an email sent to them hard bounce.|
|marked_email_as_spam|boolean|false|none|Whether the contact has marked an email sent to them as spam.|
|unsubscribed_from_emails|boolean|false|none|Whether the contact is unsubscribed from emails.|
|created_at|integer(date-time)|false|none|(Unix timestamp in seconds) The time when the contact was created.|
|updated_at|integer(date-time)|false|none|(Unix timestamp in seconds) The time when the contact was last updated.|
|signed_up_at|integer(date-time) \| null|false|none|(Unix timestamp in seconds) The time specified for when a contact signed up.|
|last_seen_at|integer(date-time) \| null|false|none|(Unix timestamp in seconds) The time when the contact was last seen (either where the Intercom Messenger was installed or when specified manually).|
|last_replied_at|integer(date-time) \| null|false|none|(Unix timestamp in seconds) The time when the contact last messaged in.|
|last_contacted_at|integer(date-time) \| null|false|none|(Unix timestamp in seconds) The time when the contact was last messaged.|
|last_email_opened_at|integer(date-time) \| null|false|none|(Unix timestamp in seconds) The time when the contact last opened an email.|
|last_email_clicked_at|integer(date-time) \| null|false|none|(Unix timestamp in seconds) The time when the contact last clicked a link in an email.|
|language_override|string \| null|false|none|A preferred language setting for the contact, used by the Intercom Messenger even if their browser settings change.|
|browser|string \| null|false|none|The name of the browser which the contact is using.|
|browser_version|string \| null|false|none|The version of the browser which the contact is using.|
|browser_language|string \| null|false|none|The language set by the browser which the contact is using.|
|os|string \| null|false|none|The operating system which the contact is using.|
|android_app_name|string \| null|false|none|The name of the Android app which the contact is using.|
|android_app_version|string \| null|false|none|The version of the Android app which the contact is using.|
|android_device|string \| null|false|none|The Android device which the contact is using.|
|android_os_version|string \| null|false|none|The version of the Android OS which the contact is using.|
|android_sdk_version|string \| null|false|none|The version of the Android SDK which the contact is using.|
|android_last_seen_at|integer(date-time) \| null|false|none|(Unix timestamp in seconds) The time when the contact was last seen on an Android device.|
|ios_app_name|string \| null|false|none|The name of the iOS app which the contact is using.|
|ios_app_version|string \| null|false|none|The version of the iOS app which the contact is using.|
|ios_device|string \| null|false|none|The iOS device which the contact is using.|
|ios_os_version|string \| null|false|none|The version of iOS which the contact is using.|
|ios_sdk_version|string \| null|false|none|The version of the iOS SDK which the contact is using.|
|ios_last_seen_at|integer(date-time) \| null|false|none|(Unix timestamp in seconds) The last time the contact used the iOS app.|
|custom_attributes|object|false|none|The custom attributes which are set for the contact.|
|avatar|string(uri) \| null|false|none|An image URL containing the avatar of a contact.|
|tags|[contact_tags](#schemacontact_tags)|false|none|An object containing tags meta data about the tags that a contact has. Up to 10 will be displayed here. Use the url to get more.|
|notes|[contact_notes](#schemacontact_notes)|false|none|An object containing notes meta data about the notes that a contact has. Up to 10 will be displayed here. Use the url to get more.|
|companies|[contact_companies](#schemacontact_companies)|false|none|An object with metadata about companies attached to a contact . Up to 10 will be displayed here. Use the url to get more.|
|location|[contact_location](#schemacontact_location)|false|none|An object containing location meta data about a Intercom contact.|
|social_profiles|[contact_social_profiles](#schemacontact_social_profiles)|false|none|An object containing social profiles that a contact has.|
|opted_out_subscription_types|[contact_subscription_types](#schemacontact_subscription_types)|false|none|An object containing Subscription Types meta data about the SubscriptionTypes that a contact has.|
|opted_in_subscription_types|[contact_subscription_types](#schemacontact_subscription_types)|false|none|An object containing Subscription Types meta data about the SubscriptionTypes that a contact has.|
|utm_campaign|string \| null|false|none|The `utm_campaign` value recorded for the contact.|
|utm_content|string \| null|false|none|The `utm_content` value recorded for the contact.|
|utm_medium|string \| null|false|none|The `utm_medium` value recorded for the contact.|
|utm_source|string \| null|false|none|The `utm_source` value recorded for the contact.|
|utm_term|string \| null|false|none|The `utm_term` value recorded for the contact.|
|referrer|string \| null|false|none|The URL of the page the contact came from, as recorded by the Messenger.|
|sms_consent|boolean|false|none|Whether the contact has consented to receive SMS messages.|
|unsubscribed_from_sms|boolean|false|none|Whether the contact is unsubscribed from SMS messages.|
|enabled_push_messaging|boolean \| null|false|none|Whether the contact has a mobile device registered to receive push messages.|
|merge_history|[[merge_history_item](#schemamerge_history_item)]|false|none|A list of contacts that were merged into this contact, most recent first, capped at 10. Only included in the response when `include_merge_history=true` is passed as a query parameter.|

<h2 id="tocS_content_bulk_action_request">content_bulk_action_request</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemacontent_bulk_action_request"></a>
<a id="schema_content_bulk_action_request"></a>
<a id="tocScontent_bulk_action_request"></a>
<a id="tocscontent_bulk_action_request"></a>

```json
{
  "action": "publish",
  "content_ids": [
    {
      "type": "article_content",
      "id": "12345678"
    }
  ],
  "availability": {
    "ai_agent": true,
    "copilot": true,
    "sales_agent": true
  },
  "audience": {
    "add_segment_ids": [
      100
    ],
    "remove_segment_ids": [
      200
    ],
    "remove_all": false
  },
  "tags": {
    "add_tag_ids": [
      100
    ],
    "remove_tag_ids": [
      200
    ]
  }
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|action|string|true|none|The bulk action to perform. Allowed `content_ids[].type` values vary per action:<br>  * `publish`, `unpublish`: `article_content`<br>  * `delete`: `article_content`, `content_snippet`, `file_source_content`, `internal_article`<br>  * `set_availability`, `set_audience`: `article_content`, `content_snippet`, `external_content`, `file_source_content`, `internal_article`<br>  * `update_tags`: `article` (the parent Article id, not `article_content`), `content_snippet`, `external_content`, `file_source_content`, `internal_article`<br>|
|content_ids|[object]|true|none|Up to 1,000 content items to apply the action to.|
|availability|object|false|none|Required when `action` is `set_availability`. Each field is optional — only the<br>properties present in the request are toggled.<br>|
|audience|object|false|none|Required when `action` is `set_audience`. Manages segment membership.|
|tags|object|false|none|Required when `action` is `update_tags`. Applies and/or removes existing tags.<br>Supply at least one of `add_tag_ids` / `remove_tag_ids`. At most 100 distinct tag IDs<br>may be supplied across `add_tag_ids` and `remove_tag_ids` combined. Tag IDs must<br>reference existing, non-archived tags; exceeding the limit or referencing unknown or<br>archived IDs is rejected with `parameter_invalid` (HTTP 422).<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|action|publish|
|action|unpublish|
|action|delete|
|action|set_availability|
|action|set_audience|
|action|update_tags|

<h2 id="tocS_content_snippet_create_request">content_snippet_create_request</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemacontent_snippet_create_request"></a>
<a id="schema_content_snippet_create_request"></a>
<a id="tocScontent_snippet_create_request"></a>
<a id="tocscontent_snippet_create_request"></a>

```json
{
  "title": "How to reset your password",
  "json_blocks": [
    {
      "type": "paragraph",
      "text": "Navigate to Settings > Security > Reset password."
    }
  ],
  "body_markdown": "# Hello\n\nSome content.\n",
  "locale": "en",
  "audience_ids": [
    1,
    2
  ],
  "ai_chatbot_availability": true,
  "ai_copilot_availability": true,
  "ai_sales_agent_availability": true
}
```

The request payload for creating a content snippet. You can provide either `json_blocks` or `body_markdown` for the snippet content — they are mutually exclusive. When `json_blocks` is omitted or `null` and `body_markdown` is omitted or blank, the snippet is created with a single empty paragraph.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|title|string|true|none|The title of the content snippet. The API accepts a missing, `null` or empty title.|
|json_blocks|[object]|false|none|The content blocks that make up the body of the snippet. Mutually exclusive with `body_markdown`.|
|body_markdown|string|false|none|The content of the snippet in markdown. An alternative to `json_blocks` — you can provide content as markdown instead of structured blocks. Mutually exclusive with `json_blocks`.|
|locale|string|false|none|The locale of the content snippet. Defaults to `en`.|
|audience_ids|[integer]|false|none|The list of audience IDs to target this content snippet to for Fin AI Agent. Pass an empty array or omit the field for no audience targeting. Unknown audience IDs return a `404` error with no partial commit.|
|ai_chatbot_availability|boolean|false|none|Whether the content snippet should be available for AI Chatbot (Fin). Defaults to true.|
|ai_copilot_availability|boolean|false|none|Whether the content snippet should be available for AI Copilot. Defaults to true.|
|ai_sales_agent_availability|boolean|false|none|Whether the content snippet should be available for AI Sales Agent. Defaults to true.|

<a id="schemacontent_snippet_update_request"></a>
<a id="schema_content_snippet_update_request"></a>
<a id="tocScontent_snippet_update_request"></a>
<a id="tocscontent_snippet_update_request"></a>

```json
{
  "title": "How to reset your password",
  "json_blocks": [
    {
      "type": "paragraph",
      "text": "Navigate to Settings > Security > Reset password."
    }
  ],
  "body_markdown": "## Updated heading\n\nNew content.\n",
  "locale": "en",
  "audience_ids": [
    1,
    2
  ],
  "ai_chatbot_availability": true,
  "ai_copilot_availability": true,
  "ai_sales_agent_availability": true
}
```

The request payload for updating a content snippet. All fields are optional — only provided fields will be updated. `json_blocks` and `body_markdown` are mutually exclusive.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|title|string|false|none|The title of the content snippet.|
|json_blocks|[object]|false|none|The content blocks that make up the body of the snippet. Mutually exclusive with `body_markdown`.|
|body_markdown|string|false|none|The content of the snippet in markdown. An alternative to `json_blocks` — you can provide content as markdown instead of structured blocks. Mutually exclusive with `json_blocks`.|
|locale|string|false|none|The locale of the content snippet.|
|audience_ids|[integer]|false|none|The list of audience IDs to target this content snippet to for Fin AI Agent. Omitting the field leaves existing audience memberships unchanged (PATCH semantics). Pass `[]` to clear all audience memberships. Unknown audience IDs return a `404` error with no partial commit.|
|ai_chatbot_availability|boolean|false|none|Whether the content snippet should be available for AI Chatbot (Fin).|
|ai_copilot_availability|boolean|false|none|Whether the content snippet should be available for AI Copilot.|
|ai_sales_agent_availability|boolean|false|none|Whether the content snippet should be available for AI Sales Agent.|

<h2 id="tocS_dynamic_content">dynamic_content</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemadynamic_content"></a>
<a id="schema_dynamic_content"></a>
<a id="tocSdynamic_content"></a>
<a id="tocsdynamic_content"></a>

```json
{
  "type": "dynamic_content",
  "id": "123",
  "name": "Support phone number",
  "key": "support-phone-number",
  "content_type": "inline",
  "default_locale": "en",
  "variations": [
    {
      "type": "dynamic_content_variation",
      "id": "456",
      "locale": "en",
      "brand_id": "42",
      "text_content": "+1-555-0100",
      "json_blocks": [
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "You can request a refund within 30 days of purchase."
        }
      ],
      "intentionally_empty": false,
      "created_at": 1663597223,
      "updated_at": 1663597223
    }
  ],
  "created_at": 1663597223,
  "updated_at": 1663597223
}
```

Dynamic content is a reusable piece of content that you can insert into Help Center articles. It holds one variation per locale, and optionally per brand.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|type|string|false|none|String representing the object's type. Always has the value `dynamic_content`.|
|id|string|false|none|The unique identifier for the dynamic content.|
|name|string|false|none|The name of the dynamic content. Returned HTML-escaped, for example `&` as `&amp;`.|
|key|string|false|none|The identifier that articles use to reference the dynamic content. Derived from the name when the dynamic content is created, and never changes.|
|content_type|string|false|none|Whether the dynamic content is a short inline value (`inline`) or one or more blocks of content (`block`).|
|default_locale|string|false|none|The locale whose variation is used when there's no variation for the requested locale.|
|variations|[[dynamic_content_variation](#schemadynamic_content_variation)]|false|none|The variations of the dynamic content.|
|created_at|integer(date-time)|false|none|The time the dynamic content was created as a Unix timestamp.|
|updated_at|integer(date-time)|false|none|The time the dynamic content was last updated as a Unix timestamp.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|content_type|inline|
|content_type|block|

<h2 id="tocS_dynamic_content_variation">dynamic_content_variation</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemadynamic_content_variation"></a>
<a id="schema_dynamic_content_variation"></a>
<a id="tocSdynamic_content_variation"></a>
<a id="tocsdynamic_content_variation"></a>

```json
{
  "type": "dynamic_content_variation",
  "id": "456",
  "locale": "en",
  "brand_id": "42",
  "text_content": "+1-555-0100",
  "json_blocks": [
    {
      "type": "paragraph",
      "text": "You can request a refund within 30 days of purchase."
    }
  ],
  "intentionally_empty": false,
  "created_at": 1663597223,
  "updated_at": 1663597223
}
```

The value of a dynamic content for one locale, and optionally one brand.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|type|string|false|none|String representing the object's type. Always has the value `dynamic_content_variation`.|
|id|string|false|none|The unique identifier for the variation.|
|locale|string|false|none|The locale of the variation.|
|brand_id|string \| null|false|none|The unique identifier for the brand the variation applies to. `null` for a variation that applies to all brands.|
|text_content|string \| null|false|none|The value of an inline variation. `null` for block dynamic content.|
|json_blocks|[object]|false|none|The content blocks of a block variation. `null` for inline dynamic content.|
|intentionally_empty|boolean|false|none|Whether the variation is intentionally empty. An intentionally empty variation shows nothing instead of falling back to the default content, and has an empty `text_content` or `json_blocks`.|
|created_at|integer(date-time)|false|none|The time the variation was created as a Unix timestamp.|
|updated_at|integer(date-time)|false|none|The time the variation was last updated as a Unix timestamp.|

<h2 id="tocS_dynamic_content_variation_request">dynamic_content_variation_request</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemadynamic_content_variation_request"></a>
<a id="schema_dynamic_content_variation_request"></a>
<a id="tocSdynamic_content_variation_request"></a>
<a id="tocsdynamic_content_variation_request"></a>

```json
{
  "locale": "en",
  "brand_id": "42",
  "text_content": "+1-555-0100",
  "body": "<p>You can request a refund within 30 days of purchase.</p>",
  "intentionally_empty": false
}
```

A variation of a dynamic content. Provide `text_content` for inline dynamic content, or `body` for block dynamic content.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|locale|string|true|none|The locale of the variation. Each locale can appear once per brand.|
|brand_id|string \| null|false|none|The unique identifier for the brand the variation applies to. Omit for a variation that applies to all brands.|
|text_content|string|false|none|The value of an inline variation.|
|body|string|false|none|The content of a block variation in HTML.|
|intentionally_empty|boolean|false|none|Set to `true` to make the variation show nothing instead of falling back to the default content. Any `text_content` or `body` sent with it is ignored.|

<h2 id="tocS_dynamic_content_create_request">dynamic_content_create_request</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemadynamic_content_create_request"></a>
<a id="schema_dynamic_content_create_request"></a>
<a id="tocSdynamic_content_create_request"></a>

```json
{
  "name": "Support phone number",
  "content_type": "inline",
  "default_locale": "en",
  "variations": [
    {
      "locale": "en",
      "brand_id": "42",
      "text_content": "+1-555-0100",
      "body": "<p>You can request a refund within 30 days of purchase.</p>",
      "intentionally_empty": false
    }
  ]
}
```

The request payload for creating dynamic content.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|string|true|none|The name of the dynamic content. Must be unique in the workspace.|
|content_type|string|true|none|Whether the dynamic content is a short inline value (`inline`) or one or more blocks of content (`block`). Can't be changed later.|
|default_locale|string|true|none|The locale whose variation is used when there's no variation for the requested locale. `variations` must include a variation for this locale that applies to all brands.|
|variations|[[dynamic_content_variation_request](#schemadynamic_content_variation_request)]|true|none|The variations of the dynamic content, one per locale and optionally per brand. Set `brand_id` on a variation to override the all-brands value for that brand. At least one is required.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|content_type|inline|
|content_type|block|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|name|string|false|none|The name of the dynamic content. Must be unique in the workspace. Renaming doesn't change the `key`.|

|variations|[[dynamic_content_variation_request](#schemadynamic_content_variation_request)]|false|none|The full set of variations. Existing variations that aren't included are deleted.|

The data returned about your conversations when you list or search them.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|type|string|false|none|Always conversation.|
|id|string|false|none|The id representing the conversation.|
|title|string \| null|false|none|The title given to the conversation.|
|created_at|integer(date-time)|false|none|The time the conversation was created.|
|updated_at|integer(date-time)|false|none|The last time the conversation was updated.|
|waiting_since|integer(date-time) \| null|false|none|The last time a Contact responded to an Admin. In other words, the time a customer started waiting for a response. Set to null if last reply is from an Admin.|
|snoozed_until|integer(date-time) \| null|false|none|If set this is the time in the future when this conversation will be marked as open. i.e. it will be in a snoozed state until this time. i.e. it will be in a snoozed state until this time.|
|open|boolean|false|none|Indicates whether a conversation is open (true) or closed (false).|
|state|string|false|none|Can be set to "open", "closed" or "snoozed".|
|read|boolean|false|none|Indicates whether a conversation has been read.|
|priority|string|false|none|The priority level of the conversation. Returns one of none, low, medium, high, or urgent.|
|admin_assignee_id|integer|false|none|The id of the admin assigned to the conversation. If it's not assigned to an admin it will return 0.|
|team_assignee_id|integer|false|none|The id of the team assigned to the conversation. If it's not assigned to a team it will return 0.|
|company|[company](#schemacompany)|false|none|The company associated with the conversation.|
|tags|[tags](#schematags)|false|none|A list of tags objects associated with a conversation, article or internal article|
|conversation_rating|[conversation_rating](#schemaconversation_rating)|false|none|The Conversation Rating object which contains information on the rating and/or remark added by a Contact and the Admin assigned to the conversation.|
|source|[conversation_source](#schemaconversation_source)|false|none|The type of the conversation part that started this conversation. Can be Contact, Admin, Campaign, Automated or Operator initiated.|
|contacts|[conversation_contacts](#schemaconversation_contacts)|false|none|The list of contacts (users or leads) involved in this conversation. This will only contain one customer unless more were added via the group conversation feature.|
|teammates|[conversation_teammates](#schemaconversation_teammates)|false|none|The list of teammates who participated in the conversation (wrote at least one conversation part).|
|custom_attributes|[custom_attributes](#schemacustom_attributes)|false|none|An object containing the custom attributes on a conversation as key-value pairs. For relationship attributes the value is a list of custom object instance models. System-defined attributes such as "AI Topic and Subtopic", "CX Score rating", "CX Score explanation" and "CX Score reasons" may also be included.|
|first_contact_reply|[conversation_first_contact_reply](#schemaconversation_first_contact_reply)|false|none|An object containing information on the first users message. For a contact initiated message this will represent the users original message.|
|sla_applied|[sla_applied](#schemasla_applied)|false|none|The SLA Applied object contains the details for which SLA has been applied to this conversation.<br>Important: if there are any canceled sla_events for the conversation - meaning an SLA has been manually removed from a conversation, the sla_status will always be returned as null.<br>|
|statistics|[conversation_statistics](#schemaconversation_statistics)|false|none|A Statistics object containing all information required for reporting, with timestamps and calculated metrics.|
|linked_objects|[linked_object_list](#schemalinked_object_list)|false|none|An object containing metadata about linked conversations and linked tickets. Up to 1000 can be returned.|
|ai_agent_participated|boolean|false|none|Indicates whether the AI Agent participated in the conversation.|
|ai_agent|[ai_agent](#schemaai_agent)|false|none|Data related to AI Agent involvement in the conversation.|
|sales_agent_participated|boolean|false|none|Indicates whether the Sales Agent participated in the conversation.|
|sales_agent|[sales_agent](#schemasales_agent)|false|none|Data related to Sales Agent involvement in the conversation.|
|channel|object \| null|false|none|The channel through which the conversation was initiated and its current channel.|
|external_references|[[conversation_external_reference](#schemaconversation_external_reference)]|false|none|References linking this conversation to records in an external helpdesk or CRM system. Populated for Fin Standalone workspaces synced from an external platform; an empty array otherwise. Sorted alphabetically by `type` and capped at 20 entries.|
|monitor_evaluations|[[conversation_monitor_evaluation](#schemaconversation_monitor_evaluation)]|false|none|QA monitor evaluations that flagged this conversation. Only included when `include_monitors=true` is passed as a query parameter.|
|scorecards|[[conversation_scorecard](#schemaconversation_scorecard)]|false|none|QA scorecard results for this conversation. Only included when `include_scorecards=true` is passed as a query parameter.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|state|open|
|state|closed|
|state|snoozed|
|priority|none|
|priority|low|
|priority|medium|
|priority|high|
|priority|urgent|

System-defined attributes such as "AI Topic and Subtopic", "CX Score rating", "CX Score explanation" and "CX Score reasons" may also be included.|

|sla_applied|[sla_applied](#schemasla_applied)|false|none|The SLA Applied object contains the details for which SLA has been applied to this conversation.<br>Important: if there are any canceled sla_events for the conversation - meaning an SLA has been manually removed from a conversation, the sla_status will always be returned as null.<br>|
|statistics|[conversation_statistics](#schemaconversation_statistics)|false|none|A Statistics object containing all information required for reporting, with timestamps and calculated metrics.|
|conversation_parts|[conversation_parts](#schemaconversation_parts)|false|none|A list of Conversation Part objects for each part message in the conversation. This is only returned when Retrieving a Conversation, and ignored when Listing all Conversations. There is a limit of 500 parts.|
|linked_objects|[linked_object_list](#schemalinked_object_list)|false|none|An object containing metadata about linked conversations and linked tickets. Up to 1000 can be returned.|
|ai_agent_participated|boolean|false|none|Indicates whether the AI Agent participated in the conversation.|
|ai_agent|[ai_agent](#schemaai_agent)|false|none|Data related to AI Agent involvement in the conversation.|
|sales_agent_participated|boolean|false|none|Indicates whether the Sales Agent participated in the conversation.|
|sales_agent|[sales_agent](#schemasales_agent)|false|none|Data related to Sales Agent involvement in the conversation.|
|channel|object \| null|false|none|The channel through which the conversation was initiated and its current channel.|
|external_references|[[conversation_external_reference](#schemaconversation_external_reference)]|false|none|References linking this conversation to records in an external helpdesk or CRM system. Populated for Fin Standalone workspaces synced from an external platform; an empty array otherwise. Sorted alphabetically by `type` and capped at 20 entries.|
|monitor_evaluations|[[conversation_monitor_evaluation](#schemaconversation_monitor_evaluation)]|false|none|QA monitor evaluations that flagged this conversation. Only included when `include_monitors=true` is passed as a query parameter.|
|scorecards|[[conversation_scorecard](#schemaconversation_scorecard)]|false|none|QA scorecard results for this conversation. Only included when `include_scorecards=true` is passed as a query parameter.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|state|open|
|state|closed|
|state|snoozed|
|priority|none|
|priority|low|
|priority|medium|
|priority|high|
|priority|urgent|

```json
{
```

```json
  "score": 0.85,
  "ai_score": 0.9,
  "evaluated_at": 1719493065,
  "reviewed_teammate": {
    "type": "admin",
    "admin_id": "991267715"
  },
  "reviewer": {
    "type": "admin",
    "admin_id": "884120017"
  },
  "review_status": "submitted",
  "submitted_by": {
    "type": "admin",

  },
  "revised_by": {
    "type": "admin",
    "admin_id": "884120017"
  },
  "notes": [
    {
      "id": "9001",
      "created_at": 1734537900,
      "updated_at": 1734537900,
      "author": {
        "type": "admin",
        "admin_id": "884120017"
      },
      "body": "Great empathy in the second reply."
    }
  ],
  "evaluators": [
    {
      "evaluator_id": "54321",
      "name": "Tone of voice",
      "result": {
        "value": "pass",
        "value_label": "Pass",
        "source": "ai",
        "reasoning": "The agent acknowledged the issue and resolved it within the same response.",
        "reason_ids": [
          "101",
          "102"
        ],
        "reasons": [
          {
            "name": "Clear and concise"
          },
          {
            "name": "Empathetic tone"
          }
        ],
        "other_text": "Agent acknowledged the issue but missed the follow-up question about billing."
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

A QA scorecard result for this conversation. Returned in the `scorecards` array on conversation responses when `include_scorecards=true` is passed.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|scorecard_id|string|false|none|The unique identifier of the scorecard definition.|
|scorecard_version_id|string|false|none|The unique identifier of the specific scorecard version that produced this result.|
|name|string|false|none|The name of the scorecard.|
|scorecard_type|string|false|none|The type of scorecard.|
|passed|boolean \| null|false|none|Whether the conversation passed the scorecard. Null when the scorecard has not been scored.|
|score|number \| null|false|none|The numeric score for the scorecard. Null when the scorecard has not been scored.|
|ai_score|number \| null|false|none|The numeric score produced by AI evaluation, if applicable. Null when not AI-scored.|
|evaluated_at|integer(date-time) \| null|false|none|The time the scorecard was last evaluated. Null in the rare case the underlying record's timestamp is not yet set.|
|reviewed_teammate|[conversation_scorecard_reviewed_teammate](#schemaconversation_scorecard_reviewed_teammate)|false|none|The teammate (or AI agent) whose handling of the conversation was reviewed by this scorecard.|
|reviewer|[conversation_scorecard_reviewer](#schemaconversation_scorecard_reviewer)|false|none|Who the review of this scorecard is assigned to. `ai` when it is assigned to Fin; `admin` when it is assigned to a teammate. Null when no review exists for this scorecard or the review is unassigned.|
|review_status|string \| null|false|none|The status of the review of this scorecard, as shown in the QA reviews list in Intercom. `unreviewed` while the review is waiting for a reviewer's verdict; `submitted` once the review has been submitted; `passed_review`, `needs_fix`, `wont_fix` or `fix_complete` when a teammate set a specific outcome. Null when no review exists for this scorecard.|
|submitted_by|[conversation_scorecard_submitted_by](#schemaconversation_scorecard_submitted_by)|false|none|Who last submitted the review of this scorecard, which can differ from the `reviewer` it is assigned to. `ai` when Fin submitted it; `admin` when a teammate did. Null while the review is unreviewed or when no review exists for this scorecard.|
|revised_by|[conversation_scorecard_revised_by](#schemaconversation_scorecard_revised_by)|false|none|Who last changed the review of this scorecard after it was submitted. `ai` when Fin made the change; `admin` when a teammate did. Null while the review is unreviewed, when it has not been changed since it was submitted, or when no review exists for this scorecard.|
|notes|[[conversation_scorecard_note](#schemaconversation_scorecard_note)]|false|none|The notes teammates left on the QA review linked to this scorecard entry. Empty when the scorecard has no linked review.|
|evaluators|[[conversation_scorecard_evaluator](#schemaconversation_scorecard_evaluator)]|false|none|Per-evaluator results within this scorecard.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|review_status|unreviewed|
|review_status|submitted|
|review_status|passed_review|
|review_status|needs_fix|
|review_status|wont_fix|
|review_status|fix_complete|

Conversations are how you can communicate with users in Intercom. They are created when a contact replies to an outbound message, or when one admin directly sends a message to a single contact.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|type|string|false|none|Always conversation.list|
|conversations|[[conversation_list_item](#schemaconversation_list_item)]|false|none|The list of conversation objects|
|total_count|integer|false|none|A count of the total number of objects.|
|pages|[cursor_pages](#schemacursor_pages)|false|none|Cursor-based pagination is a technique used in the Intercom API to navigate through large amounts of data.<br>A "cursor" or pointer is used to keep track of the current position in the result set, allowing the API to return the data in small chunks or "pages" as needed.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|conversation.list|

A Conversation Part represents a message in the conversation.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|type|string|false|none|Always conversation_part|
|id|string|false|none|The id representing the conversation part.|
|part_type|string|false|none|The type of conversation part.|
|body|string \| null|false|none|The message body, which may contain HTML. For Twitter, this will show a generic message regarding why the body is obscured. In webhook payloads for API version 2.15+, this field returns plain text.|
|created_at|integer(date-time)|false|none|The time the conversation part was created.|
|updated_at|integer(date-time)|false|none|The last time the conversation part was updated.|
|notified_at|integer(date-time)|false|none|The time the user was notified with the conversation part.|
|assigned_to|[reference](#schemareference)|false|none|The assignee this conversation_part assigned the conversation to, as a reference whose `type` is `admin`, `team` or `bot`. When the part unassigned the conversation, `type` is `nobody_admin` and `id` is `null`. Null when the part did not change the assignment, or when the assignee has since been deleted.|
|admin_assignee_id|integer \| null|false|none|The id of the teammate that this conversation_part assigned the conversation to, or 0 if the part removed the teammate. Null or absent when the part did not change the teammate, including an unassignment that did not name which assignee it cleared. A bot is reported here, because assignment treats anything that is not a team as a teammate.|
|team_assignee_id|integer \| null|false|none|The id of the team that this conversation_part assigned the conversation to, or 0 if the part removed the team. Null or absent when the part did not change the team, including an unassignment that did not name which assignee it cleared. A part can assign a team and a teammate at the same time, for example when the team uses Round Robin distribution and the teammate is resolved inline. In that case assigned_to reports only the teammate, and these two fields report each assignee separately.|
|author|[conversation_part_author](#schemaconversation_part_author)|false|none|The object who initiated the conversation, which can be a Contact, Admin or Team. Bots and campaigns send messages on behalf of Admins or Teams. For Twitter, this will be blank.|
|attachments|[[part_attachment](#schemapart_attachment)]|false|none|A list of attachments for the part.|
|external_id|string \| null|false|none|The external id of the conversation part|
|redacted|boolean|false|none|Whether or not the conversation part has been redacted.|
|email_message_metadata|[email_message_metadata](#schemaemail_message_metadata)|false|none|Contains metadata if the message was sent as an email|
|metadata|[conversation_part_metadata](#schemaconversation_part_metadata)|false|none|Metadata for a conversation part|
|state|string|false|none|Indicates the current state of conversation when the conversation part was created.|
|tags|[[tag_basic](#schematag_basic)]|false|none|A list of tags objects associated with the conversation part.|
|event_details|[event_details](#schemaevent_details)|false|none|none|
|app_package_code|string \| null|false|none|The app package code if this part was created via API. null if the part was not created via API.|
|translations|object \| null|false|none|A map of the reply text keyed by locale code. Backs the `conversation.admin.replied.translated` webhook topic. `original` holds the locale code the reply was written in; every other key holds the reply translated into that locale.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|state|open|
|state|closed|
|state|snoozed|

|email|string(email) \| null|false|none|The email of the author. `null` if the author is a contact that has since been archived or deleted.|
|from_ai_agent|boolean|false|none|If this conversation part was sent by the AI Agent|
|is_ai_answer|boolean|false|none|If this conversation part body was generated by the AI Agent|

```json
{
```

```json
  "created_at": 1671028894,
  "updated_at": 1671028894,

    "type": "contact",

  },
  "teammate": {
    "type": "admin",

  }
```

The Conversation Rating object which contains information on the rating and/or remark added by a Contact and the Admin assigned to the conversation.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|rating|integer|false|none|The rating, between 1 and 5, for the conversation.|
|remark|string|false|none|An optional field to add a remark to correspond to the number rating|
|created_at|integer(date-time)|false|none|The time the rating was requested in the conversation being rated.|
|updated_at|integer(date-time)|false|none|The time the rating was last updated.|
|contact|[contact_reference](#schemacontact_reference)|false|none|reference to contact object|
|teammate|object \| null|false|none|The teammate, bot or workflow the rating is attributed to.|

<h2 id="tocS_conversation_source">conversation_source</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaconversation_source"></a>
<a id="schema_conversation_source"></a>
<a id="tocSconversation_source"></a>
<a id="tocsconversation_source"></a>

```json
{
  "type": "email",
  "id": "3",
  "delivered_as": "operator_initiated",
  "recipients": [
    {
      "type": "to",
      "email": "user@example.com",
      "drop_reason": null
    }
  ],
  "reply_to": [
    {
      "email": "replies@example.com",
      "name": "Support Team"
    }
  ],
  "subject": "",
  "body": "<p>Hey there!</p>",
  "author": {
    "type": "admin",
    "id": "274",
    "name": "Jane Doe",
    "email": "jane.doe@example.com"
  },
  "attachments": [
    {
      "type": "upload",
      "name": "example.png",
      "url": "https://picsum.photos/200/300",
      "content_type": "image/png",
      "filesize": 100,
      "width": 100,
      "height": 100
    }
  ],
  "url": null,
  "redacted": false,
  "email_message_metadata": {
    "message_id": "<CADKw7xrXzqSn8v3mP8K8Q8yZ6K8Q8yZ6@mail.gmail.com>",
    "subject": "Question about my order",
    "email_address_headers": [
      {
        "type": "from",
        "email_address": "jdoe@example.com",
        "name": "Joe Example"
      }
    ],
    "history": "<div><span>On Jan 28, wrote:</span><blockquote>Previous thread</blockquote></div>"
  }
}
```

The type of the conversation part that started this conversation. Can be Contact, Admin, Campaign, Automated or Operator initiated.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|type|string|false|none|The origin of this conversation.|
|id|string \| null|false|none|The id of the source message.|
|delivered_as|string|false|none|How the conversation was initiated.|
|recipients|[object]|false|none|The recipients of the source message. Only present for email conversations.|
|reply_to|[object]|false|none|The Reply-To header addresses of the source message, where a reply will be routed. Can differ from the sender's From address. Only present for email conversations.|
|subject|string|false|none|Optional. The message subject. For Twitter, this will show a generic message regarding why the subject is obscured. In webhook payloads for API version 2.15+, this field returns plain text.|
|body|string|false|none|The message body, which may contain HTML. For Twitter, this will show a generic message regarding why the body is obscured. In webhook payloads for API version 2.15+, this field returns plain text.|
|author|[conversation_source_author](#schemaconversation_source_author)|false|none|The author who started the conversation. Can be a Contact, Admin, or Bot.|
|attachments|[[part_attachment](#schemapart_attachment)]|false|none|A list of attachments for the part.|
|url|string \| null|false|none|The URL where the conversation was started. For Twitter, Email, and Bots, this will be blank.|
|redacted|boolean|false|none|Whether or not the source message has been redacted. Only applicable for contact initiated messages.|
|email_message_metadata|[source_email_message_metadata](#schemasource_email_message_metadata)|false|none|Contains metadata if the message was sent as an email|

```json
  "first_close_at": 1663597233,
  "last_assignment_at": 1663597233,
  "last_assignment_admin_reply_at": 1663597233,
  "last_contact_reply_at": 1663597233,

```

A Statistics object containing all information required for reporting, with timestamps and calculated metrics.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|type|string|false|none|none|
|time_to_assignment|integer|false|none|Duration until last assignment before first admin reply. In seconds.|
|time_to_admin_reply|integer|false|none|Duration until first admin reply. Subtracts out of business hours. In seconds.|
|time_to_first_close|integer|false|none|Duration until conversation was closed first time. Subtracts out of business hours. In seconds.|
|time_to_last_close|integer|false|none|Duration until conversation was closed last time. Subtracts out of business hours. In seconds.|
|median_time_to_reply|integer|false|none|Median based on all admin replies after a contact reply. Subtracts out of business hours. In seconds.|
|first_contact_reply_at|integer(date-time)|false|none|Time of first text conversation part from a contact.|
|first_assignment_at|integer(date-time)|false|none|Time of first assignment after first_contact_reply_at.|
|first_admin_reply_at|integer(date-time)|false|none|Time of first admin reply after first_contact_reply_at.|
|first_close_at|integer(date-time)|false|none|Time of first close after first_contact_reply_at.|
|last_assignment_at|integer(date-time)|false|none|Time of last assignment after first_contact_reply_at.|
|last_assignment_admin_reply_at|integer(date-time)|false|none|Time of first admin reply since most recent assignment.|
|last_contact_reply_at|integer(date-time)|false|none|Time of the last conversation part from a contact.|
|last_admin_reply_at|integer(date-time)|false|none|Time of the last conversation part from an admin.|
|last_close_at|integer(date-time)|false|none|Time of the last conversation close.|
|last_closed_by_id|string|false|none|The last admin who closed the conversation. Returns a reference to an Admin object.|
|count_reopens|integer|false|none|Number of reopens after first_contact_reply_at.|
|count_assignments|integer|false|none|Number of assignments after first_contact_reply_at.|
|count_conversation_parts|integer|false|none|Total number of conversation parts.|
|assigned_team_first_response_time|[[conversation_response_time](#schemaconversation_response_time)]|false|none|An array of conversation response time objects|
|assigned_team_first_response_time_in_office_hours|[[conversation_response_time](#schemaconversation_response_time)]|false|none|An array of conversation response time objects within office hours|
|handling_time|integer|false|none|Time from conversation assignment to conversation close in seconds.|
|adjusted_handling_time|integer \| null|false|none|Adjusted handling time for conversation in seconds. This is the active handling time excluding idle periods when teammates are not actively working on the conversation.|

<h2 id="tocS_convert_conversation_to_ticket_request">convert_conversation_to_ticket_request</h2>

<a id="tocsconvert_conversation_to_ticket_request"></a>

```json
{
  "ticket_type_id": "1234",
  "ticket_state_id": "string",
  "attributes": {
    "_default_title_": "Found a bug",
    "_default_description_": "The button is not working"
  }
}
```

You can convert a Conversation to a Ticket

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ticket_type_id|string|true|none|The ID of the type of ticket you want to convert the conversation to|
|ticket_state_id|string|false|none|The ID of the ticket state associated with the ticket type.|
|attributes|[ticket_request_custom_attributes](#schematicket_request_custom_attributes)|false|none|The attributes set on the ticket. When setting the default title and description attributes, the attribute keys that should be used are `_default_title_` and `_default_description_`. When setting ticket type attributes of the list attribute type, the key should be the attribute name and the value of the attribute should be the list item id, obtainable by [listing the ticket type](ref:get_ticket-types). For example, if the ticket type has an attribute called `priority` of type `list`, the key should be `priority` and the value of the attribute should be the guid of the list item (e.g. `de1825a0-0164-4070-8ca6-13e22462fa7e`).|

You can merge a Visitor to a Contact of role type lead or user.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|type|string|true|none|Represents the role of the Contact model. Accepts `lead` or `user`.|
|user|object|false|none|The unique identifiers retained after converting or merging. Required when `type` is `user`; not read when `type` is `lead`.|
|visitor|object|true|none|The unique identifiers to convert a single Visitor. One of `id` or `user_id` is required; an `email` on its own does not identify a visitor.|

<h2 id="tocS_create_audience_request">create_audience_request</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemacreate_audience_request"></a>
<a id="schema_create_audience_request"></a>
<a id="tocScreate_audience_request"></a>
<a id="tocscreate_audience_request"></a>

```json
{
  "name": "VIP Customers",
  "predicates": [
    {
      "attribute": "company.name",
      "type": "string",
      "comparison": "contains",
      "value": "Acme"
    }
  ],
  "role_predicates": [
    {
      "attribute": "role",
      "type": "role",
      "comparison": "in",
      "value": [
        "user_role",
        "contact_role",
        "visitor_role"
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

The request payload for creating an audience.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|string|true|none|The name of the audience.|
|predicates|[[predicate](#schemapredicate)]|false|none|The predicates that define which contacts belong to the audience.|
|role_predicates|[[predicate](#schemapredicate)]|false|none|Role-based predicates that further filter audience membership by contact role. Defaults to all three contact roles when omitted.|

You can create an Article

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|title|string|false|none|The title of the article. For multilingual articles, this will be the title of the default language's content. Required unless a title is provided in `translated_content` under the workspace's default Help Center locale.|
|description|string|false|none|The description of the article. For multilingual articles, this will be the description of the default language's content.|
|body|string|false|none|The content of the article in HTML. For multilingual articles, this will be the body of the default language's content. Mutually exclusive with `body_markdown`.|
|body_markdown|string|false|none|The content of the article in markdown. For multilingual articles, this will be the body of the default language's content. An alternative to `body` — you can provide content as markdown instead of HTML. Mutually exclusive with `body`.|
|author_id|integer|false|none|The id of the author of the article. For multilingual articles, this will be the id of the author of the default language's content. Must be a teammate on the help center's workspace. Required unless an `author_id` is provided in `translated_content` under the workspace's default Help Center locale.|
|state|string|false|none|Whether the article will be `published` or will be a `draft`. Defaults to draft. For multilingual articles, this will be the state of the default language's content.|
|parent_id|integer|false|none|The id of the article's parent collection or section. An article without this field stands alone.|
|parent_ids|[integer]|false|none|The ids of the parent collections to place this article in. Send an empty array to leave the article without a collection. When provided, this takes precedence over `parent_id`.|
|locale|string|false|none|The locale of the article's default content, for example `en`. Defaults to the locale of the help center that the parent collection belongs to when `parent_id` is sent, and otherwise to the default Help Center locale. Must be a locale supported by the workspace's Help Center.|
|translated_content|[article_translated_content](#schemaarticle_translated_content)|false|none|Content for other locales, keyed by locale code. Content for the article's default locale can also be given here instead of at the top level. If it is given in both places, the values must match.|
|folder_id|integer \| null|false|none|The ID of the folder to place this article in, or null to leave it without a folder.|
|audience_ids|[integer]|false|none|The list of audience IDs to assign to this article for Fin AI Agent targeting. Sending a top-level `audience_ids` broadcasts the same set to every locale. For per-locale targeting, use `translated_content.<locale>.audience_ids` instead. Sending both top-level and per-locale in the same request causes top-level to win. Unknown audience IDs return a 404 error. No partial commit occurs.|
|ai_chatbot_availability|boolean|false|none|Whether the article should be available for AI Chatbot (Fin). For multilingual articles, this sets the default language's availability.|
|ai_copilot_availability|boolean|false|none|Whether the article should be available for AI Copilot. For multilingual articles, this sets the default language's availability.|
|ai_sales_agent_availability|boolean|false|none|Whether the article should be available for AI Sales Agent. For multilingual articles, this sets the default language's availability.|
|scheduled_publish_at|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|ISO 8601 timestamp at which to schedule a future publish of the article. When set together with `state: "published"`, the article is scheduled instead of published immediately. Setting `null` cancels a pending publish schedule. Timestamps in the past or equal to the current time are rejected with 400 `parameter_invalid` — the value must be strictly in the future. Combining with `state: "draft"` returns 400 `parameter_invalid`. Sending in the same request as `scheduled_unpublish_at` returns 400 — only one pending schedule per article. Empty string returns 400 `parameter_invalid`.|
|scheduled_unpublish_at|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|ISO 8601 timestamp at which to schedule a future unpublish of the article. The same request must also publish the article (`state: "published"`), otherwise it returns 400 `parameter_invalid`. The value must be strictly in the future; timestamps in the past or equal to the current time are rejected with 400 `parameter_invalid`. Setting `null` cancels a pending unpublish schedule. Sending in the same request as `scheduled_publish_at` returns 400 — only one pending schedule per article. Empty string returns 400 `parameter_invalid`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|state|published|
|state|draft|

You can create an Internal Article

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|title|string|true|none|The title of the article.|
|body|string|false|none|The content of the article in HTML. Mutually exclusive with `body_markdown`.|
|body_markdown|string|false|none|The content of the article in markdown. An alternative to `body` — you can provide content as markdown instead of HTML. Mutually exclusive with `body` and `json_blocks`.|

|author_id|integer|true|none|The id of the author of the article.|
|owner_id|integer|true|none|The id of the owner of the article.|
|folder_id|integer \| null|false|none|The ID of the folder to place this article in. Pass `null` to leave it without a folder.|
|audience_ids|[integer]|false|none|The list of audience IDs to target this internal article to for Fin AI Agent. Pass an empty array or omit the field for no audience targeting. Unknown audience IDs return a `404` error with no partial commit.|
|ai_chatbot_availability|boolean|false|none|Whether the internal article should be available for AI Chatbot (Fin). Defaults to false.|
|ai_copilot_availability|boolean|false|none|Whether the internal article should be available for AI Copilot. Defaults to false.|
|ai_sales_agent_availability|boolean|false|none|Whether the internal article should be available for AI Sales Agent. Defaults to false.|

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

Intercom reuses leads with a verified email when an inbound email, conversation or ticket matches the address.|
|email|string|false|none|The contacts email|
|phone|string \| null|false|none|The contacts phone|
|name|string \| null|false|none|The contacts name|
|avatar|string \| null|false|none|An image URL containing the avatar of a contact|
|signed_up_at|integer(date-time) \| null|false|none|(Unix timestamp in seconds) The time specified for when a contact signed up.|
|last_seen_at|integer(date-time) \| null|false|none|(Unix timestamp in seconds) The time when the contact was last seen (either where the Intercom Messenger was installed or when specified manually).|
|owner_id|string \| null|false|none|The id of an admin that has been assigned account ownership of the contact|
|unsubscribed_from_emails|boolean \| null|false|none|Whether the contact is unsubscribed from emails|
|sms_consent|boolean|false|none|Whether the contact has consented to receive SMS messages.|
|unsubscribed_from_sms|boolean|false|none|Whether the contact is unsubscribed from SMS messages.|
|language_override|string \| null|false|none|A preferred language setting for the contact, used by the Intercom Messenger even if their browser settings change.|
|custom_attributes|object \| null|false|none|The custom attributes which are set for the contact|
|*anyOf*|object|false|none|none|
|*anyOf*|object|false|none|none|
|*anyOf*|object|false|none|none|

<h2 id="tocS_create_conversation_request">create_conversation_request</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemacreate_conversation_request"></a>
<a id="schema_create_conversation_request"></a>
<a id="tocScreate_conversation_request"></a>
<a id="tocscreate_conversation_request"></a>

```json
{
  "from": {
    "type": "user",
    "id": "536e564f316c83104c000020",
    "user_id": "25",
    "email": "joe@example.com"
  },
  "body": "Hello",
  "subject": "Thanks for everything",
  "attachment_urls": [
    "http://example.com"
  ],
  "created_at": 1671028894,
  "brand_id": "123"
}
```

Conversations are how you can communicate with users in Intercom. They are created when a contact replies to an outbound message, or when one admin directly sends a message to a single contact.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|from|object|true|none|none|
|body|string|true|none|The content of the message. HTML is not supported.|
|subject|string|false|none|The title of the email. Only applicable if the message type is email.|
|attachment_urls|[string(uri)]|false|none|A list of image URLs that will be added as attachments. You can include up to 10 URLs.|
|created_at|integer(date-time)|false|none|The time the conversation was created as a UTC Unix timestamp. If not provided, the current time will be used. This field is only recommneded for migrating past conversations from another source into Intercom.|
|brand_id|string|false|none|The unique identifier of the brand to associate with this conversation.|

```json
{
  "user_id": "314159",
  "id": "63a0979a5eeebeaf28dd56ba",
  "email": "frodo.baggins@example.com",
  "event_summaries": [
    {
      "event_name": "invited-friend",
      "count": 1,
      "first": 1671028894,
      "last": 1671028894
    }
  ]
}
```

You can send a list of event summaries for a user. Each event summary should contain the event name, the time the event occurred, and the number of times the event occurred. The event name should be a past tense "verb-noun" combination, to improve readability, for example `updated-plan`.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|user_id|string|false|none|Your identifier for the user.|
|id|string|false|none|The Intercom defined id of the user. Takes precedence over `user_id` and `email`.|
|email|string|false|none|The user's email address. Only used when neither `id` nor `user_id` is supplied.|
|event_summaries|[object]|true|none|A list of event summaries for the user. Each event summary should contain the event name, the time the event occurred, and the number of times the event occurred. The event name should be a past tense 'verb-noun' combination, to improve readability, for example `updated-plan`.|
|*anyOf*|object|false|none|none|
|*anyOf*|object|false|none|none|
|*anyOf*|object|false|none|none|

<h2 id="tocS_create_external_page_request">create_external_page_request</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemacreate_external_page_request"></a>
<a id="schema_create_external_page_request"></a>
<a id="tocScreate_external_page_request"></a>
<a id="tocscreate_external_page_request"></a>

```json
{
  "title": "Getting started with...",
  "html": "<p>Hello world!</p>",
  "url": "https://help.example.com/en/articles/1234-getting-started",
  "ai_agent_availability": true,
  "ai_copilot_availability": true,
  "ai_sales_agent_availability": true,
  "locale": "en",
  "source_id": 1234,
  "external_id": "5678",
  "audience_ids": [
    1,
    2
  ]
}
```

You can add an External Page to your Fin Content Library.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|title|string|true|none|The title of the external page.|
|html|string|true|none|The body of the external page in HTML.|
|url|string|false|none|The URL of the external page. This will be used by Fin to link end users to the page it based its answer on. When a URL is not present, Fin will not reference the source.|
|ai_agent_availability|boolean|false|none|Whether the external page should be used to answer questions by AI Agent. Will not default when updating an existing external page.|
|ai_copilot_availability|boolean|false|none|Whether the external page should be used to answer questions by AI Copilot. Will not default when updating an existing external page.|
|ai_sales_agent_availability|boolean|false|none|Whether the external page should be used to answer questions by AI Sales Agent. Will not default when updating an existing external page.|
|locale|string|true|none|The language code of the external page, for example `en` or `fr`. It must be a language supported by the workspace.|
|source_id|integer|true|none|The unique identifier for the source of the external page which was given by Intercom. Every external page must be associated with a Content Import Source which represents the place it comes from and from which it inherits a default audience (configured in the UI). For a new source, make a POST request to the Content Import Source endpoint and an ID for the source will be returned in the response.|
|external_id|string|true|none|The identifier for the external page which was given by the source. Must be unique for the source.|
|audience_ids|[integer]|false|none|The list of audience IDs to target this external page to for Fin AI Agent. Omitting the field keeps the default audience inherited from the source. Pass `[]` to clear all audience memberships, including the inherited ones. If an external page already exists with the specified source_id and external_id, omitting the field leaves its audience memberships unchanged. Unknown audience IDs return a `404` error.|

```json
{

  },

    "type": "user",

  },
  "cc": {
    "type": "user",
    "id": "536e564f316c83104c000020"
  },
  "bcc": {
    "type": "user",
    "id": "536e564f316c83104c000020"
  },
```

You can create a message

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|message_type|string|false|none|The kind of message being created. Values: `in_app`, `email` or `whatsapp`.|
|subject|string|false|none|The title of the email.|
|body|string|false|none|The content of the message. HTML and plaintext are supported.|
|template|string|false|none|The style of the outgoing message. Possible values `plain` or `personal`.|
|from|object|false|none|The sender of the message. If not provided, the default sender will be used.|
|to|[recipient](#schemarecipient) \| [[recipient](#schemarecipient)]|false|none|none|
|cc|[recipient](#schemarecipient) \| [[recipient](#schemarecipient)]|false|none|none|
|bcc|[recipient](#schemarecipient) \| [[recipient](#schemarecipient)]|false|none|none|
|created_at|integer|false|none|The time the message was created. If not provided, the current time will be used.|
|create_conversation_without_contact_reply|boolean|false|none|Whether a conversation should be opened in the inbox for the message without the contact replying. Defaults to false if not provided.|
|*anyOf*|object|false|none|none|
|*anyOf*|object|false|none|none|
|*anyOf*|object|false|none|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|message_type|in_app|
|message_type|email|
|message_type|whatsapp|

<h2 id="tocS_create_or_update_company_request">create_or_update_company_request</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemacreate_or_update_company_request"></a>
<a id="schema_create_or_update_company_request"></a>
<a id="tocScreate_or_update_company_request"></a>
<a id="tocscreate_or_update_company_request"></a>

```json
{
  "name": "Intercom",
  "company_id": "625e90fc55ab113b6d92175f",
  "id": "625e90fc55ab113b6d92175f",
  "plan": "Enterprise",
  "size": 100,
  "website": "https://www.example.com",
  "industry": "Manufacturing",
  "custom_attributes": {
    "paid_subscriber": true,
    "monthly_spend": 155.5,
    "team_mates": 9
  },
  "remote_created_at": 1394531169,
  "update_last_request_at": true,
  "monthly_spend": 1000
}
```

You can create or update a Company. Send either `company_id` or `id`; a request with neither returns a `400` error.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|string|false|none|The name of the Company. Leading and trailing whitespace is removed.|
|company_id|string|false|none|The company id you have defined for the company. Can't be updated|
|id|string|false|none|An alternative name for `company_id`. Supply this or `company_id`.|
|plan|string|false|none|The name of the plan you have associated with the company.|
|size|integer|false|none|The number of employees in this company.|
|website|string|false|none|The URL for this company's website. Please note that the value specified here is not validated. Accepts any string.|
|industry|string|false|none|The industry that this company operates in.|
|custom_attributes|object|false|none|Values for custom attributes that already exist in your workspace. Each value can be a string, integer, number, boolean or null. Arrays and objects aren't accepted.|
|remote_created_at|integer|false|none|The time the company was created by you.|
|update_last_request_at|boolean|false|none|Set to true to update the company's last seen time to now.|
|monthly_spend|integer|false|none|How much revenue the company generates for your business. Floats are truncated to whole integers, so 155.98 is stored as 155. A value above 2147483647 (2**31-1) is stored as 0. 2147483647 itself, or a value of -2147483648 or below, returns a `422` error.|

<h2 id="tocS_create_or_update_custom_object_instance_request">create_or_update_custom_object_instance_request</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemacreate_or_update_custom_object_instance_request"></a>
<a id="schema_create_or_update_custom_object_instance_request"></a>
<a id="tocScreate_or_update_custom_object_instance_request"></a>
<a id="tocscreate_or_update_custom_object_instance_request"></a>

```json
{
  "external_id": "string",
  "external_created_at": 1571672154,
  "external_updated_at": 1571672154,
  "custom_attributes": {
    "order_number": "ORDER-12345",
    "total_amount": 99.99
  }
}
```

Payload to create or update a Custom Object instance

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|external_id|string|false|none|A unique identifier for the Custom Object instance in the external system it originated from. The value `reference_not_found` is reserved and is rejected with a `400`. Omitting this field creates a new instance on every request instead of updating an existing one.|
|external_created_at|integer(date-time) \| null|false|none|The time when the Custom Object instance was created in the external system it originated from. A value that cannot be read as a time is stored as `null` rather than rejected.|
|external_updated_at|integer(date-time) \| null|false|none|The time when the Custom Object instance was last updated in the external system it originated from. A value that cannot be read as a time is stored as `null` rather than rejected.|
|custom_attributes|object \| null|false|none|The custom attributes which are set for the Custom Object instance.<br><br>Each value must match the type of the attribute it is set on: a string, integer, number or boolean, a Unix timestamp or date string for a datetime attribute, or `null` to clear the attribute. A list attribute takes the label or id of one of its options; a value that matches no option clears the attribute rather than being rejected. A reference attribute takes the Intercom id of the record it points at, or an array of ids for a reference to several records; an id that matches no record is skipped.|

<h2 id="tocS_create_or_update_tag_request">create_or_update_tag_request</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemacreate_or_update_tag_request"></a>
<a id="schema_create_or_update_tag_request"></a>
<a id="tocScreate_or_update_tag_request"></a>
<a id="tocscreate_or_update_tag_request"></a>

```json
{
  "name": "Independent",
  "id": "656452352",
  "ids_to_add": [
    "536e564f316c83104c000020"
  ],
  "taggable_type": "user"
}
```

You can create or update an existing tag, and optionally apply it to a list of contact or company ids.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|string|true|none|The name of the tag, which will be created if not found, or the new name for the tag if this is an update request. Names are case insensitive and can be at most 191 characters long. Creating a tag with a longer name returns a 400. When updating by `id`, a longer name or one that another tag already has returns 200 with the new name, but the tag keeps its old name.|
|id|string|false|none|The id of tag to updates.|
|ids_to_add|[string]|false|none|The Intercom ids of the contacts or companies to apply the tag to. A contact id that does not exist returns a 404; a company id that does not exist is skipped. A 404 still leaves the tag created or renamed. The `users` and `companies` arrays in the response are always empty when this field is used.|
|taggable_type|string|false|none|Whether the ids in `ids_to_add` are contacts or companies. Defaults to `user`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|taggable_type|user|
|taggable_type|company|

```json
{
  "ticket_type_id": "1234",

    {
      "id": "1234"
    }
  ],
  "conversation_to_link_id": "1234",
  "company_id": "5f4d3c1c-7b1b-4d7d-a97e-6095715c6632",
  "created_at": 1590000000,
  "ticket_attributes": {
    "_default_title_": "Found a bug",
    "_default_description_": "The button is not working"
  },
  "assignment": {
    "admin_assignee_id": "123",
    "team_assignee_id": "8"
  },
  "channel": "email"
}
```

You can create a Ticket

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ticket_type_id|string|true|none|The ID of the type of ticket you want to create|
|contacts|[object]|false|none|The list of contacts (users or leads) affected by this ticket. Currently only one is allowed. Required for Customer and Back-office ticket types, and optional for Tracker ticket types.|
|conversation_to_link_id|string|false|none|The ID of the conversation you want to link to the ticket. Here are the valid ways of linking two tickets:<br> - conversation \| back-office ticket<br> - customer tickets \| non-shared back-office ticket<br> - conversation \| tracker ticket<br> - customer ticket \| tracker ticket|
|company_id|string|false|none|The ID of the company that the ticket is associated with. The unique identifier for the company which is given by Intercom|
|created_at|integer|false|none|The time the ticket was created. If not provided, the current time will be used.|
|ticket_attributes|[ticket_request_custom_attributes](#schematicket_request_custom_attributes)|false|none|The attributes set on the ticket. When setting the default title and description attributes, the attribute keys that should be used are `_default_title_` and `_default_description_`. When setting ticket type attributes of the list attribute type, the key should be the attribute name and the value of the attribute should be the list item id, obtainable by [listing the ticket type](ref:get_ticket-types). For example, if the ticket type has an attribute called `priority` of type `list`, the key should be `priority` and the value of the attribute should be the guid of the list item (e.g. `de1825a0-0164-4070-8ca6-13e22462fa7e`).|
|assignment|object|false|none|none|
|channel|string|false|none|The channel for the ticket. Only supported for customer ticket types. Defaults to messenger if not provided.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|channel|email|

<h2 id="tocS_cursor_pages">cursor_pages</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemacursor_pages"></a>
<a id="schema_cursor_pages"></a>
<a id="tocScursor_pages"></a>
<a id="tocscursor_pages"></a>

```json
{
  "type": "pages",
  "page": 1,
  "next": {
    "page": 2,
    "starting_after": "your-cursor-from-response"
  },
  "per_page": 2,
  "total_pages": 13
}
```

Cursor-based pagination is a technique used in the Intercom API to navigate through large amounts of data.
A "cursor" or pointer is used to keep track of the current position in the result set, allowing the API to return the data in small chunks or "pages" as needed.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|type|string|false|none|the type of object `pages`.|
|page|integer|false|none|The current page|
|next|object \| null|false|none|Fetch the next page by sending this `starting_after` cursor. Omitted on the last page.|
|per_page|integer|false|none|Number of results per page|
|total_pages|integer|false|none|Total number of pages|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|pages|

### Properties

|answered_at|[datetime](#schemadatetime)|false|none|none|
|ended_at|[datetime](#schemadatetime)|false|none|none|

|updated_at|[datetime](#schemadatetime)|false|none|none|
|recording_url|string(uri) \| null|false|none|API URL to download or redirect to the call recording if available.|
|transcription_url|string(uri) \| null|false|none|API URL to download or redirect to the call transcript if available.|
|call_type|string|false|none|The type of call.|
|direction|string|false|none|The direction of the call.|
|ended_reason|string \| null|false|none|The reason for the call end, if applicable.|

|fin_transcription_url|string(uri) \| null|false|none|API URL to the AI Agent (Fin) call transcript if available.|

|CX Score reasons|[[cx_score_reason](#schemacx_score_reason)]|false|read-only|Read-only reasons behind the conversation's CX Score. Intercom generates this attribute, so it cannot be set. Omitted when the conversation has no CX Score reasons.|
|**additionalProperties**|string \| integer \| number \| boolean \| [datetime](#schemadatetime) \| [custom_object_instance_list](#schemacustom_object_instance_list)|false|none|none|

```json
  "external_created_at": 1571672154,

  "created_at": 1671028894,
  "updated_at": 1671028894,
  "type": "Order",
  "custom_attributes": {
    "order_number": "ORDER-12345",
    "total_amount": 99.99
  }
}
```

A Custom Object Instance represents an instance of a custom object type. This allows you to create and set custom attributes to store data about your customers that is not already captured by Intercom. The parent object includes recommended default attributes and you can add your own custom attributes.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|false|none|The Intercom defined id representing the custom object instance.|
|external_id|string|false|none|The id you have defined for the custom object instance.|
|external_created_at|integer(date-time) \| null|false|none|The time when the Custom Object instance was created in the external system it originated from.|
|external_updated_at|integer(date-time) \| null|false|none|The time when the Custom Object instance was last updated in the external system it originated from.|
|created_at|integer(date-time)|false|none|The time the attribute was created as a UTC Unix timestamp|
|updated_at|integer(date-time)|false|none|The time the attribute was last updated as a UTC Unix timestamp|
|type|string|false|none|The identifier of the custom object type that defines the structure of the custom object instance.|
|custom_attributes|object|false|none|The custom attributes you have set on the custom object instance.<br><br>Each value is returned with the type of the attribute it is set on: a string, integer, number or boolean, or `null` when the attribute is unset. A list attribute returns the label of the selected option. A reference attribute returns an object holding the referenced records, under `contacts` for a contact reference, `conversations` for a conversation reference, or `instances` for a reference to another custom object type.|

|archived|boolean|false|none|Is this attribute archived. (Only applicable to CDAs)|

|updated_at|integer(date-time)|false|none|The time the attribute was last updated as a UTC Unix timestamp|
