<h2 id="tocS_create_data_connector_request">create_data_connector_request</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemacreate_data_connector_request"></a>
<a id="schema_create_data_connector_request"></a>
<a id="tocScreate_data_connector_request"></a>
<a id="tocscreate_data_connector_request"></a>

```json
{
  "name": "Get Order Status",
  "description": "Looks up order status from an external service",
  "internal_description": "string",
  "http_method": "get",
  "url": "https://api.example.com/orders/{{order_id}}/status",
  "body": "string",
  "direct_fin_usage": false,
  "audiences": [
    "leads",
    "visitors"
  ],
  "headers": [
    {
      "name": "Content-Type",
      "value": "application/json"
    }
  ],
  "data_inputs": [
    {
      "name": "order_id",
      "type": "string",
      "description": "The order ID to look up",
      "required": true,
      "default_value": "string"
    }
  ],
  "customer_authentication": false,
  "bypass_authentication": false,
  "enforce_auth": true,
  "validate_missing_attributes": false,
  "mock_response": {
    "order": {
      "id": 12345,
      "status": "shipped"
    }
  },
  "token_ids": [
    "1234",
    "5678"
  ]
}
```

You can create a data connector by providing the required parameters.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|string|true|none|The name of the data connector.|
|description|string|false|none|A description of what this data connector does.|
|internal_description|string|false|none|The internal description of the data connector. If omitted, it is an empty string.|
|http_method|string|false|none|The HTTP method used when calling the external API.|
|url|string|false|none|The URL of the external API endpoint. Supports template variables like `{{order_id}}`.|
|body|string|false|none|The request body template. Supports template variables.|
|direct_fin_usage|boolean|false|none|Whether the connector is used directly by Fin (true) or only in workflows (false). Defaults to false.|
|audiences|[string]|false|none|The user types this connector is available for.|
|headers|[object]|false|none|HTTP headers to include in the request. Don't put credentials such as API keys here: header values are recorded unmasked in the connector's execution logs, except `Authorization`, which is always masked. Attach an authentication token with `token_ids` instead; its value is masked in execution logs.<br>|
|data_inputs|[object]|false|none|Input parameters accepted by the connector.|
|customer_authentication|boolean|false|none|Whether the connector requires customer authentication before executing. Defaults to false.|
|bypass_authentication|boolean|false|none|Whether authentication is bypassed entirely (public endpoint). Defaults to false.|
|enforce_auth|boolean|false|none|Whether authentication is enforced. On workspaces where this is supported, it takes precedence over `customer_authentication` and `bypass_authentication` when sent together, and setting it to false disables OTP.|
|validate_missing_attributes|boolean|false|none|Whether to validate that all required data inputs have values before executing.|
|mock_response|object|false|none|A sample JSON response from the external API. Auto-generates `response_fields` and sets `configuration_response_type` to `mock_response_type`.|
|token_ids|[string]|false|none|IDs of authentication tokens to attach to this data connector.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|http_method|get|
|http_method|post|
|http_method|put|
|http_method|delete|
|http_method|patch|
|audiences|leads|
|audiences|users|
|audiences|visitors|

Update an existing data connector. All fields are optional — only provided fields will be updated. Set `state` to `live` or `draft` to change the connector's state.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|string|false|none|The name of the data connector.|
|description|string|false|none|A description of what this data connector does.|
|internal_description|string|false|none|The internal description of the data connector. If omitted, it keeps its current value, unless the connector has no internal description yet, in which case it is set to the connector's `description`.|
|state|string|false|none|The desired state of the connector.|
|http_method|string|false|none|The HTTP method used by the data connector.|
|url|string|false|none|The URL of the external API endpoint. Supports template variables like `{{order_id}}`.|
|body|string|false|none|The request body template. Supports template variables.|
|direct_fin_usage|boolean|false|none|Whether this connector is used directly by Fin.|
|audiences|[string]|false|none|The audience types this connector targets.|
|headers|[object]|false|none|HTTP headers to include in the request. Don't put credentials such as API keys here: header values are recorded unmasked in the connector's execution logs, except `Authorization`, which is always masked. Attach an authentication token with `token_ids` instead; its value is masked in execution logs.<br>|
|data_inputs|[object]|false|none|The input parameters accepted by this data connector. Replaces all existing inputs.|
|customer_authentication|boolean|false|none|Whether OTP authentication is enabled for this connector.|
|bypass_authentication|boolean|false|none|Whether authentication is bypassed for this connector.|
|enforce_auth|boolean|false|none|Whether authentication is enforced. On workspaces where this is supported, it takes precedence over `customer_authentication` and `bypass_authentication` when sent together, and setting it to false disables OTP.|
|validate_missing_attributes|boolean|false|none|Whether to validate missing attributes before execution.|
|mock_response|object|false|none|A sample JSON response from the external API. Auto-generates `response_fields` and sets `configuration_response_type` to `mock_response_type`.|
|token_ids|[string]|false|none|IDs of authentication tokens to attach to this data connector. An empty array removes all tokens.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|state|draft|
|state|live|
|http_method|get|
|http_method|post|
|http_method|put|
|http_method|delete|
|http_method|patch|
|audiences|leads|
|audiences|users|
|audiences|visitors|

```json
  "download_url": "https://api.intercom.io/download/content/data/orzzsbd7hk67xyu"
}
```

The data export API is used to export message delivery and engagement statistics for outbound content (Emails, Posts, Custom Bots, Surveys, Tours, Series, and more) sent in a given timeframe. The exported data includes who received each message, when they received it, and how they engaged with it (opens, clicks, replies, completions, dismissals, unsubscribes, and bounces).

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|job_identifier|string|false|none|The identifier for your job.|
|status|string|false|none|The current state of your job.|
|download_expires_at|string|false|none|The time after which you will not be able to access the data, as a Unix timestamp. It is one week from the time the job was created. Empty until the job completes.|
|download_url|string|false|none|The location where you can download your data. Empty until the job completes.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|status|pending|
|status|in_progress|
|status|failed|
|status|completed|
|status|no_data|
|status|canceled|

A CSV output file

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|user_id|string|false|none|The user_id of the user who was sent the message.|
|user_external_id|string|false|none|The external_user_id of the user who was sent the message|
|company_id|string|false|none|The company ID of the user in relation to the message that was sent. Will return -1 if no company is present.|
|email|string|false|none|The users email who was sent the message.|
|name|string|false|none|The full name of the user receiving the message|
|ruleset_id|string|false|none|The id of the message.|
|content_id|string|false|none|The specific content that was received. In an A/B test each version has its own Content ID.|
|content_type|string|false|none|Email, Chat, Post etc.|
|content_title|string|false|none|The title of the content you see in your Intercom workspace.|
|ruleset_version_id|string|false|none|As you edit content we record new versions. This ID can help you determine which version of a piece of content that was received.|
|receipt_id|string|false|none|ID for this receipt. Will be included with any related stats in other files to identify this specific delivery of a message.|
|received_at|integer|false|none|Timestamp for when the receipt was recorded.|
|series_id|string|false|none|The id of the series that this content is part of. Will return -1 if not part of a series.|
|series_title|string|false|none|The title of the series that this content is part of.|
|node_id|string|false|none|The id of the series node that this ruleset is associated with. Each block in a series has a corresponding node_id.|
|first_reply|integer|false|none|The first time a user replied to this message if the content was able to receive replies. Only events within the export job's requested date range are counted.|
|first_completion|integer|false|none|The first time a user completed this message if the content was able to be completed e.g. Tours, Surveys. Only events within the export job's requested date range are counted.|
|first_series_completion|integer|false|none|The first time the series this message was a part of was completed by the user. Only events within the export job's requested date range are counted.|
|first_series_disengagement|integer|false|none|The first time the series this message was a part of was disengaged by the user. Only events within the export job's requested date range are counted.|
|first_series_exit|integer|false|none|The first time the series this message was a part of was exited by the user. Only events within the export job's requested date range are counted.|
|first_goal_success|integer|false|none|The first time the user met this messages associated goal if one exists. Only events within the export job's requested date range are counted.|
|first_open|integer|false|none|The first time the user opened this message. Only events within the export job's requested date range are counted.|
|first_click|integer|false|none|The first time the series the user clicked on a link within this message. Only events within the export job's requested date range are counted.|
|first_dismisall|integer|false|none|The first time the series the user dismissed this message. Only events within the export job's requested date range are counted.|
|first_unsubscribe|integer|false|none|The first time the user unsubscribed from this message. Only events within the export job's requested date range are counted.|
|first_hard_bounce|integer|false|none|The first time this message hard bounced for this user. Only events within the export job's requested date range are counted.|

Contains the id of the call the summary describes, for conversation part type <code>call_summary</code>. A conversation can contain several calls, and therefore several call summaries, so this identifies which call each summary belongs to. The id matches the <code>id</code> returned by the Calls API and by the <code>call.started</code>, <code>call.ended</code>, <code>call.recording_available</code> and <code>call.transcription_available</code> webhook topics.

<h2 id="tocS_fin_agent_message">fin_agent_message</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemafin_agent_message"></a>
<a id="schema_fin_agent_message"></a>
<a id="tocSfin_agent_message"></a>
<a id="tocsfin_agent_message"></a>

```json
{
  "author": "user",
  "body": "How can I see my account details?",
  "timestamp": "2025-01-24T10:01:20.000Z",
  "timestamp_ms": "2025-01-24T10:01:20.456Z"
}
```

A message exchanged within a Fin Agent conversation.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|author|string|true|none|The author that created the message. In `conversation_metadata.history`, only `user` and `agent` are accepted.|
|body|string|true|none|The body of the message. Accepts both plain text and HTML format.<br>For the message you send to Fin, this is the user's message. For an `agent` item in `conversation_metadata.history`, it is the agent's message.<br>Fin's response is returned in the format set by `response_format` (HTML by default).<br>|
|timestamp|string(date-time)|false|none|The timestamp when the message was created.<br>Used to deduplicate messages sent within a 5 minute window.<br>Ideally should include milliseconds for higher precision.<br>Send `timestamp` or `timestamp_ms`; at least one is required. If you send both, `timestamp_ms` is used.<br>On the top-level `message`, sending neither fails with a 422 error (`message: timestamp_ms is required`). In `conversation_metadata.history`, an item with neither causes the whole history to be ignored.<br>|
|timestamp_ms|string(date-time)|false|none|The timestamp when the message was created, with millisecond precision.<br>Accepted in place of `timestamp` when you send a message, and also present in webhook event responses (fin_replied). At least one of `timestamp` or `timestamp_ms` is required.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|author|user|
|author|agent|
|author|fin|

<h2 id="tocS_fin_agent_status_updated_event">fin_agent_status_updated_event</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemafin_agent_status_updated_event"></a>
<a id="schema_fin_agent_status_updated_event"></a>
<a id="tocSfin_agent_status_updated_event"></a>
<a id="tocsfin_agent_status_updated_event"></a>

```json
{
  "event_name": "fin_status_updated",
  "conversation_id": "123456",
  "user_id": "7891",
  "status": "escalated",
  "reason": "Escalation requested via API",
  "created_at_ms": "2025-01-24T10:00:00.123Z"
}
```

Event fired when Fin's status changes during a conversation.
Delivered via webhooks. Fin will report its status to the client via this event.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|event_name|string|true|none|The name of the event.|
|conversation_id|string|true|none|The ID of the conversation.|
|user_id|string|true|none|The ID of the user.|
|status|string|true|none|Fin's current status.<br>- thinking: Fin has started running a procedure. Not sent on every turn<br>- awaiting_user_reply: Fin has finished replying and is waiting for the user to respond<br>- escalated: The conversation has been escalated to a human<br>- resolved: The user's query has been resolved<br>- complete: Fin has completed its workflow. When CSAT is enabled a csat_requested event may follow<br>|
|reason|string|false|none|Optional. A human-readable explanation of why the conversation was escalated.<br>Only present when status is 'escalated'.<br><br>When you escalate deterministically with `/fin/escalate`, the reason is always<br>"Escalation requested via API".<br><br>The following reasons apply to Fin-decided escalations when Fin owns the<br>conversation (`/fin/start`, `/fin/procedures/{procedure_id}/run`, and<br>`/fin/reply` on a conversation that was started that way). `/fin/ask` can<br>report any of them, because escalation rules still apply and the conversation<br>can still be routed to a team or finish without resolution. On an Ask,<br>"Escalation requested by user" normally only follows an escalation rule match.<br>- "Escalation requested by user"<br>- "Escalation rule: {rule_name}"<br>- "Escalation rule matched"<br>- "Routed to team"<br>- "Conversation finished without resolution"<br><br>"Escalation requested by user" is sent whenever Fin decides to hand over, not<br>only when the user asks for a human, for example on a procedure handoff or a<br>custom answer handover. It also follows an escalation rule match, as a second<br>`escalated` event after the rule's reason. While a procedure is running, every<br>escalation Fin decides on reports it.<br>|
|created_at_ms|string(date-time)|true|none|The timestamp the event was created at, with millisecond precision.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|event_name|fin_status_updated|
|status|thinking|
|status|awaiting_user_reply|
|status|escalated|
|status|resolved|
|status|complete|

<h2 id="tocS_fin_agent_replied_event">fin_agent_replied_event</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemafin_agent_replied_event"></a>
<a id="schema_fin_agent_replied_event"></a>

```json
{
  "event_name": "fin_replied",
  "conversation_id": "123456",
  "user_id": "7891",
  "message": {
    "id": "98765",
    "author": "fin",
    "body": "<p>You can see your account details by clicking on the <em>Account</em> tab in the top right corner of the screen.</p>",
    "format": "html",
    "timestamp_ms": "2025-01-24T09:01:00.456Z",
    "sources": [
      {
        "title": "Managing your account",
        "type": "article",
        "url": "https://www.example.com/help/en/articles/1-managing-your-account"
      }
    ]
  },

  "created_at_ms": "2025-01-24T10:00:00.123Z"
}
```

Event fired when Fin replies to a user.
Delivered via webhooks. The content of the response will be contained in the message object.
Intermediate replies have status 'replying'; a separate fin_status_updated event with 'awaiting_user_reply' fires once Fin's reply is done.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|event_name|string|true|none|The name of the event.|
|conversation_id|string|true|none|The ID of the conversation.|
|user_id|string|true|none|The ID of the user.|
|message|object|true|none|Fin's answer to the user's query.|
|status|string|true|none|Fin's current status.<br>- replying: Intermediate reply part; more parts may follow<br>- awaiting_user_reply: Legacy status; instead use the fin_status_updated event with 'awaiting_user_reply', which fires once Fin's reply is done<br>- complete: Fin's reply is final and no user reply is expected. Sent for one-shot Ask replies only<br>|
|created_at_ms|string(date-time)|true|none|The timestamp the event was created at, with millisecond precision.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|event_name|fin_replied|
|status|replying|
|status|awaiting_user_reply|
|status|complete|

|rule_id|string \| null|false|none|The escalation rule that triggered the consultation, as recorded when it began. Null if no rule triggered it.|
|rule_name|string \| null|false|none|The rule's name as recorded when the consultation began, which may differ from its current name.|
|created_at|integer|false|none|Unix timestamp for when the event occurred. Approximate on `fin_draft_proposed`.|
|data|object|false|none|Fields specific to this event. Which are present depends on `event_type` — see the endpoint description for the full mapping.<br>|

<h2 id="tocS_jobs">jobs</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemajobs"></a>
<a id="schema_jobs"></a>
<a id="tocSjobs"></a>
<a id="tocsjobs"></a>

```json
{
  "type": "job",
  "id": "20",
  "url": "https://api.intercom.io/jobs/status/20",
  "status": "pending",
  "resource_type": "ticket",
  "resource_id": "123",
  "resource_url": "https://api.intercom.io/tickets/123"
}
```

Jobs are tasks that are processed asynchronously by the Intercom system after being enqueued via the API. This allows for efficient handling of operations that may take time to complete, such as data imports or exports. You can check the status of your jobs to monitor their progress and ensure they are completed successfully.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|type|string|false|none|The type of the object|
|id|string|true|none|The id of the job that's currently being processed or has completed.|
|url|string|false|none|API endpoint URL to check the job status.|
|status|string|false|none|The status of the job execution.|
|resource_type|string|false|none|The type of resource created during job execution.|
|resource_id|string \| null|false|none|The id of the resource created during job execution (e.g. ticket id). Only set once the job has succeeded.|
|resource_url|string \| null|false|none|The url of the resource created during job execution. Use this url to fetch the resource. Only set once the job has succeeded.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|job|
|status|pending|
|status|success|
|status|failed|

Two counts per object type — `from`, how many are on the lead and would move to the surviving contact, and `into`, how many the surviving contact already has. Only types with reassignments are included, and both counts are always present on a type that is included.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|conversations|object|false|none|Distinct non-ticket conversations, counting both conversations the contact owns and conversations it participates in. Tickets are excluded here and reported separately under `tickets`.|
|tickets|object|false|none|Tickets, meaning conversations of any ticket type. Counted separately from `conversations` so a single conversation is never counted twice.|
|phone_calls|object|false|none|Phone calls. Present only for phone-lead merges.|
|tags|object|false|none|Tags. `from` counts only tags the surviving contact does not already have.|
|notes|object|false|none|Notes attached to the contact.|

A News Item is a content type in Intercom enabling you to announce product updates, company news, promotions, events and more with your customers.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|type|string|false|none|The type of object.|
|id|string|false|none|The unique identifier for the news item which is given by Intercom.|
|workspace_id|string|false|none|The id of the workspace which the news item belongs to.|
|title|string|false|none|The title of the news item.|
|body|string|false|none|The news item body, which may contain HTML.|
|sender_id|integer|false|none|The id of the sender of the news item. Must be a teammate on the workspace.|
|state|string|false|none|News items will not be visible to your users in the assigned newsfeeds until they are set live.|
|newsfeed_assignments|[[newsfeed_assignment](#schemanewsfeed_assignment)]|false|none|A list of newsfeed_assignments to assign to the specified newsfeed.|
|labels|[string]|false|none|Label names displayed to users to categorize the news item, sorted with uppercase letters before lowercase.|
|cover_image_url|string(uri) \| null|false|none|URL of the image used as cover. Must have .jpg or .png extension. Intercom copies the image you send on write, so the URL returned here is a signed Intercom URL that expires; fetch the news item again for a fresh one.|
|reactions|[string]|false|none|Ordered list of emoji reactions to the news item. When empty, reactions are disabled. An update that leaves out `reactions` also disables them but leaves this list as it was.|
|deliver_silently|boolean|false|none|When set to true, the news item will appear in the messenger newsfeed without showing a notification badge.|
|created_at|integer(timestamp)|false|none|Timestamp for when the news item was created.|
|updated_at|integer(timestamp)|false|none|Timestamp for when the news item was last updated.|
|published_at|integer(timestamp) \| null|false|none|Timestamp for when the news item last went live. Null if the news item has never been live.|

|type|news-item|
|state|draft|
|state|live|

```json
  ],

    {
      "newsfeed_id": 198313,
```

A News Item is a content type in Intercom enabling you to announce product updates, company news, promotions, events and more with your customers.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|title|string|true|none|The title of the news item.|
|body|string|false|none|The news item body, which may contain HTML.|
|sender_id|integer|true|none|The id of the sender of the news item. Must be a teammate on the workspace.|
|state|string|false|none|News items will not be visible to your users in the assigned newsfeeds until they are set live.|
|deliver_silently|boolean|false|none|When set to `true`, the news item will appear in the messenger newsfeed without showing a notification badge.|
|labels|[string]|false|none|Label names displayed to users to categorize the news item.|
|cover_image_url|string(uri)|false|none|URL of the image to use as the cover. Must contain `.png` or `.jpg` in lower case, so `.jpeg` and `.PNG` are rejected. Intercom copies the image and serves it from its own signed URL.|
|reactions|[string]|false|none|Ordered list of emoji reactions to the news item. Send an empty list to disable reactions. Send at most five, each a single Unicode code point, so an emoji with a skin tone, a joiner sequence or a variation selector (such as ❤️) is rejected. More than five returns a 400, but the news item is still saved as a draft, with no reactions or cover image.|
|newsfeed_assignments|[[newsfeed_assignment](#schemanewsfeed_assignment)]|false|none|A list of newsfeed_assignments to assign to the specified newsfeed.|

|deliver_silently|boolean|false|none|When set to `true`, the news item will appear in the messenger newsfeed without showing a notification badge.|
|labels|[string]|false|none|Label names displayed to users to categorize the news item. Send the full list; the labels you leave out are removed.|
|cover_image_url|string(uri)|false|none|URL of the image to use as the cover. Must contain `.png` or `.jpg` in lower case, so `.jpeg` and `.PNG` are rejected. Intercom copies the image and serves it from its own signed URL.|
|reactions|[string]|false|none|Ordered list of emoji reactions to the news item. Send an empty list to disable reactions. Send at most five, each a single Unicode code point, so an emoji with a skin tone, a joiner sequence or a variation selector (such as ❤️) is rejected.|
|newsfeed_assignments|[[newsfeed_assignment](#schemanewsfeed_assignment)]|false|none|A list of newsfeed_assignments to assign to the specified newsfeed. Send the full list; the assignments you leave out are removed.|

|state|live|

```json
  "next": "http://example.com",
  "prev": "http://example.com",
  "per_page": 50,
  "total_pages": 1
}
```

The majority of list resources in the API are paginated to allow clients to traverse data over multiple requests.

Their responses are likely to contain a pages object that hosts pagination links which a client can use to paginate through the data without having to construct a query. The link relations for the pages field are as follows.

|type|string|false|none|none|

|next|string(uri) \| null|false|none|A link to the next page of results. Omitted or `null` on the last page, depending on the list. Some lists never include `next` or `prev`, so compare `page` with `total_pages` to tell whether more pages remain.|
|prev|string(uri) \| null|false|none|A link to the previous page of results. Omitted on the first page.|
|per_page|integer|false|none|none|
|total_pages|integer|false|none|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|pages|

|operator|string|false|none|The accepted operators you can use to define how you want to search for the value. Operator support depends on the field's data type. The breakdown below is for Contacts search; the other search endpoints that share this schema accept a different set per field:<br>- `string` fields: `=`, `!=`, `IN`, `NIN`, `~`, `!~`, `^`, `$`<br>- `tag_id`: `=` and `!=` only. Every other operator returns an error.<br>- `boolean` fields: `=`, `!=`, `IN`, `NIN`<br>- `integer` fields: `=`, `!=`, `IN`, `NIN`, `<`, `>`, `<=`, `>=`<br>- `datetime` fields (standard contact timestamps such as `created_at` and `last_seen_at`): `=`, `!=`, `<`, `>`, `<=`, `>=`. Filtering is on the exact second, in UTC.<br>- `date` fields (Date custom attributes): `=`, `<`, `>` only. `!=`, `<=`, and `>=` are not supported and return an error. Values are truncated to a whole UTC day.|
|value|string \| integer \| boolean \| [string \| integer] \| null|false|none|The value that you want to search on.|

<h2 id="tocS_sla_applied">sla_applied</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemasla_applied"></a>
<a id="schema_sla_applied"></a>
<a id="tocSsla_applied"></a>
<a id="tocssla_applied"></a>

```json
{
  "type": "conversation_sla_summary",
  "sla_name": "",
  "sla_status": "hit"
}
```

The SLA Applied object contains the details for which SLA has been applied to this conversation.
Important: if there are any canceled sla_events for the conversation - meaning an SLA has been manually removed from a conversation, the sla_status will always be returned as null.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|type|string|false|none|object type|
|sla_name|string|false|none|The name of the SLA as given by the teammate when it was created.|
|sla_status|string|false|none|SLA statuses:<br>            - `hit`: If there’s at least one hit event in the underlying sla_events table, and no “missed” or “canceled” events for the conversation.<br>            - `missed`: If there are any missed sla_events for the conversation and no canceled events. If there’s even a single missed sla event, the status will always be missed. A missed status is not applied when the SLA expires, only the next time a teammate replies.<br>            - `active`: An SLA has been applied to a conversation, but has not yet been fulfilled. SLA status is active only if there are no “hit, “missed”, or “canceled” events.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|sla_status|hit|
|sla_status|missed|
|sla_status|canceled|
|sla_status|active|

Tickets are how you track requests from your users.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|type|string|false|none|Always ticket|
|id|string|false|none|The unique identifier for the ticket which is given by Intercom.|
|ticket_id|string|false|none|The ID of the Ticket used in the Intercom Inbox and Messenger. Do not use ticket_id for API queries.|
|category|string|false|none|Category of the Ticket.|
|channel|string \| null|false|none|The channel the ticket was created through. Defaults to messenger when no channel is specified at creation.|
|ticket_attributes|[ticket_custom_attributes](#schematicket_custom_attributes)|false|none|An object containing the different attributes associated to the ticket as key-value pairs. For the default title and description attributes, the keys are `_default_title_` and `_default_description_`.|
|ticket_state|[ticket_state](#schematicket_state)|false|none|A ticket state, used to define the state of a ticket.|
|ticket_type|[ticket_type](#schematicket_type)|false|none|A ticket type, used to define the data fields to be captured in a ticket.|
|contacts|[ticket_contacts](#schematicket_contacts)|false|none|The list of contacts affected by a ticket.|
|admin_assignee_id|integer|false|none|The id representing the admin assigned to the ticket. If it's not assigned to an admin it will return 0.|
|team_assignee_id|integer|false|none|The id representing the team assigned to the ticket. If it's not assigned to a team it will return 0.|
|created_at|integer(date-time)|false|none|The time the ticket was created as a UTC Unix timestamp.|
|updated_at|integer(date-time)|false|none|The last time the ticket was updated as a UTC Unix timestamp.|
|open|boolean|false|none|Whether or not the ticket is open. If false, the ticket is closed.|
|snoozed_until|integer(date-time)|false|none|The time the ticket will be snoozed until as a UTC Unix timestamp. If null, the ticket is not currently snoozed.|
|linked_objects|[linked_object_list](#schemalinked_object_list)|false|none|An object containing metadata about linked conversations and linked tickets. Up to 1000 can be returned.|
|ticket_parts|[ticket_parts](#schematicket_parts)|false|none|A list of Ticket Part objects for each note and event in the ticket. There is a limit of 500 parts.|
|is_shared|boolean|false|none|Whether or not the ticket is shared with the customer.|
|company_id|string \| null|false|none|The ID of the company the ticket is associated with. Omitted when the ticket has no company.|
|previous_ticket_state_id|string \| null|false|none|The ID of the previous ticket state from the most recent state change. Returns null if no state change history exists. Useful for tracking state transitions for reporting and compliance.|

|category|Customer|
|category|Back-office|
|category|Tracker|

A Ticket Part represents a message in the ticket.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|type|string|false|none|Always ticket_part|
|id|string|false|none|The id representing the ticket part.|
|part_type|string|false|none|The type of ticket part.|
|body|string \| null|false|none|The message body, which may contain HTML.|
|previous_ticket_state|string|false|none|The previous state of the ticket.|
|ticket_state|string|false|none|The state of the ticket.|
|created_at|integer(date-time)|false|none|The time the ticket part was created.|
|updated_at|integer(date-time)|false|none|The last time the ticket part was updated.|
|assigned_to|[reference](#schemareference)|false|none|The assignee this ticket_part assigned the ticket to, as a reference whose `type` is `admin`, `team` or `bot`. When the part unassigned the ticket, `type` is `nobody_admin` and `id` is `null`. Null when the part did not change the assignment, or when the assignee has since been deleted.|
|admin_assignee_id|integer \| null|false|none|The id of the teammate that this ticket_part assigned the ticket to, or 0 if the part removed the teammate. Null or absent when the part did not change the teammate, including an unassignment that did not name which assignee it cleared. A bot is reported here, because assignment treats anything that is not a team as a teammate.|
|team_assignee_id|integer \| null|false|none|The id of the team that this ticket_part assigned the ticket to, or 0 if the part removed the team. Null or absent when the part did not change the team, including an unassignment that did not name which assignee it cleared. A part can assign a team and a teammate at the same time, for example when the team uses Round Robin distribution and the teammate is resolved inline. In that case assigned_to reports only the teammate, and these two fields report each assignee separately.|
|author|[ticket_part_author](#schematicket_part_author)|false|none|The author that wrote or triggered the part. Can be a bot, admin, team or user.|
|attachments|[[part_attachment](#schemapart_attachment)]|false|none|A list of attachments for the part.|
|external_id|string \| null|false|none|The external id of the ticket part|
|redacted|boolean|false|none|Whether or not the ticket part has been redacted.|
|app_package_code|string|false|none|The app package code if this part was created via API. Note this field won't show if the part was not created via API.|
|translations|object \| null|false|none|A map of the reply text keyed by locale code. Backs the `ticket.admin.replied.translated` webhook topic. `original` holds the locale code the reply was written in; every other key holds the reply translated into that locale.|
|updated_attribute_data|object \| null|false|none|The updated attribute data of the ticket part. Only present for attribute update parts.|

|previous_ticket_state|in_progress|
|previous_ticket_state|waiting_on_customer|
|previous_ticket_state|resolved|
|ticket_state|submitted|
|ticket_state|in_progress|
|ticket_state|waiting_on_customer|
|ticket_state|resolved|

A Ticket Part representing a note, comment, or quick_reply on a ticket

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|type|string|false|none|Always ticket_part|
|id|string|false|none|The id representing the part.|
|part_type|string|false|none|Type of the part|
|body|string \| null|false|none|The message body, which may contain HTML.|
|created_at|integer(date-time)|false|none|The time the note was created.|
|updated_at|integer(date-time)|false|none|The last time the note was updated.|
|author|[ticket_part_author](#schematicket_part_author)|false|none|The author that wrote or triggered the part. Can be a bot, admin, team or user.|
|attachments|[[part_attachment](#schemapart_attachment)]|false|none|A list of attachments for the part.|
|redacted|boolean|false|none|Whether or not the ticket part has been redacted.|
|app_package_code|string|false|none|The app package code if this part was created via API. Note this field won't show if the part was not created via API.|
|translations|object \| null|false|none|A map of the reply text keyed by locale code. Backs the `ticket.admin.replied.translated` webhook topic. `original` holds the locale code the reply was written in; every other key holds the reply translated into that locale.|

<h2 id="tocS_ticket_request_custom_attributes">ticket_request_custom_attributes</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schematicket_request_custom_attributes"></a>
<a id="schema_ticket_request_custom_attributes"></a>
<a id="tocSticket_request_custom_attributes"></a>
<a id="tocsticket_request_custom_attributes"></a>

```json
{
  "_default_title_": "Found a bug",
  "_default_description_": "The button is not working"
}
```

The attributes set on the ticket. When setting the default title and description attributes, the attribute keys that should be used are `_default_title_` and `_default_description_`. When setting ticket type attributes of the list attribute type, the key should be the attribute name and the value of the attribute should be the list item id, obtainable by [listing the ticket type](ref:get_ticket-types). For example, if the ticket type has an attribute called `priority` of type `list`, the key should be `priority` and the value of the attribute should be the guid of the list item (e.g. `de1825a0-0164-4070-8ca6-13e22462fa7e`).

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|**additionalProperties**|string \| null \| number \| boolean \| array|false|none|none|

Optional body for publishing a staged article draft. On a single-language
workspace the body can be omitted. On a multilingual workspace, `locales`
is required and lists which locales' drafts to publish.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|locales|[string]|false|none|The locales whose staged drafts should be published. Required on<br>multilingual workspaces; each locale must have a pending draft.<br>|
|author_id|integer|false|none|The id of the teammate to publish as. This is only used when the access token is not associated with a teammate, and is then required; omitting it returns 400 `parameter_not_found`. Otherwise the authenticating teammate is used. Must be a teammate on the workspace.|

You can Update an Article

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|title|string|false|none|The title of the article. For multilingual articles, this will be the title of the default language's content.|
|description|string|false|none|The description of the article. For multilingual articles, this will be the description of the default language's content.|
|body|string|false|none|The content of the article in HTML. For multilingual articles, this will be the body of the default language's content. Mutually exclusive with `body_markdown`.|
|body_markdown|string|false|none|The content of the article in markdown. For multilingual articles, this will be the body of the default language's content. An alternative to `body` — you can provide content as markdown instead of HTML. Mutually exclusive with `body`.|
|author_id|integer|false|none|The id of the author of the article. For multilingual articles, this will be the id of the author of the default language's content. Must be a teammate on the help center's workspace.|
|state|string|false|none|Whether the article will be `published` or will be a `draft`. Omitting this field leaves the publish state unchanged, so a draft stays a draft and an edit to a published article goes live immediately unless that article already has a pending draft or a scheduled publish time is set in the same request. For multilingual articles, this will be the state of the default language's content.|
|parent_id|string \| null|false|none|The id of the collection or section to move the article into. Omitting this field or sending `null` leaves the article's parent unchanged. Send `home` to remove the article from its collection so that it stands alone.|
|parent_ids|[integer]|false|none|The ids of the parent collections to place this article in. Send an empty array to remove the article from all collections. When provided, this takes precedence over `parent_id`.|
|translated_content|[article_translated_content](#schemaarticle_translated_content)|false|none|The Translated Content of an Article. The keys are the locale codes and the values are the translated content of the article.|
|folder_id|integer \| null|false|none|The ID of the folder to place this article in, or null to remove it from its folder.|
|audience_ids|[integer]|false|none|The list of audience IDs to assign to this article for Fin AI Agent targeting. Sending a top-level `audience_ids` broadcasts the same set to every locale. Sending `audience_ids: []` clears all audience memberships from every locale. For per-locale targeting, use `translated_content.<locale>.audience_ids` instead. Sending both top-level and per-locale in the same request causes top-level to win. Unknown audience IDs return a 404 error. No partial commit occurs.|
|ai_chatbot_availability|boolean|false|none|Whether the article should be available for AI Chatbot (Fin). For multilingual articles, this sets the default language's availability.|
|ai_copilot_availability|boolean|false|none|Whether the article should be available for AI Copilot. For multilingual articles, this sets the default language's availability.|
|ai_sales_agent_availability|boolean|false|none|Whether the article should be available for AI Sales Agent. For multilingual articles, this sets the default language's availability.|
|scheduled_publish_at|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|ISO 8601 timestamp at which to schedule a future publish of the article. When set together with `state: "published"`, the article is scheduled instead of published immediately. Setting `null` cancels a pending publish schedule. Timestamps in the past or equal to the current time are rejected with 400 `parameter_invalid` — the value must be strictly in the future. Combining with `state: "draft"` returns 400 `parameter_invalid`. Sending in the same request as `scheduled_unpublish_at` returns 400 — only one pending schedule per article. Empty string returns 400 `parameter_invalid`.|
|scheduled_unpublish_at|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|ISO 8601 timestamp at which to schedule a future unpublish of the article. The article must already be published; setting `state: "published"` in the same request does not count, and the request returns 400 `parameter_invalid`. Combining with `state: "draft"` also returns 400 `parameter_invalid`. The value must be strictly in the future; timestamps in the past or equal to the current time are rejected with 400 `parameter_invalid`. Setting `null` cancels a pending unpublish schedule. Sending in the same request as `scheduled_publish_at` returns 400 — only one pending schedule per article. Empty string returns 400 `parameter_invalid`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|state|published|
|state|draft|

You can Update an Internal Article

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|title|string|false|none|The title of the article.|
|body|string|false|none|The content of the article in HTML. Mutually exclusive with `body_markdown`.|
|body_markdown|string|false|none|The content of the article in markdown. An alternative to `body` — you can provide content as markdown instead of HTML. Mutually exclusive with `body` and `json_blocks`.|
|json_blocks|[object]|false|none|The content of the article as a list of content blocks. Used only when `body` is not provided. Cannot be combined with `body_markdown`. If none of `body`, `body_markdown` and `json_blocks` is provided, the existing content is kept.|
|locale|string|false|none|The locale of the article. If omitted, the existing locale is kept.|
|author_id|integer|false|none|The id of the author of the article.|
|owner_id|integer|false|none|The id of the author of the article.|
|folder_id|integer \| null|false|none|The ID of the folder to place this article in. Pass `null` to remove it from its folder. If omitted, the folder is unchanged.|
|audience_ids|[integer]|false|none|The list of audience IDs to target this internal article to for Fin AI Agent. Omitting the field leaves existing audience memberships unchanged (PATCH semantics). Pass `[]` to clear all audience memberships. Unknown audience IDs return a `404` error with no partial commit.|
|ai_chatbot_availability|boolean|false|none|Whether the internal article should be available for AI Chatbot (Fin).|
|ai_copilot_availability|boolean|false|none|Whether the internal article should be available for AI Copilot.|
|ai_sales_agent_availability|boolean|false|none|Whether the internal article should be available for AI Sales Agent.|

You can update a contact

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|role|string|false|none|The role of the contact, either `user` or `lead`. Any other value is ignored. A user can't be changed to a lead; sending `lead` for a user returns a `400` error.|
|external_id|string|false|none|A unique identifier for the contact which is given to Intercom|
|email|string|false|none|The contacts email|
|email_verified|boolean \| null|false|none|Whether the contact has proved they own this email address, for example through a confirmation link or one-time code you sent. Send it together with `email`. `email_verified` without `email` is rejected.<br><br>Changing a contact's email resets it to not verified. Intercom reuses leads with a verified email when an inbound email, conversation or ticket matches the address.|
|phone|string \| null|false|none|The contacts phone|
|name|string \| null|false|none|The contacts name|
|avatar|string \| null|false|none|An image URL containing the avatar of a contact|
|signed_up_at|integer(date-time) \| null|false|none|(Unix timestamp in seconds) The time specified for when a contact signed up.|
|last_seen_at|integer(date-time) \| null|false|none|(Unix timestamp in seconds) The time when the contact was last seen (either where the Intercom Messenger was installed or when specified manually).|
|owner_id|string \| null|false|none|The id of an admin that has been assigned account ownership of the contact|
|unsubscribed_from_emails|boolean \| null|false|none|Whether the contact is unsubscribed from emails|
|sms_consent|boolean|false|none|Whether the contact has consented to receive SMS messages.|
|unsubscribed_from_sms|boolean|false|none|Whether the contact is unsubscribed from SMS messages.|
|language_override|string \| null|false|none|A preferred language setting for the contact, used by the Intercom Messenger even if their browser settings change.|
|custom_attributes|object \| null|false|none|The custom attributes which are set for the contact|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|sync_behavior|string|true|none|If you intend to create or update External Pages via the API, this should be set to `api`. You can not change the value to or from api.|
|status|string|false|none|The status of the content import source.|
|url|string|true|none|The URL of the content import source. It must be an http or https URL whose host is a valid public domain name. This may only be different from the existing value if the sync behavior is API.|
|audience_ids|integer \| [integer] \| null|false|none|The unique identifiers for the audiences to associate with this content import source. Can be a single integer or an array of integers. Set to null or an empty array to remove all audiences.|
|apply_audience_to_existing_content|boolean|false|none|When true, the audience will be applied to all existing external pages belonging to this content import source.|

|sync_behavior|automatic|
|sync_behavior|manual|
|status|active|
|status|deactivated|

|title|string|true|none|The title of the external page.|
|html|string|true|none|The body of the external page in HTML.|
|url|string|false|none|The URL of the external page. This will be used by Fin to link end users to the page it based its answer on. If omitted, the page's existing URL is removed.|
|ai_agent_availability|boolean|false|none|Whether the external page should be used to answer questions by AI Agent.|
|ai_copilot_availability|boolean|false|none|Whether the external page should be used to answer questions by AI Copilot.|
|ai_sales_agent_availability|boolean|false|none|Whether the external page should be used to answer questions by AI Sales Agent.|
|locale|string|true|none|The language code of the external page, for example `en` or `fr`. It must be a language supported by the workspace.|
|source_id|integer|true|none|The unique identifier for the source of the external page which was given by Intercom. Every external page must be associated with a Content Import Source which represents the place it comes from and from which it inherits a default audience (configured in the UI). For a new source, make a POST request to the Content Import Source endpoint and an ID for the source will be returned in the response.|
|external_id|string|true|none|The identifier for the external page which was given by the source. Must be unique for the source.|
|audience_ids|[integer]|false|none|The list of audience IDs to target this external page to for Fin AI Agent. Replaces all existing audience memberships. Omitting the field leaves existing audience memberships unchanged. Pass `[]` to clear all audience memberships. Unknown audience IDs return a `404` error.|

<h2 id="tocS_update_ticket_request">update_ticket_request</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaupdate_ticket_request"></a>
<a id="schema_update_ticket_request"></a>
<a id="tocSupdate_ticket_request"></a>
<a id="tocsupdate_ticket_request"></a>

```json
{
  "ticket_attributes": {
    "_default_title_": "example",
    "_default_description_": "having a problem"
  },
  "ticket_state_id": "123",
  "company_id": "5f4d3c1c-7b1b-4d7d-a97e-6095715c6632",
  "open": true,
  "is_shared": true,
  "snoozed_until": 1673609604,
  "admin_id": 123,
  "assignee_id": "123"
}
```

You can update a Ticket

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ticket_attributes|object|false|none|The attributes set on the ticket.|
|ticket_state_id|string|false|none|The ID of the ticket state associated with the ticket type.|
|company_id|string|false|none|The ID of the company that the ticket is associated with. The unique identifier for the company which is given by Intercom. Set to nil to remove company.|
|open|boolean|false|none|Specify if a ticket is open. Set to false to close a ticket. Closing a ticket will also unsnooze it.|
|is_shared|boolean|false|none|Set to `true` to share a ticket with the customer. Only a ticket that isn't shared yet can be shared: a Back-office ticket, of a ticket type that isn't internal, that is linked to a conversation with no other shared linked ticket. Sending `false`, or `true` for a ticket that is already shared (Customer tickets are shared by default) or can't be shared (Tracker tickets), returns a `400`.|
|snoozed_until|integer(timestamp)|false|none|The time you want the ticket to reopen.|
|admin_id|integer|false|none|The ID of the admin performing ticket update. Needed for workflows execution and attributing actions to specific admins.|
|assignee_id|string|false|none|The ID of the admin or team to which the ticket is assigned. Set this 0 to unassign it.|

<h2 id="tocS_update_ticket_type_attribute_request">update_ticket_type_attribute_request</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaupdate_ticket_type_attribute_request"></a>
<a id="schema_update_ticket_type_attribute_request"></a>
<a id="tocSupdate_ticket_type_attribute_request"></a>
<a id="tocsupdate_ticket_type_attribute_request"></a>

```json
{
  "name": "Bug Priority",
  "description": "Priority level of the bug",
  "required_to_create": false,
  "required_to_create_for_contacts": false,
  "visible_on_create": true,
  "visible_to_contacts": true,
  "multiline": false,
  "list_items": "Low Priority,Medium Priority,High Priority",
  "allow_multiple_values": false,
  "archived": false
}
```

You can update a Ticket Type Attribute

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|string|false|none|The name of the ticket type attribute|
|description|string|false|none|The description of the attribute presented to the teammate or contact|
|required_to_create|boolean|false|none|Whether the attribute is required to be filled in when teammates are creating the ticket in Inbox.|
|required_to_create_for_contacts|boolean|false|none|Whether the attribute is required to be filled in when contacts are creating the ticket in Messenger.|
|visible_on_create|boolean|false|none|Whether the attribute is visible to teammates when creating a ticket in Inbox.|
|visible_to_contacts|boolean|false|none|Whether the attribute is visible to contacts when creating a ticket in Messenger.|
|multiline|boolean|false|none|Whether the attribute allows multiple lines of text (only applicable to string attributes)|
|list_items|string|false|none|A comma delimited list of items for the attribute value (only applicable to list attributes)|
|allow_multiple_values|boolean|false|none|Whether the attribute allows multiple files to be attached to it (only applicable to file attributes)|
|archived|boolean|false|none|Whether the attribute should be archived and not shown during creation of the ticket (it will still be present on previously created tickets)|

|*anyOf*|object|false|none|none|
|*anyOf*|object|false|none|none|

### Properties

|anonymous|boolean|false|none|Identifies if this visitor is anonymous.|
|email|string(email)|false|none|The email of the visitor.|
|phone|string \| null|false|none|The phone number of the visitor.|
|name|string \| null|false|none|The name of the visitor.|
|pseudonym|string \| null|false|none|The pseudonym of the visitor.|
|avatar|object|false|none|none|
|app_id|string|false|none|The id of the app the visitor is associated with.|
|companies|object|false|none|none|
|location_data|object|false|none|none|

|created_at|integer|false|none|The time the Visitor was added to Intercom.|
|remote_created_at|integer|false|none|The time the Visitor was added to Intercom.|
|signed_up_at|integer|false|none|The time the Visitor signed up for your product.|
|updated_at|integer|false|none|The last time the Visitor was updated.|
|session_count|integer|false|none|The number of sessions the Visitor has had.|
|social_profiles|object|false|none|none|
|owner_id|string \| null|false|none|The id of the admin that owns the Visitor.|
|unsubscribed_from_emails|boolean|false|none|Whether the Visitor is unsubscribed from emails.|
|marked_email_as_spam|boolean|false|none|Identifies if this visitor has marked an email as spam.|
|has_hard_bounced|boolean|false|none|Identifies if this visitor has had a hard bounce.|
|tags|object|false|none|none|
|segments|object|false|none|none|
|custom_attributes|object|false|none|The custom attributes you have set on the Visitor.|
|referrer|string \| null|false|none|The referer of the visitor.|
|utm_campaign|string \| null|false|none|The utm_campaign of the visitor.|
|utm_content|string \| null|false|none|The utm_content of the visitor.|
|utm_medium|string \| null|false|none|The utm_medium of the visitor.|
|utm_source|string \| null|false|none|The utm_source of the visitor.|
|utm_term|string \| null|false|none|The utm_term of the visitor.|
|do_not_track|boolean \| null|false|none|Identifies if this visitor has do not track enabled.|
